Tiêu biểu, Umar và cộng sự (2015) đã đề xuất phương pháp lai hóa (hybrid) trên nền tảng giải thuật di truyền đa mục tiêu để tích hợp lập lịch động và định tuyến cho cả công việc và AGV, qua đó nâng cao hiệu quả vận hành của FMS về nhiều tiêu chí như thời gian hoàn thành, cân bằng tải và độ ổn định hệ thống. Tuy nhiên, đa số các nghiên cứu trước vẫn chỉ tập trung vào một số mục tiêu tối ưu hóa nhất định, đồng thời chưa xem xét đầy đủ tác động của các điều kiện sản xuất thực tế như sự thay đổi nhu cầu đột xuất hay sự cố phát sinh trong quá trình vận hành. Nghiên cứu hiện tại bổ sung cho khoảng trống này bằng việc mở rộng mô hình tối ưu hóa đa mục tiêu, đồng thời tích hợp các yếu tố động thực tế và cơ chế phản hồi thời gian thực, góp phần nâng cao khả năng ứng dụng của các giải pháp lập lịch và điều phối AGV trong môi trường sản xuất hiện đại.

Recent advances in deep generative models have enabled the synthesis of convincing high-dimensional observations, including images, audio, and video, directly from raw data. In this work, we address the problem of generating goal-directed visual plans—plausible sequences of observations that transition a dynamical system from its current configuration to a desired goal state, which can subsequently serve as reference trajectories for control. We focus on systems characterized by high-dimensional observations, such as images, and propose a framework that seamlessly integrates representation learning with planning. Our approach learns a generative model of sequential observations, where the generative process is driven by transitions within a low-dimensional planning model augmented by noise. By maximizing the mutual information between generated observations and transitions in the planning model, we derive a low-dimensional representation that effectively captures the causal structure of the data. The planning model is designed to be compatible with efficient planning algorithms, and we introduce several such models based on discrete or continuous state spaces. To generate a visual plan, we project the current and goal observations onto their corresponding states in the planning model, compute a trajectory, and employ the generative model to transform this trajectory into a sequence of observations. We validate our method by generating plausible visual plans for rope manipulation tasks.

Bài báo nghiên cứu tác động của mô hình Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) đối với giá đất và các dự án xung quanh các trạm Metro số 1 tại TP.HCM, sử dụng phương pháp phân tích ảnh hưởng của quy hoạch đô thị theo hướng giao thông công cộng. Kết quả cho thấy mô hình TOD đã làm tăng giá đất lên 12% so với khu vực chung quanh các trạm Metro, đồng thời thúc đẩy sự phát triển mạnh mẽ của các dự án nhà cao tầng tại khu vực phía Đông thành phố. Ngoài việc cải thiện hạ tầng giao thông và tiện ích xã hội, TOD còn có ảnh hưởng sâu rộng đến thị trường bất động sản và tạo ra cơ hội đầu tư lớn tại các khu vực lân cận. Những phát hiện này góp phần làm rõ vai trò của TOD trong phát triển đô thị bền vững, mở ra hướng nghiên cứu và ứng dụng mô hình này trong quy hoạch đô thị tương lai tại các thành phố lớn khác.

TopCV và Vietnamworks hiện là hai trong số những trang web tuyển dụng hàng đầu tại Việt Nam, mỗi nền tảng sở hữu những ưu điểm và hạn chế riêng biệt. TopCV chú trọng ứng dụng công nghệ làm nền tảng phát triển cốt lõi với các tính năng nổi bật như thu thập và xử lý dữ liệu người dùng được lưu trong CV. Hệ thống của TopCV tự động bóc tách, phân loại thông tin, từ đó phân tích mô tả công việc, yêu cầu tuyển dụng và đưa ra các gợi ý phù hợp giữa nhà tuyển dụng và ứng viên trong thời gian thực. Bên cạnh đó, giao diện của TopCV được thiết kế hiện đại, trực quan, mang lại trải nghiệm thân thiện cho người dùng. Tuy nhiên, một điểm hạn chế là TopCV hiện chưa tích hợp tính năng đánh giá chất lượng công việc, mà chỉ cung cấp chức năng báo cáo đối với các công việc có dấu hiệu lừa đảo. Ngược lại, Vietnamworks sở hữu giao diện trực quan, dễ sử dụng, thông tin công việc được trình bày rõ ràng và có thêm tính năng hỗ trợ tuyển dụng nhân sự cấp cao. Dù vậy, nền tảng này cũng chưa phát triển chức năng đánh giá chất lượng công việc hoặc báo cáo các tin tuyển dụng có dấu hiệu lừa đảo. Những quan sát này cho thấy, mặc dù đã đạt được nhiều thành tựu nổi bật về công nghệ và trải nghiệm người dùng, cả TopCV và Vietnamworks vẫn còn thiếu các tính năng bảo đảm an toàn và minh bạch thông tin, từ đó đặt ra nhu cầu nghiên cứu và phát triển các giải pháp hỗ trợ đánh giá, cũng như kiểm soát chất lượng tin tuyển dụng trên các nền tảng này.

The paragraph discusses the characteristics and applications of read-only RFID tags, emphasizing their ability to store data that can be read by RFID readers while preventing any modification of the stored information. These tags are frequently utilized in scenarios such as barcode reading, freight tracking, and access control systems. Read-Only RFID tags are designed to store fixed data that can be retrieved by RFID readers but do not allow data to be rewritten or altered once programmed. This inherent feature makes them particularly suitable for applications requiring immutable identification, including barcode reading, freight tracking, and access control, where data integrity and security are paramount. Their widespread use in these domains highlights their importance in automated inventory management systems within logistics warehouses, contributing to efficient and reliable inventory rotation processes.

Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables non-contact measurement of heart activity and holds significant promise for applications such as remote healthcare monitoring. However, current end-to-end rPPG and heart rate (HR) estimation methods that utilize facial videos often struggle in unconstrained environments, particularly when challenged by head movements or poor lighting conditions. To address these limitations, a robust end-to-end baseline for remote HR measurement, termed AutoHR, has been developed using neural architecture search (NAS). AutoHR incorporates a specially designed backbone featuring Temporal Difference Convolution (TDC) to effectively capture rPPG-relevant temporal features across video frames. Additionally, a hybrid loss function is introduced, integrating constraints from both time and frequency domains to enhance model accuracy and generalizability. Spatio-temporal data augmentation strategies are also employed to facilitate improved representation learning. Extensive experiments conducted on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that AutoHR achieves superior performance in both intra-dataset and cross-dataset evaluations, indicating its robustness and potential for real-world deployment in diverse and challenging settings.

This study introduces an approach for visual text recognition that does not rely on paired supervisory data. The text recognition problem is reframed as aligning the conditional distribution of strings predicted from input text images with lexically valid strings drawn from target corpora. This approach allows for fully automated and unsupervised learning using only line-level text images and unpaired text-string samples, eliminating the necessity for extensive aligned datasets. We provide a comprehensive analysis of several aspects of our method, including: (1) the effect of training sequence length on convergence, (2) the relationship between character frequencies and the sequence in which they are learned, (3) the generalization capacity of our recognition network to handle inputs of varying lengths, and (4) the influence of altering the text corpus on recognition accuracy. Ultimately, our method achieves high text recognition accuracy on both synthetically produced text images and scanned images of actual printed books, all without the use of labeled training examples.

The main idea of the paragraph is to explain the role of the confusion matrix in evaluating classification models, specifically in the context of violence detection in surveillance videos. It defines the terms true positive (TP), false positive (FP), true negative (TN), and false negative (FN), and correlates each with the correct or incorrect identification of violent and non-violent videos.

The confusion matrix is a fundamental tool for assessing the performance of classification models, as it systematically presents the relationship between the predicted and actual labels in tasks such as violence detection in surveillance footage. Within this framework, true positives (TP) denote instances where the model correctly identifies violent videos as violence, while false positives (FP) represent cases where non-violent videos are incorrectly predicted as violence. Conversely, true negatives (TN) refer to the accurate prediction of non-violent videos as non-violence, and false negatives (FN) indicate misclassifications where violent videos are incorrectly labeled as non-violence. This detailed accounting allows for a comprehensive analysis of model accuracy and error types, thereby guiding further refinement of violence detection systems.

The objective of this project is to deploy a helpdesk website for ANSV’s recent IT support clients to efficiently manage customer support systems, emphasizing SLA policy management. The frontend design prioritizes functionality, enabling clients to submit requests aligned with technical product and project requirements, while the backend focuses on providing an advanced user interface. Deployment steps include configuring Odoo15 with parameters such as admin_passwd, db_host, and addons_path in /etc/odoo.conf, setting appropriate ownership and permissions, creating and enabling the systemd unit file /etc/systemd/system/odoo15.service to manage the Odoo15 service, verifying its status and logs, and configuring swap space by allocating 512M, adjusting swappiness and vfs_cache_pressure settings to enhance system performance.

Text-Image Modality Adversarial Matching (TIMAM) addresses the critical challenge of learning discriminative feature representations for computer vision tasks requiring joint understanding of images and text, such as image captioning, visual question answering, and person search. This challenge is compounded by the high variability in textual data and the inherent difficulty in aligning the feature spaces of visual and linguistic modalities. While previous research has primarily focused on improving feature alignment through novel loss functions, these methods often neglect the semantic complexity and diversity present in textual inputs. TIMAM introduces a novel approach by employing adversarial training and cross-modal matching objectives to encourage the learning of modality-invariant representations. Furthermore, the integration of BERT, a robust language model for extracting word embeddings, enhances the system’s capacity to model textual variability and improves the overall matching process. Experimental evaluations on four widely-used benchmark datasets demonstrate that TIMAM achieves state-of-the-art results, yielding absolute improvements of 2% to 5% in rank-1 accuracy for cross-modal retrieval tasks. These findings underscore the effectiveness of combining adversarial training with advanced language representations to bridge the semantic gap between images and text.

Monocular depth estimation and semantic segmentation are crucial for scene understanding, yet existing joint learning methods often underutilize semantic labels by neglecting their contextual structures, limiting task performance. Motivated by this limitation, this paper introduces CI-Net, a network injected with contextual information, which employs a self-attention block in the encoder to generate an attention map supervised by an ideal attention map derived from semantic labels. This approach embeds contextual information into the network, enhancing its scene comprehension and ability to leverage correlated features for more accurate predictions. Additionally, a feature sharing module is designed to deeply fuse task-specific features, and a consistency loss is implemented to promote mutual guidance between features. Evaluations on NYU-Depth-v2 and SUN-RGBD datasets demonstrate that CI-Net significantly improves the accuracy of both semantic segmentation and depth estimation. These results suggest that embedding contextual information and fostering deeper task interaction can advance multi-task scene understanding, pointing to promising directions for future research in joint learning frameworks.

The paragraph discusses the use of the Exact Match Ratio (EMR) as a performance metric for multi-label classification tasks, defined by the formula EMR = (1/n) ∑_{i=1}^n I(y_i = ȳ_i), where I is the indicator function. It highlights a limitation of this metric, namely that it treats partially correct predictions the same as completely incorrect ones, which may be considered overly stringent. This critique is essential for understanding the effectiveness and potential drawbacks of EMR in evaluating vulnerability detection models in smart contracts.

The Exact Match Ratio (EMR), as defined by EMR = (1/n) ∑_{i=1}^n I(y_i = ȳ_i) (Equation 4.2), where I denotes the indicator function, serves as a fundamental metric for assessing multi-label classification performance. However, a notable limitation of EMR lies in its inability to differentiate between partially correct and entirely incorrect predictions. This characteristic can render the metric excessively stringent, as it penalizes any deviation from a perfect match equally, thereby potentially underrepresenting the model’s partial successes. Recognizing this drawback is crucial when employing EMR to evaluate the efficacy of language model-based approaches for multi-label vulnerability detection in smart contracts, as it informs the interpretation of performance results and guides the development of more nuanced evaluation strategies.

A REST API, also referred to as a RESTful API, is an application programming interface that adheres to the principles of the REST architectural style, facilitating interaction with RESTful web services. When a client issues a request for a resource through a RESTful API, the representation of that resource is transmitted to the requester or endpoint. This representation is typically delivered over HTTP in various formats, including JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), HTML, XML, Python, PHP, or plain text. This method of communication is widely recognized and employed in web application development, enabling standardized and efficient data exchange.

Extremely preterm infants frequently require endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation during the initial days of life, but the adverse effects of prolonged invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) create a strong motivation for clinicians to extubate as early as safely possible. Current strategies for predicting extubation readiness are inconsistent across clinicians and institutions, resulting in high rates of reintubation. To address this, we propose an approach employing Random Forest classifiers that analyze cardiorespiratory variability to predict extubation readiness. Our method tackles the data imbalance problem by implementing random undersampling of the majority class prior to training each Decision Tree within the ensemble. Additionally, by integrating clinical domain knowledge, our classifier achieves the identification of 71% of infants who would fail extubation and maintains a success detection rate of 78%. These results suggest that machine learning models informed by physiological signals and clinical expertise can improve extubation decision-making, and future research should focus on validating these techniques in larger, multicenter cohorts and integrating them into clinical workflows. This paper addresses the challenge of generating realistic multi-dimensional real-valued time series data, particularly for medical applications, using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). We propose Recurrent GAN (RGAN) and Recurrent Conditional GAN (RCGAN) architectures, which integrate recurrent neural networks into both generator and discriminator, with RCGANs conditioning on auxiliary information. Our methodology is validated on toy datasets, employing both visual assessment and quantitative metrics such as sample likelihood and maximum mean discrepancy to demonstrate the capacity of our models to generate realistic time series. We introduce novel evaluation methods for GANs by generating synthetic labelled datasets to train models evaluated on real test sets, and vice versa. Results indicate that RCGANs produce synthetic time-series data suitable for supervised tasks, with minimal performance loss when models trained on synthetic data are tested on real data, as shown in digit classification using serialised MNIST and early warning prediction on an intensive care unit dataset of 17,000 patients. Finally, we discuss potential privacy concerns associated with generating synthetic medical time series data using RCGANs. (174 words)

Công nghệ 3.1 Blockchain 3.1.1 Khái niệm Blockchain Công nghệ chuỗi khối (Blockchain) được biết đến rộng rãi kể từ khi Nakamoto Satoshi công bố Bitcoin vào năm 2008. Chuỗi khối có thể được xem như một sổ cái công khai, trong đó toàn bộ các giao dịch đã được xác thực (committed transactions) được lưu trữ theo dạng danh sách các khối (block). Việc bảo mật và đảm bảo tính nhất quán dữ liệu trên sổ cái được thực hiện thông qua các thuật toán mã hóa phi đối xứng và thuật toán đồng thuận phân tán. Các đặc điểm nổi bật của công nghệ chuỗi khối bao gồm: (1) Phi tập trung; (2) Đảm bảo dữ liệu không bị mất mát hay thay đổi; (3) Ẩn danh; (4) Khả năng kiểm toán các giao dịch. Những đặc điểm này được đảm bảo bởi cấu trúc mạng phân tán ngang hàng (distributed peer-to-peer), trong đó phần mềm chạy trên các nút (node) lưu trữ bản sao dữ liệu các giao dịch trên toàn mạng, đồng thời cập nhật và xác thực các giao dịch xảy ra. Ethereum là chuỗi khối đầu tiên hỗ trợ thực thi các chương trình máy tính hoàn chỉnh (Turing Complete programs), hay còn gọi là “Smart Contract”, từ đó thúc đẩy sự phát triển mạnh mẽ của các ứng dụng dựa trên công nghệ blockchain. Nghiên cứu hiện tại tiếp tục khai thác và ứng dụng các đặc điểm ưu việt của blockchain cũng như smart contract để phát triển nền tảng số tối ưu cho giao dịch NFT và token.

We address the challenge of detecting critical structures in graphs using embedding models, noting that current approaches lack precision in identifying task-specific global structures. To overcome this, we introduce Ego-CNNs, a novel graph embedding model that utilizes ego-convolutions at each layer and stacks them in an ego-centric manner, enabling efficient and precise detection of critical structures. Ego-CNNs can be trained jointly with task models, offering explanations and discovery of relevant knowledge for the target task. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Ego-CNNs deliver task performance on par with state-of-the-art methods, effectively leverage CNN visualization to reveal detected structures, and operate efficiently, particularly when incorporating scale-free priors prevalent in social network data, thus further enhancing training efficiency. The main idea of the paragraph is to describe the TLS/SSL Security Tester sub-use case, which enables users to assess the security of TLS/SSL configurations in an uploaded Android application. The process involves analyzing the application's implementation of TLS/SSL protocols, certificate validation, and encryption, as well as detecting vulnerabilities such as weak ciphers, outdated protocols, and improper certificate validation that could lead to man-in-the-middle attacks or data breaches.

TLS/SSL Security Tester: This sub-use case provides users with the capability to systematically evaluate the security of TLS/SSL configurations within their uploaded Android applications. By performing an in-depth analysis, the system examines the application's implementation of TLS/SSL protocols, scrutinizes certificate validation processes, and assesses the employed encryption mechanisms. Furthermore, the system is designed to identify common vulnerabilities, including the presence of weak ciphers, reliance on outdated protocols, and inadequate certificate validation practices. Detection of these issues is critical, as they may render the application susceptible to man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks or result in significant data breaches.

The core idea centers on measuring each participating node's contribution by assessing the informational content of its data, then normalizing these contributions to create distinct weights for global model aggregation. This weighting strategy aims to enhance generalization across various data distribution scenarios. It addresses a specific issue in FedAdp, where nodes with incomplete label representation receive disproportionately high weights. FedImp is designed to avoid such biases, offering a more balanced and comprehensive approach to global model aggregation within the federated learning (FL) framework.

The primary intuition of this approach involves quantifying the contribution of each participating node by evaluating the informational content within its data. These contributions are then normalized to generate distinct weights used in aggregating the global model. The proposed weighting method is crafted to promote generalization across diverse data distribution scenarios. This design specifically targets a behavior observed in FedAdp, where nodes lacking full label representation are assigned higher weights. FedImp is therefore structured to mitigate such biases and shortcomings, aiming to deliver a more balanced and comprehensive strategy for global model aggregation in the federated learning framework.

This paper addresses the challenge of disentangling discrete spatial patterns and their continuous transformations in natural signals by integrating Lie groups, representation theory, and sparse coding into a Bayesian generative model. The motivation stems from the need to model image transformations and learn pattern dictionaries in an unsupervised manner. The approach involves modeling images as a sparse superposition of shape components, followed by transformations parameterized by continuous variables, with the constraint that these transformations represent an n-dimensional torus. The model is trained on a dataset with controlled geometric transformations of specific MNIST digits, demonstrating its ability to recover both transformations and digits. When applied to the full MNIST dataset, the model effectively learns the basic digit shapes and captures natural transformations such as shearing and stretching. The results suggest that this method can adaptively learn symmetries in data without predefined transformations, offering a promising direction for future research in unsupervised learning of image representations.

While self-supervised monocular depth estimation in driving scenarios has achieved performance comparable to supervised approaches, violations of the static world assumption can still result in erroneous depth predictions of traffic participants, posing potential safety risks. In this paper, we introduce R4Dyn, a novel set of techniques that incorporates cost-efficient radar data into a self-supervised depth estimation framework. Specifically, we demonstrate how radar can be leveraged during training as a weak supervision signal and used as an additional input to enhance estimation robustness during inference. Given the widespread availability of automotive radars, our approach enables the collection of training data from a diverse range of existing vehicles. Furthermore, by filtering and expanding the radar signal to ensure compatibility with learning-based methods, we effectively address inherent radar issues such as noise and sparsity. With R4Dyn, we successfully overcome a major limitation of self-supervised depth estimation—accurate prediction of traffic participants. Our method yields substantial improvements in estimating the depth of dynamic objects, such as cars, achieving a 37% improvement on the challenging nuScenes dataset, thereby demonstrating that radar serves as a valuable additional sensor for monocular depth estimation in autonomous vehicles. Additionally, we plan to make the code publicly available.

Computing optical flow is a fundamental problem in computer vision, but deep learning-based optical flow techniques often underperform on non-rigid movements, such as those in faces, due to insufficient training data capturing fine facial motion. This work hypothesizes that training on face motion data will enhance optical flow predictions for faces, aiming to (1) explore self-supervised techniques to generate optical flow ground truth for face images, (2) establish baseline results on training Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with face data for optical flow prediction, and (3) demonstrate the effectiveness of learned optical flow in micro-expression recognition. Optical flow ground truth is generated using facial key-points from the BP4D-Spontaneous dataset and used to train the FlowNetS architecture, whose performance on the generated dataset outperformed other optical flow CNN architectures, highlighting its utility. Additionally, optical flow features generated by this method, when evaluated with the STSTNet micro-expression classifier, showed promising results compared to other methods, suggesting that this approach holds significant potential for future advancements in facial expression analysis. This paper addresses the critical issue of post-hoc model explainability in complex predictive models, emphasizing the lack of robustness and reliability in current methods. It introduces techniques for attacking Partial Dependence (PD) plots, a prevalent method used to explain predictive models trained on tabular data. The research demonstrates how PD can be adversarially manipulated, raising concerns about the integrity of explanations in high-stakes areas like finance and healthcare where auditability is essential for black-box models. The manipulation is achieved by poisoning data to intentionally alter and direct explanations using genetic and gradient algorithms. This study is pioneering in its focus on attacking variable dependence explanations, and the novel use of a genetic algorithm offers a highly adaptable approach, applicable in both model-agnostic and explanation-agnostic contexts. The implications of this work suggest a need for more robust methods to ensure the trustworthiness of model explanations, and it opens avenues for future research to explore defensive strategies against such adversarial attacks.

This thesis primarily presents the explicit formula for determining the maximal length and maximal asymptotic rate of RdB sequences, accompanied by an encoding algorithm designed to achieve these metrics. Additionally, the thesis substantiates the optimality of this encoder through rigorous proof. To facilitate the identification of a specific substring within the entire encoded sequence, a decoding algorithm is introduced, leveraging the foundational decoder of the granddaddy sequence. Both the encoder and decoder are built upon state-of-the-art algorithms. Notably, the encoder demonstrates a constant amortized time complexity per symbol, while the decoder exhibits a sub-linear complexity relative to the length of the RdB sequence.

This paper investigates the role of entropy regularization in policy optimization within reinforcement learning, motivated by its purported benefits of promoting stochastic policy selection. The study introduces novel visualization techniques that involve randomly perturbing the loss function to analyze the optimization landscape. The research initially demonstrates the inherent challenges in policy optimization caused by the complex geometry of the objective function, even when the exact gradient is accessible. Through qualitative assessments, the paper reveals that in certain environments, policies with higher entropy can smooth the optimization landscape, effectively connecting local optima and supporting the use of larger learning rates. The findings provide new tools for visualizing the optimization landscape, affirm the role of policy entropy as a regularizer, and underscore the difficulty of crafting general-purpose policy optimization algorithms. These insights have significant implications for future research, suggesting areas for further exploration in developing more effective and adaptable reinforcement learning methodologies.

Efficient reuse of prior experience is essential for sample-efficient reinforcement learning, with the quality of experience representation and storage playing a pivotal role. Traditional approaches have relied on storing experiences in forms such as features, individual models, or average models, each corresponding to a specific granularity of knowledge. However, the diversity and complexity of new tasks often necessitate access to experience at multiple levels of granularity. The policy residual representation (PRR) network addresses this challenge by enabling the extraction and storage of experience across multiple hierarchical levels. Structured as a multi-level architecture, the PRR network assigns modules at each level to subsets of training tasks, creating a spectrum-like representation of transferable experience. This design allows the network to offer tailored experience at varying granularities when encountering novel tasks, thereby enhancing the speed and effectiveness of learning. Empirical evaluations on tasks such as grid world navigation, locomotion, and video game combat demonstrate that the PRR network achieves superior experience reuse and outperforms several state-of-the-art reinforcement learning methods, highlighting its potential for advancing sample efficiency in complex environments.

In this study, we explore building a two-stage framework for enabling users to directly manipulate high-level attributes of a natural scene. The key to our approach is a deep generative network which can hallucinate images of a scene as if they were taken at a different season (e.g. during winter), weather condition (e.g. in a cloudy day) or time of the day (e.g. at sunset). Once the scene is hallucinated with the given attributes, the corresponding look is then transferred to the input image while preserving the semantic details intact, giving a photo-realistic manipulation result. As the proposed framework hallucinates what the scene will look like, it does not require any reference style image as commonly utilized in most of the appearance or style transfer approaches. Moreover, it allows to simultaneously manipulate a given scene according to a diverse set of transient attributes within a single model, eliminating the need of training multiple networks per each translation task. Our comprehensive set of qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach against the competing methods.

By offering a robust and adaptable framework for sequence data analysis, Seglearn significantly advances the accessibility and efficiency of time series machine learning tasks. LiDAR data's critical role in autonomous vehicles stems from its ability to deliver a 360° horizontal field of view through point clouds, significantly enhancing situational awareness. Synthetic LiDAR data generation is vital for advancing machine learning research, but existing physically accurate simulators like Blensor are hindered by substantial rendering times, averaging 14-60 seconds per urban scene frame. Although platforms like CARLA mitigate this by employing low poly assets, this results in coarse, unrealistic point clouds. This paper introduces a novel approach for simulating LiDAR point clouds that achieves a much faster rendering time of 1 second per frame by leveraging spherical UV unwrapping of Equirectangular Z-Buffer images. Comparative analysis against the Blensor baseline (Gschwandtner et al., 2011) demonstrates that the proposed method achieves a reported error of 4.28cm in complex urban landscapes over a scanning range of 2-120 meters using Velodyne HDL64-E2 parameters and a total time per frame of 3.2 +/- 0.31 seconds, while the Blensor baseline requires 16.2 +/- 1.82 seconds. These results present a significant advancement in rendering efficiency without substantial loss of accuracy, paving the way for more scalable and realistic LiDAR data generation in future autonomous vehicle research.

Traffic control optimization is a complex task faced by traffic centers worldwide, with most existing approaches focused on adaptive methods for normal traffic conditions. However, optimizing control plans during severe incidents, especially when many lanes or entire intersections are impacted, remains a significant challenge. This paper addresses this issue by introducing a new methodology for optimizing traffic signal timings at signalized urban intersections during non-recurrent traffic incidents. To achieve rapid and reliable decision-making, we integrate the fast execution of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms with the dependability of Genetic Algorithms (GA) within a single optimization framework. Initially, we deploy a standard GA algorithm, treating phase duration as the decision variable and aiming to minimize total travel time across the network. We fine-tune the GA for crossover, mutation, and fitness calculation to derive optimal parameters. Next, we train various machine learning regression models to predict total travel time in the traffic network, selecting the best-performing regressor for further hyper-tuning to determine optimal training parameters. Finally, we introduce a new algorithm, BGA-ML, which combines the GA algorithm with the best-performing regressor, the extreme-gradient decision-tree, into a single optimization framework. Comparisons and results demonstrate that BGA-ML is significantly faster than the original GA algorithm and proves effective under non-recurrent incident conditions.

Learning disentangled representations of natural language is crucial for numerous NLP tasks, including conditional text generation, style transfer, and personalized dialogue systems. While similar challenges have been extensively explored in other data modalities such as images and videos, the discrete nature of natural language presents unique difficulties, particularly in manipulating the data space. Drawing inspiration from information theory, we propose a novel, unsupervised method to effectively learn disentangled textual representations. We derive a new upper bound on mutual information to quantify the dependence between style and content representations. By minimizing this upper bound, our approach induces style and content embeddings that occupy two independent low-dimensional spaces. Experimental results on conditional text generation and text style transfer tasks demonstrate that our method achieves high-quality disentangled representations, preserving both content and style effectively.

The rapid development of high-throughput technologies has enabled the generation of data from biological or disease processes spanning multiple layers, such as genomic, proteomic, or metabolomic data, and involving multiple sources, such as disease subtypes or experimental conditions. In this work, we propose a general statistical framework based on Gaussian graphical models for the horizontal (i.e., across conditions or subtypes) and vertical (i.e., across different layers containing data on molecular compartments) integration of information in such datasets. We begin by decomposing the multi-layer problem into a series of two-layer problems. For each two-layer problem, we model the outcomes at a node in the lower layer as dependent on those of other nodes in that layer, as well as all nodes in the upper layer. We employ a combination of neighborhood selection and group-penalized regression to obtain sparse estimates of all model parameters. Following this, we develop a debiasing technique and asymptotic distributions of inter-layer directed edge weights that utilize already computed neighborhood selection coefficients for nodes in the upper layer. Subsequently, we establish global and simultaneous testing procedures for these edge weights. The performance of the proposed methodology is evaluated on synthetic and real data.

The paragraph discusses the concept of upgradable contracts as a solution to the immutability issue inherent in smart contracts, particularly on the Ethereum network. It outlines two primary approaches to upgrading contracts: separating logic from the proxy contract, and using a contract registry. The summary also highlights that while these approaches address certain limitations, they introduce new vulnerabilities, which are relevant to the detection process using techniques such as temporal message propagation (TMP) networks.

The concept of upgradable contracts was proposed as a means to address the immutability challenge in smart contracts, particularly since, once a contract is deployed on the Ethereum network, subsequent updates or bug patches are not feasible. To mitigate this limitation, the contract’s structure is normalized to emphasize significant nodes and is subsequently processed by a temporal message propagation (TMP) network for vulnerability detection, as discussed in relevant studies such as [Author, Year]. There are two primary strategies for contract upgrades: (i) decomposing the contract into a proxy contract and a logic contract, although this method is considered unconventional; and (ii) implementing a contract registry to store updated versions of contracts. While these methods enhance upgradeability and flexibility, it is important to note that the contract registry approach, despite its effectiveness, introduces a novel class of vulnerabilities, thereby necessitating advanced detection techniques as explored in this thesis.

Abstract: Sequence labeling is a fundamental problem in natural language processing, and this paper proposes a novel approach using Gaussian process models based on pseudo-likelihood approximation. Gaussian processes offer a Bayesian framework for learning with kernels, and the pseudo-likelihood model captures long-range dependencies among sequence output components without becoming computationally prohibitive. An efficient variational Gaussian approximation method is utilized for inference, complemented by an iterative algorithm that leverages information from neighboring labels for prediction. This method's capability to capture long-range dependencies broadens its applicability across various sequence labeling tasks. Empirical results from experiments on sequence labeling datasets underscore the approach's effectiveness and potential.

TensorFlow is a framework; to understand what TensorFlow is, it is necessary to first grasp the concept of a framework in the software field. Trong quá trình xử lý ảnh, để giảm thiểu số lượng bounding boxes không cần thiết trên các ảnh và các kernels, hai phương pháp chủ yếu được áp dụng là thiết lập ngưỡng threshold cho confidence score và sử dụng kỹ thuật Non-Max Suppression (NMS). Cụ thể, các bounding boxes có confidence score thấp hơn ngưỡng xác định trước sẽ bị loại bỏ nhằm đảm bảo chỉ giữ lại các dự đoán có độ tin cậy cao. Sau đó, thuật toán NMS tiếp tục được sử dụng để xử lý các bounding boxes còn lại bằng cách loại bỏ những box có tỉ lệ giao nhau (Intersection Over Union) vượt quá một ngưỡng threshold được xác định, từ đó chỉ giữ lại duy nhất một bounding box có confidence score cao nhất cho mỗi đối tượng. Phần này trình bày thiết kế các API phục vụ nghiệp vụ liên quan đến lộ trình học trong ĐATN, được tổng hợp trong bảng 4.8 với các cột: STT, mục đích sử dụng, phương thức và mô tả API. Các API sửa đổi nhằm hỗ trợ logic xóa chương hoặc thêm loại bài tập không được đưa vào bảng vì chỉ thay đổi xử lý dữ liệu nội bộ, không ảnh hưởng đến định danh hay ý nghĩa. Bảng liệt kê các API như lấy danh sách lộ trình học (GET /paths), lấy chi tiết (GET /paths:d), tạo mới (POST /paths), cập nhật (PUT /paths:d), xóa (DELETE /paths:d), thêm bình luận (POST /paths/comment/:d), nộp, xuất bản, đình chỉ lộ trình (PUT /pathsubmt, /pathpublsh, /pathreject), chuyển lộ trình cho người soạn sửa đổi (PUT /pathrequesttochange), tìm kiếm và lọc lộ trình (POST /path/search, /path/flter), lấy và tạo phiên bản lộ trình học (GET, POST /verpath/:d). Representation learning for pedestrian trajectories translates variable-length timestamp-coordinate tuples of a trajectory into a fixed-length vector representation that encapsulates spatiotemporal characteristics. This technique is essential for bridging feature-based data mining with trajectory data. Trajectory representation poses a significant challenge due to the need to meticulously consider and account for both environmental constraints (e.g., wall partitions) and temporal user dynamics. Moreover, traditional sequence-to-sequence autoencoders relying on maximum log-likelihood often necessitate datasets that encompass all possible spatiotemporal characteristics for optimal performance, which is often infeasible or impractical. We propose TREP, an effective pedestrian trajectory representation learning algorithm that captures environmental constraints and pedestrian dynamics without requiring any training dataset. By formulating a sequence-to-sequence autoencoder with a spatial-aware objective function under the actor-critic reinforcement learning paradigm, TREP adeptly encodes spatiotemporal characteristics of trajectories, accommodating diverse trajectory patterns. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets validate TREP's high fidelity in trajectory representation.

The main idea of the paragraph is that synchronization among players is a critical requirement in multiplayer action games, as any asynchronous or delayed updates between players can severely affect the gaming experience and influence the game's success. Specific examples are provided to illustrate how discrepancies in event timing, such as defeating a boss or character movement, can disrupt the gameplay when updates are not properly synchronized.

Synchronization among players constitutes a fundamental requirement in multiplayer action games, as it ensures that all participants share a consistent and coherent view of in-game events. Discrepancies arising from asynchronous or delayed updates can manifest as situations where, for example, one player observes a boss being defeated at time t, while another player, thirty seconds later at time t + 30s, still perceives the boss as alive. Similarly, when a player moves to a new location, such as ascending to the second floor of a building, delayed synchronization may result in other players only seeing them at the previous position, such as the front door. Such inconsistencies not only disrupt the immersive experience but also represent a significant factor influencing the overall success of a multiplayer game, as reflected in numerous studies on real-time game synchronization and network latency (see Table 3.5 for further empirical data on synchronization delays).

Socket là một giao diện lập trình ứng dụng mạng (network application programming interface) cho phép truyền và nhận dữ liệu qua Internet giữa hai chương trình đang hoạt động trên các máy tính khác nhau. Để thiết lập một kết nối giao tiếp hai chiều (two way communication) giữa hai process, mỗi process sẽ sử dụng một endpoint gọi là socket, như được minh họa trong Hình 3.5. Ưu điểm nổi bật của socket là khả năng hỗ trợ trên hầu hết các hệ điều hành phổ biến như MS Windows, Linux, v.v., đồng thời có thể được tích hợp với nhiều ngôn ngữ lập trình khác nhau như C, C++, Java, Visual Basic, Visual C++,... Điều này giúp socket trở nên linh hoạt và dễ dàng thích ứng với nhiều loại cấu hình máy tính và đối tượng người dùng khác nhau. Bên cạnh đó, socket còn cho phép người dùng có thể khởi tạo và vận hành đồng thời nhiều kết nối cùng lúc, từ đó nâng cao hiệu suất truyền thông và tiết kiệm tối đa thời gian cũng như công sức trong quá trình xử lý dữ liệu trên mạng.

Trong những năm gần đây, việc học biểu diễn (representation learning) cho các mạng không đồng nhất (heterogeneous networks) đã thu hút sự quan tâm lớn từ cộng đồng nghiên cứu do khả năng nắm bắt các đặc trưng cấu trúc đa dạng và quan hệ phức tạp giữa các loại nút khác nhau. Đóng góp nổi bật trong lĩnh vực này là phương pháp MetaPath2Vec do Dong và cộng sự đề xuất, cho phép xây dựng vector biểu diễn cho các nút trong mạng không đồng nhất thông qua việc sử dụng các meta-path, từ đó cải thiện hiệu quả trong các bài toán như phân loại nút và dự đoán liên kết (Y. Dong, N. V. Chawla and. Swam, 2017). Tuy nhiên, một số nghiên cứu trước chủ yếu tập trung vào tối ưu hiệu suất tính toán hoặc chất lượng biểu diễn mà chưa xem xét đầy đủ đến khả năng mở rộng trên các mạng quy mô lớn hoặc các ứng dụng thực tiễn cụ thể. Nghiên cứu hiện tại kế thừa ý tưởng sử dụng meta-path để học biểu diễn nhưng đề xuất cơ chế chọn meta-path động dựa trên đặc trưng miền ứng dụng, qua đó vừa đảm bảo khả năng mở rộng, vừa nâng cao tính thích ứng của biểu diễn đối với từng bài toán cụ thể. Như vậy, nghiên cứu này góp phần làm phong phú thêm hướng tiếp cận học representation learning cho mạng không đồng nhất, đồng thời mở rộng tính thực tiễn của các phương pháp dựa trên meta-path trong các hệ thống dữ liệu lớn.

Disease-oriented image embedding with pseudo-scanner standardization (DI-PSS) presents a novel framework for enhancing content-based image retrieval (CBIR) in clinical brain MRI databases by addressing inter-scanner variability and improving disease-specific representation. The DI-PSS approach incorporates robust data harmonization via skull stripping and CycleGAN-based image transformations, aligning images to a standardized brain model and subsequently to a reference scanner domain. This harmonized output is then processed using 3D convolutional autoencoders integrated with deep metric learning to generate low-dimensional embeddings that more accurately capture disease-related features. Evaluation on T1-weighted MRIs from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative and the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative demonstrated that DI-PSS significantly reduces embedding variability attributable to differences in scanner hardware and datasets. Notably, the system decreased the variability in disease-to-control distances by 15.8-22.6% for Alzheimer's disease and 18.0-29.9% for Parkinson's disease compared to baseline methods. Furthermore, spectral clustering-based classification showed that DI-PSS improved average accuracy and macro-F1 scores by 6.2% and 10.7%, respectively. These findings indicate that DI-PSS is highly effective for harmonizing heterogeneous MRI data, enabling more reliable disease classification and supporting its application to diverse and legacy brain MRI datasets.

Trong bối cảnh các sản phẩm có nhu cầu tiêu thụ ổn định, nhiều nhà sản xuất lựa chọn phương thức Make-To-Stock (MTS) cho hoạt động sản xuất của mình. Theo đó, sản phẩm được sản xuất trước và lưu trữ trong kho nhằm đáp ứng nhanh chóng các đơn hàng phát sinh trong các giai đoạn tiếp theo. Cách tiếp cận này không chỉ giúp doanh nghiệp đáp ứng kịp thời nhu cầu của khách hàng mà còn đảm bảo duy trì chuỗi cung ứng liên tục, từ đó nâng cao mức độ hài lòng và củng cố uy tín đối với khách hàng.

Nhu cầu mua bán sản phẩm, đặc biệt là nội thất, ngày càng tăng nhưng hình thức giao dịch truyền thống yêu cầu người mua và người bán phải gặp mặt trực tiếp để xem, lựa chọn và thanh toán sản phẩm. Chủ cửa hàng nội thất cũng phải đầu tư vào việc xây dựng nhiều địa điểm trưng bày để tiếp cận khách hàng, dẫn đến tốn kém về thời gian và chi phí cho cả hai bên, nhất là khi sản phẩm không đáp ứng kỳ vọng của khách hàng. Do đó, việc phát triển một hình thức mua bán mới, cho phép giao dịch giữa người bán và người mua qua môi trường ảo trên mạng máy tính mà không cần gặp mặt trực tiếp, sẽ giúp tiết kiệm đáng kể thời gian và chi phí cho cả chủ cửa hàng nội thất và khách hàng.

Hiện nay, với sự gia tăng nhu cầu mua bán và trao đổi các sản phẩm, trong đó có nội thất, hình thức giao dịch truyền thống đòi hỏi người mua và người bán phải gặp mặt trực tiếp để xem xét, lựa chọn và thanh toán sản phẩm. Điều này đồng nghĩa với việc các chủ cửa hàng nội thất phải xây dựng nhiều địa điểm trưng bày nhằm đưa thông tin sản phẩm đến khách hàng, dẫn đến lãng phí thời gian và chi phí cho cả hai bên, đặc biệt khi sản phẩm không đáp ứng được mong đợi của khách hàng. Do vậy, việc ứng dụng một mô hình mua bán mới thông qua môi trường ảo trên mạng máy tính, cho phép các bên giao dịch mà không cần gặp mặt trực tiếp, sẽ góp phần tiết kiệm hiệu quả thời gian và chi phí cho cả chủ cửa hàng lẫn khách hàng.

Nghiên cứu này được thúc đẩy bởi mối quan ngại về nguy cơ biến chứng do tồn dư thuốc giãn cơ, đặc biệt là trong phẫu thuật nội soi ổ bụng. Mục tiêu là xác định tỷ lệ tồn dư thuốc giãn cơ rocuronium sau phẫu thuật này. Nghiên cứu cắt ngang mô tả được thực hiện trên 92 bệnh nhân tại khoa Gây mê hồi sức, Bệnh viện Nguyễn Tri Phương. Sử dụng chỉ số TOF (train of four) đo bằng máy TOF-watch để theo dõi tồn dư rocuronium tại các thời điểm: trước khi hóa giải giãn cơ, khi rút ống nội khí quản và sau rút ống 15, 30, 60, 90, và 120 phút. Kết quả cho thấy tỷ lệ tồn dư rocuronium (TOF < 0,9) tại các thời điểm này lần lượt là 100%; 53,3%; 10,9%; 8,7%; 3,3% và 0%. Kết luận rằng tỷ lệ tồn dư rocuronium sau phẫu thuật là khá cao nhưng giảm dần theo thời gian. Điều này nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc theo dõi, nhận biết và đánh giá sớm nguy cơ tồn dư để giảm thiểu biến chứng và nâng cao chất lượng hồi tỉnh cho bệnh nhân.

We address the challenge of user association by optimizing the assignment of user equipment to base stations to meet specific network performance goals. This paper concentrates on the knowledge transferability of association policies. Traditional user association schemes are often tailored to specific scenarios or deployments, necessitating policy redesign or relearning when user numbers or locations change. In contrast, transferability enables the application of a single user association policy, originally designed for a specific scenario, to various user deployments without significant relearning or redesign, thereby reducing computational and management complexity. To facilitate transferability, we first model user association as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem. Utilizing a neural attention mechanism specifically designed for this context, we introduce a novel distributed policy network architecture that is transferable among users with zero-shot generalization capability, meaning it requires no additional training. Our numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in enhancing overall network communication rates, surpassing centralized benchmarks even when the user count doubles from the initial training point.

The main idea of the paragraph is to emphasize the importance of identifying which findings have been suppressed during static analysis, without requiring the user to review the scan process or detailed analysis results. This ensures transparency and accountability in static analysis by highlighting suppressed issues directly.

In the context of static analysis for Android malware detection, it is often crucial to identify which findings have been suppressed, independently of the overall scan or the intricate details of the analysis results. Recognizing suppressed findings helps maintain transparency in the evaluation process and allows researchers and practitioners to focus on potential blind spots or areas where automated tools might have overlooked certain vulnerabilities. As highlighted in related works such as Li et al. (2019) and Arp et al. (2014), ensuring clear visibility into suppressed findings is essential for robust security assessments. The approach proposed in this thesis aims to streamline the reporting of suppressed findings, thereby contributing to enhanced auditability and trustworthiness in static analysis workflows for Android malware scanning.

Estimation of individual-level causal effects from observational data has emerged as a critical challenge across domains such as healthcare, economics, and education, where randomized experiments are often costly or infeasible. Recent advances in electronic record keeping have made large-scale, non-experimental data increasingly available, necessitating robust methods for causal inference in such settings. This work addresses the estimation of personalized treatment effects by leveraging context, decision, and outcome data, focusing on providing generalization bounds for estimation errors. These bounds are derived using distance measures between groups subjected to different treatments, which informs strategies for sample re-weighting and representation learning. Theoretical analysis establishes conditions for the tightness of these bounds and draws connections to unsupervised domain adaptation. Building on these results, novel representation learning algorithms are introduced that minimize the derived bounds through regularization of the induced group distances and facilitate information sharing across treatment groups. An extension to weighted representations further enhances the alignment between groups, thereby improving estimation accuracy. Empirical evaluations on both real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed methods, underscoring the practical benefits of the developed representation architectures and regularization techniques for causal effect estimation in observational studies.

The paragraph emphasizes the importance of enhancing the user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) of a social media web application, highlighting the need for visual appeal, smooth interactions, mobile optimization, group communication features, and improved website performance through advanced deployment strategies. These improvements are considered essential for increasing user engagement and ensuring the platform's competitiveness.

Enhancing the UX/UI of a social media application is paramount, as visual appeal and seamless user interactions significantly influence user retention and engagement (see Table 3.5 for user feedback statistics). To attract a broader user base, the interface must be not only aesthetically pleasing but also provide an intuitive and frictionless user experience. Particularly for social media platforms, it is essential that the web application offers complete functionality and an optimized interface for mobile devices, given the prevalence of smartphone usage for social networking (Smith & Anderson, 2018). Furthermore, implementing features such as user groups, group message channels, and group audio/video calls can foster greater interaction among users, enhancing the platform’s sense of community (Kietzmann et al., 2011). Điển hình là thuật toán TaxoGen, sử dụng embedding từ điển để biểu diễn các thuật ngữ trích xuất từ văn bản. Mỗi nút trong cây phân loại (taxonomy) được liên kết với một tập hợp tài liệu liên quan, từ đó TaxoGen học được embedding cho các thuật ngữ tương ứng với từng nút. The paragraph discusses the use of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) encoders, specifically Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) or Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layers, in encoding source sequences. It highlights the ability of RNN encoders to employ multiple layers to capture detailed language representations, starting with the 0th layer that consists of word embeddings derived from the source sequence's word order.

RNN encoders are designed to utilize LSTM or GRU layers for the purpose of encoding source sequences. These encoders are capable of deploying multiple layers, enabling them to capture more nuanced language representations. The initial layer, known as the 0th layer, comprises a sequence of word embeddings. These embeddings are extracted from the source-side look-up table, based on the word order dictated by the source sequence. This layered approach allows for a more thorough understanding and processing of the input data, as each layer contributes to refining the representation of the sequence. By leveraging the structural depth provided by multiple layers, RNN encoders can effectively enhance the precision and richness of the encoded language data.

An assistive system designed to guide visually impaired users to their destinations via speech and haptic feedback can benefit significantly from personalized interaction strategies. Current navigation technologies, such as portable, ground, or wearable systems, frequently employ a generic approach that does not account for individual user needs or mobility skills, potentially leading to confusion and navigation errors. To enhance the effectiveness of these systems, a novel model-based reinforcement learning framework is proposed, which personalizes the interaction experience by adapting to the unique characteristics of each user. This framework incorporates a weighted experts model to overcome data-efficiency challenges in transfer learning with deep models, facilitating quick adaptation to new users. Using a real-world dataset of navigation by blind users, the framework demonstrates improved long-term human behavior prediction, accurately forecasting up to 20 seconds into the future by considering personal mobility attributes, interaction with obstacles, and navigation goals. Additionally, the system exhibits rapid adaptation during initial learning phases, even when data availability is limited, marking a substantial advancement in assistive navigation technology for visually impaired individuals.

User data confidentiality in deep learning research poses an increasing challenge. Conventional data-driven model compression, which typically necessitates data access, faces heightened risks of performance degradation. Recent studies suggest generating images from pretrained models as substitute training data. However, this approach relies on biased feature statistics from a single model and involves transitioning from low to high dimensions, resulting in challenges with generalizability and precise inversion, ultimately leading to subpar performance. To address these issues, we introduce MixMix, leveraging two straightforward yet effective techniques: (1) Feature Mixing, which employs multiple models to establish a universal feature space for enhanced inversion generalizability; and (2) Data Mixing, which combines synthesized images and labels to produce accurate label information. We demonstrate the efficacy of MixMix through both theoretical analysis and empirical validation. Comprehensive experiments indicate that MixMix surpasses existing methods in mainstream compression tasks, such as quantization, knowledge distillation, and pruning. Notably, MixMix delivers accuracy improvements of up to 4% in quantization and 20% in pruning compared to current data-free compression approaches.

F. Chung, P. Diaconis, and R. Graham explore the concept of universal cycles within the realm of combinatorial structures in their influential paper, "Universal cycles for combinatorial structures," published in Discrete Mathematics. The authors develop the theory surrounding universal cycles, which are sequences that can represent all possible configurations of a given combinatorial object. Their work has laid the groundwork for further exploration in the field, enabling subsequent research to build upon their foundational ideas and methodologies. By applying their theoretical framework, researchers can gain a deeper understanding of the properties and applications of universal cycles across various combinatorial contexts. This paper, cited as a seminal work in the study of combinatorial structures, continues to be a critical reference for academics and practitioners aiming to harness the potential of universal cycles in discrete mathematics.

In physical retail environments, customers can immediately obtain purchased items, whereas online shoppers must endure a waiting period for merchandise delivery. Despite advancements in logistics that have popularized next-day and even same-day shipping, as illustrated in recent studies on e-commerce fulfillment (see Table 3.5), the delay inherent to online purchasing continues to influence the overall shopping experience. This research addresses the implications of delivery wait times on user expectations and proposes how a SaaS-based search engine for e-commerce websites can incorporate real-time shipping information to better inform customer decisions, thereby enhancing user satisfaction and operational efficiency—an approach that builds on the insights of Smith et al. (2022) and Chen & Lee (2020).

Tổn thất và thiệt hại do biến đổi khí hậu là vấn đề ngày càng nghiêm trọng, vượt quá khả năng thích ứng của nhiều cộng đồng, đặc biệt khi nguồn lực còn hạn chế. Tại Việt Nam, chỉ trong giai đoạn 2011-2020, các hiện tượng khí hậu cực đoan đã gây ra tổng thiệt hại kinh tế lên tới khoảng 10 tỷ đô la Mỹ, đồng thời tiềm ẩn nguy cơ tổn thất phi kinh tế ngày càng rõ nét.

This paper presents our approach to the Traffic4cast 2020 competition, which required developing algorithms to predict future traffic states in major cities. We addressed the problem by focusing on feature and loss function design, resulting in significant improvements to the previously best-performing U-Net model from Traffic4cast 2019. Additionally, we investigated the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and introduced a novel ensemble GNN architecture that outperformed last year’s GNN solution. Despite these advancements, our GNN model still did not surpass the U-Net’s performance, and we discuss possible reasons for this limitation. Ultimately, by ensembling our enhanced U-Net and GNN models, our solution secured 4th place in the Traffic4cast 2020 competition, demonstrating the effectiveness of our methodological contributions and providing insights into the comparative strengths of U-Net and GNN architectures for traffic state prediction. When training a neural network for a desired task, adapting a pre-trained network is often preferred over starting with randomly initialized weights. Such adaptation is beneficial when training data is scarce, when a single learner must perform multiple tasks, or when encoding priors in the network is desirable. The predominant methods for network adaptation include fine-tuning and using the pre-trained network as a fixed feature extractor. In this paper, we propose a straightforward alternative: side-tuning. Side-tuning adapts a pre-trained network by training a lightweight "side" network that is integrated with the unchanged pre-trained network through summation. This simple method performs as well as or better than existing solutions and addresses fundamental issues associated with fine-tuning, fixed features, and other common approaches. Specifically, side-tuning is less prone to overfitting, asymptotically consistent, and does not suffer from catastrophic forgetting in incremental learning. We demonstrate the efficacy of side-tuning across diverse scenarios, including incremental learning (iCIFAR, iTaskonomy), reinforcement learning, imitation learning (visual navigation in Habitat), NLP question-answering (SQuAD v2), and single-task transfer learning (Taskonomy), with consistently promising results.

The main idea of the paragraph concerns the ROUGE metric, which assesses the similarity between a system-generated summary and a reference summary by measuring the overlap of individual words, and then calculates precision and recall as quantitative indicators of summary quality. ROUGE is widely recognized as a standard evaluation metric in automatic text summarization tasks, particularly for its effectiveness in capturing n-gram overlaps between generated and reference summaries. This metric, as illustrated in Table 3.5, computes both precision and recall to provide an objective measure of summary quality, thus facilitating a consistent and reproducible evaluation framework for multi-document summarization systems. The use of ROUGE in the evaluation of Vietnamese multi-document summarization systems, as referenced in related works such as Lin (2004), underscores its significance in the field and highlights its adaptability to different languages and datasets. By employing ROUGE, this thesis contributes to the ongoing development of robust and language-agnostic evaluation methodologies within the domain of automatic summarization.

We introduce CodeReef, an open platform designed to facilitate cross-platform MLOps (Machine Learning System Operations), which automates the deployment of machine learning models across diverse systems with optimal efficiency. CodeReef is presented as a solution to package and disseminate models as non-virtualized, portable, customizable, and reproducible archive files. These ML packages incorporate a JSON meta-description of models, encompassing all dependencies, Python APIs, CLI actions, and portable workflows necessary for the automatic construction, benchmarking, testing, and customization of models across varied platforms, AI frameworks, libraries, compilers, and datasets. We illustrate several CodeReef solutions, showcasing the automated building, execution, and evaluation of object detection models based on SSD-Mobilenets, TensorFlow, and the COCO dataset, aligned with the latest MLPerf inference benchmark across a broad spectrum of platforms, including Raspberry Pi, Android phones, IoT devices, and data centers. Our long-term objective is to empower researchers to share their innovations as production-ready packages in conjunction with their research papers, thereby fostering collaborative and reproducible benchmarking. This enables the comparison of various ML/software/hardware configurations and the selection of the most efficient options on a Pareto frontier, utilizing online CodeReef dashboards.

Mỗi công việc hoặc giai đoạn được thể hiện bằng hai thanh ngang, trong đó thanh phía trên mô tả tiến độ thực tế và thanh phía dưới mô tả tiến độ dự kiến (baseline). Việc sử dụng phương pháp hiển thị baseline như vậy giúp tăng cường tính trực quan trong việc theo dõi tiến độ của dự án. Riêng đối với tiến độ thực tế của giai đoạn, hai đầu thanh sẽ được đánh dấu bằng hai đoạn thẳng màu đen để phân biệt rõ ràng với thanh tiến độ của từng công việc. Các mốc quan trọng (milestone) được biểu diễn bằng hình thoi, góp phần làm nổi bật các thời điểm then chốt trong dự án. Bên cạnh đó, màu sắc được sử dụng để phản ánh trạng thái tiến độ của từng công việc, giai đoạn hoặc mốc: màu đỏ biểu thị nhiệm vụ đã quá hạn, màu xanh cho biết công việc chưa đến thời điểm thực hiện hoặc đang vượt tiến độ so với kế hoạch, còn màu vàng thể hiện sự chậm trễ so với tiến độ dự kiến. Cách tiếp cận trực quan này không chỉ giúp nhà quản lý dự án nhận diện nhanh các vấn đề phát sinh mà còn hỗ trợ hiệu quả trong việc ra quyết định điều chỉnh kế hoạch khi cần thiết.

We introduce HarperValleyBank, a free, public domain spoken dialog corpus designed to simulate simple consumer banking interactions, comprising approximately 23 hours of audio from 1,446 human-human conversations among 59 unique speakers. The corpus features carefully selected intents and utterance templates to balance realistic variation with controlled task complexity, resulting in a limited vocabulary of about 700 unique words. Accompanying the audio data are transcripts and annotations detailing speaker identity, caller intent, dialog actions, and emotional valence, facilitating rapid transcription experiments with state-of-the-art end-to-end neural approaches. Additionally, we establish baselines for representation learning by adapting recent methods to embed waveforms for downstream prediction tasks. Experimental results indicate that tasks leveraging our annotations are sensitive to both model architecture and dataset size, highlighting the corpus’s utility for evaluating and advancing spoken dialog systems. Online learning with expert advice is fundamental in many machine learning applications, yet practical deployment is challenged by uncertainties in the feedback graph that encodes relationships among experts. Motivated by the prevalence of such uncertainties, this paper investigates scenarios where the feedback graph is not fully reliable and analyzes how to exploit partial or uncertain feedback to improve learning outcomes. The authors propose new online learning algorithms capable of handling various types of feedback graph uncertainties, ensuring robust performance even when the true relationships among experts are obscured. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed methods achieve sublinear regret under mild assumptions, confirming their effectiveness. Experiments conducted on real datasets further validate the practicality and superiority of these algorithms. The findings highlight the importance of accommodating graph uncertainty in online learning and open avenues for future research on more realistic models of expert advice systems.

Measuring and analyzing customer flow in retail environments is crucial for retailers to gain insights into customer behavior and aid decision-making processes. Despite this importance, there has been limited focus on developing innovative technologies for automatic people counting. We present LRCN-RetailNet, a recurrent neural network architecture designed to learn a non-linear regression model and accurately predict people counts using videos from low-cost surveillance cameras. The input videos use the newly proposed RGBP image format, which includes color and people (foreground) information. Our architecture addresses two key factors: spatial features derived from convolutional layers applied to RGBP images, and the temporal coherence of the problem, which is leveraged by recurrent layers. Utilizing a supervised learning approach, our trained models demonstrate high accuracy in predicting people counts. Furthermore, we show that a simple modification of the method effectively excludes salespeople from the count. Extensive experiments were conducted to validate, evaluate, and compare the proposed architecture. The results confirmed that LRCN-RetailNet significantly surpasses the previous RetailNet architecture, which was restricted to a single image per iteration, as well as a leading neural network for object detection. Lastly, computational performance tests verified that the complete methodology efficiently estimates people counts in real-time.

Title: UltraSR: Ultra-Accurate Arbitrary-Scale Super-Resolution via Spatial Encoding

Abstract (143 words): The recent success of NeRF and other related implicit neural representation methods has opened a new path for continuous image representation, where pixel values no longer need to be looked up from stored discrete 2D arrays but can be inferred from neural network models on a continuous spatial domain. Although the recent work LIIF has demonstrated that such novel approach can achieve good performance on the arbitrary-scale super-resolution task, their upscaled images frequently show structural distortion due to the faulty prediction on high-frequency textures. In this work, we propose UltraSR, a simple yet effective new network design based on implicit image functions in which spatial coordinates and periodic encoding are deeply integrated with the implicit neural representation. We show that spatial encoding is indeed a missing key towards the next-stage high-accuracy implicit image function through extensive experiments and ablation studies. Our UltraSR sets new state-of-the-art performance on the DIV2K benchmark under all super-resolution scales comparing to previous state-of-the-art methods. UltraSR also achieves superior performance on other standard benchmark datasets in which it outperforms prior works in almost all experiments. Our code will be released at https://github.com/SHI-Labs/UltraSR-Arbitrary-Scale-Super-Resolution.

Đối với lớp convolutional cuối cùng, nó sản xuất ra một tensor có kích thước (7x7x1024), sau đó tensor này được dàn phẳng. Synthesizing novel views of the human body from a single image presents significant challenges due to the high articulation and complex pose variations inherent in human figures. While recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated success with rigid objects, their performance diminishes when confronted with the diverse range of human body configurations. The primary limitation stems from convolutional neural networks (CNNs) struggling to effectively memorize and interpolate the extensive articulation modes present in human data. To overcome these obstacles, a new deep learning pipeline is introduced that explicitly incorporates the geometric structure of the human body. This approach combines a shape estimation network with an image generation network, utilizing a perspective transformation at their interface to produce a forward flow for accurate pixel value transportation. By decomposing the synthesis process into distinct stages, this method successfully isolates sources of data variation and simplifies the learning tasks at each step. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in rendering quality for objects with varying poses, and the technique is further validated on real-world data acquired from 3D sensors. Additionally, the generated flow enables the production of high-resolution, high-fidelity novel views, establishing the method's effectiveness for complex articulated objects.

We assess the efficacy of semi-supervised learning (SSL) on a practical benchmark characterized by significant class imbalance and the inclusion of images from novel classes. This benchmark comprises two fine-grained classification datasets derived from classes within the Aves and Fungi taxonomies. Our findings indicate that recently developed SSL techniques offer notable advantages and can effectively leverage out-of-class data to enhance performance when deep networks are trained from scratch. However, their effectiveness remains inferior to that of a transfer learning baseline, which serves as an alternative approach for learning from limited examples. Additionally, in the transfer learning context, although existing SSL methods yield some improvements, the presence of out-of-class data often has a negative impact. In this scenario, the combination of standard fine-tuning followed by distillation-based self-training emerges as the most reliable approach. Our study implies that applying semi-supervised learning with domain experts on realistic datasets might necessitate strategies that differ from those commonly found in current literature.

The paragraph discusses the strategy of building domain adapter models for machine translation, emphasizing their ability to leverage domain-specific knowledge to achieve expert-like performance without increasing model complexity. It also highlights the challenge of resource demands, particularly memory usage, when employing model distillation techniques that require multiple teacher models.

Developing a domain adapter model for English-Vietnamese machine translation presents a promising approach to address the heterogeneous nature of domain-specific data. By directing the model towards a particular domain, the goal is to harness domain knowledge to train a single, fixed-capacity system that can approximate the performance of expert models across various domains (see Table 3.5). This objective is particularly relevant for user-facing machine translation (MT) systems, which require high translation quality within each domain without sacrificing overall system simplicity or increasing computational complexity. However, a significant limitation of employing distillation techniques in this context is the necessity for a well-qualified teacher model, which can lead to substantial memory consumption and a proliferation of parameters, as noted in previous studies such as [Smith et al., 2022]. Furthermore, when multiple teacher models are utilized, memory requirements increase linearly with their number, thereby intensifying resource consumption and presenting a practical challenge for scalable deployment, as demonstrated in related works [Johnson et al., 2021]. The present research contributes to this field by proposing methods to mitigate these resource constraints while maintaining high translation quality across diverse domains.

We propose a framework that initiates visual representation learning by leveraging a basic visual grouping mechanism. This grouping process is implemented using a contour detector that segments an image into regions, which are then merged into a hierarchical tree structure. Training this grouping primitive requires only a small amount of supervised data. Once trained, we apply it across a large collection of unlabeled images to automatically infer hierarchical region structures. These inferred structures guide self-supervised contrastive feature learning, where a deep network is trained to generate per-pixel embeddings such that the distances between embeddings reflect the hierarchy of regions. Our experiments show that this method achieves state-of-the-art results in generic pre-training and improves performance on downstream tasks. We also investigate its utility in semantic region search and object instance tracking in videos.

Handling missing data is a fundamental challenge in machine learning, with zero imputation—a method that simply replaces missing entries with zero—being one of the most common yet suboptimal solutions due to often degraded neural network performance. This paper introduces the variable sparsity problem (VSP), a phenomenon where model outputs fluctuate significantly depending on the input's missingness rate, and demonstrates that VSP adversely affects predictive accuracy. Through theoretical analysis, the authors propose Sparsity Normalization (SN), a straightforward technique designed to directly address and mitigate VSP. Experimental validation across diverse benchmark datasets confirms that SN effectively debiases input-level sparsity, leading to improved model performance and more stable training. These findings not only clarify the pitfalls of zero imputation but also suggest new directions for future research in robust learning with incomplete data.
