The passage emphasizes the importance of decentralizing platforms to empower content creators, journalists, and activists by allowing them to produce and share content without the fear of censorship. The proposed solution, decentralization, is suggested to be applicable to various information-sharing platforms such as social media, news outlets, and file-sharing services. The main contribution of this thesis is the advocacy for a decentralized approach to platform management, which could potentially enhance freedom of expression and reduce the risk of content removal.

This thesis posits that the decentralization of platforms is a crucial solution for empowering content creators, journalists, and activists. By adopting a decentralized framework, these individuals can engage in content creation and expression without the looming threat of their materials being censored or removed. The approach proposed in this research is not limited to a single domain but extends to various platforms that facilitate information sharing, including social media, news services, and file-sharing networks. The primary contribution of this thesis lies in its advocacy for decentralization as a means to bolster freedom of expression and mitigate the challenges associated with content suppression. By implementing decentralized systems, platforms can ensure more secure and autonomous operations, ultimately benefiting users who rely on these platforms for communication and dissemination of information.

This paper addresses the challenge of text detection in natural scenes, moving beyond traditional word bounding box regression to focus on character-level detection and the critical task of linking adjacent characters. Motivated by the limitations of existing methods in handling spatially separated and arbitrarily oriented characters, the authors introduce a novel Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture capable of learning both node and edge features, surpassing the capabilities of typical GNNs that only learn node features. The proposed approach leverages the inherent strength of GNNs in link prediction, effectively connecting characters regardless of their spatial arrangement or orientation. Experimental results on the widely used SynthText dataset demonstrate that this method achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques, highlighting its effectiveness. The implications for future research include the potential for further improving scene text detection by exploring more advanced GNN architectures and expanding the approach to other datasets and multilingual scenarios. Black box machine learning models are widely used in high-stakes decision-making across healthcare, criminal justice, and other domains, leading to significant problems. While methods to explain these black box models have been proposed, relying on explanations instead of developing inherently interpretable models risks perpetuating poor practices and causing societal harm. This manuscript highlights the critical distinction between explaining black boxes and using inherently interpretable models, outlines key reasons to avoid explainable black boxes in high-stakes contexts, identifies challenges in interpretable machine learning, and presents example applications where interpretable models could replace black boxes in criminal justice, healthcare, and computer vision.

Designing convolutional neural networks (CNN) for mobile devices presents the challenge of achieving models that are small, fast, and accurate, a balance difficult to reach manually due to the vast architectural possibilities. This paper introduces an automated mobile neural architecture search (MNAS) approach that explicitly incorporates real-world model latency into the main optimization objective, enabling the search to identify models offering an optimal trade-off between accuracy and latency. Unlike prior work that relies on indirect proxies such as FLOPS, our method directly measures inference latency by executing candidate models on mobile phones. To balance flexibility and search space size, we propose a novel factorized hierarchical search space, promoting layer diversity across the network. Experimental results demonstrate our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art mobile CNNs on multiple vision tasks. Specifically, on the ImageNet classification task, our MnasNet achieves 75.2% top-1 accuracy with 78ms latency on a Pixel phone, making it 1.8x faster than MobileNetV2 [29] with 0.5% higher accuracy and 2.3x faster than NASNet [36] with 1.2% higher accuracy. Additionally, MnasNet yields superior mAP quality compared to MobileNets for COCO object detection. Code is at https://github.com/tensorflow/tpu/tree/master/models/official/mnasnet. (Word count: 217)

Recent advances in self-supervised learning (SSL) have closed the performance gap with supervised ImageNet pretraining, but their effectiveness remains limited when applied to larger, uncurated image datasets, likely because current SSL methods work best on iconic images and underperform on complex scenes containing multiple objects. This paper analyzes contrastive SSL methods and finds that they exhibit poor visual grounding and receive insufficient supervisory signals when trained on scene images. To address these shortcomings, the authors propose Contrastive Attention-Supervised Tuning (CAST), which leverages unsupervised saliency maps for intelligent crop sampling and employs Grad-CAM attention loss to provide grounding supervision. Experimental results on the COCO dataset demonstrate that CAST substantially improves the quality of features learned by SSL methods on scene images and enhances model robustness to background variations, suggesting promising directions for future research in improving SSL for real-world, complex visual environments. (153 words)

Anomaly detection in images is critical for a range of industrial and medical applications, notably in fields such as quality assurance and disease diagnosis. Manual inspection is often inefficient and prone to error, especially over extended periods, which highlights the need for automated solutions. Deep learning approaches, particularly artificial neural networks, have demonstrated superior performance over humans in repetitive image analysis tasks. This study explores various deep learning techniques for image-based anomaly detection within a quality assurance context, employing the MVTec anomaly dataset. Three distinct models were developed: a convolutional neural network (CNN) for supervised anomaly detection, a knowledge distillation convolutional autoencoder (KD-CAE) for unsupervised anomaly detection, a noise-induced convolutional autoencoder (NI-CAE), and a deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) for image reconstruction and data augmentation. Experimental results indicate that KD-CAE outperforms the other models on the majority of anomaly datasets, with NI-CAE excelling specifically on the Transistor dataset. While DCGAN was utilized for generating synthetic images, computational constraints limited its application. Overparameterization in deep networks—training with more parameters than data points—has been empirically shown to improve both large and lightweight models, specifically through its advantages for model pruning and sparsification. Motivated by these findings, this paper provides a theoretical characterization of the high-dimensional asymptotics of model pruning in the overparameterized regime, addressing the core question: "should one train a small model from the beginning, or first train a large model and then prune?". The analysis reveals regimes where, even with knowledge of the most informative features, training a large model followed by pruning outperforms direct training on the informative features. This mechanism gives rise to a new form of double descent in sparse model training: increasing model size while maintaining target sparsity improves test accuracy beyond the overparameterization threshold. Furthermore, the benefit of retraining after pruning is linked to feature correlations. These phenomena are demonstrated not only theoretically in linear and random-feature models but also numerically for neural networks. The technical contributions expand the high-dimensional analysis toolkit by precisely characterizing the asymptotic distribution of overparameterized least-squares, providing valuable intuition for future research in neural network optimization and model selection. Cryptocurrency wallets are designed to securely store private keys, enabling users to access, control, and manage their cryptocurrency funds. They typically provide tools such as address book administration, transaction history, and real-time market data for comprehensive account management. Implementing industry standards like the BIP39 specification ensures that mnemonic phrases or seed phrases are generated and managed in a standardized, human-readable form, allowing for consistent wallet backup and restoration processes. Self-supervised representation learning has garnered significant attention due to its ability to extract meaningful features from unlabeled data, particularly in computer vision applications where annotated datasets are scarce. Augmentation-based contrastive learning, a prominent paradigm in this field, has demonstrated impressive results but remains constrained by substantial memory requirements and untapped potential for performance gains. A novel method, termed AAG, introduces an auxiliary augmentation strategy coupled with a newly designed GNT-Xent loss function to address these limitations. The auxiliary augmentation increases image diversity, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of contrastive learning, while the GNT-Xent loss ensures stable and accelerated model convergence. Empirical evaluations on standard benchmarks, including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and SVHN, reveal that AAG consistently outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches. Notably, on the CIFAR10 dataset, AAG attains a top-1 accuracy of 94.5% with a batch size of 64, surpassing the previous best result obtained by SimCLR with a much larger batch size. These findings underscore the potential of AAG to advance the efficiency and accuracy of self-supervised representation learning in practical, resource-constrained settings.

Recent advancements in Natural Language Processing (NLP) have demonstrated machine capabilities exceeding human performance in various tasks, notably Question Answering (QA). However, domains such as Nuclear and Atomic energy remain underexplored, particularly in utilizing non-annotated data for practical applications. Addressing the scarcity of domain-specific datasets, a new dataset was compiled from 7000 research papers focused on the nuclear field. This study introduces the Nuclear Bidirectional Encoder Representational Transformers (NukeBERT), an innovative model designed to enhance BERT's vocabulary for applications with limited training data. The model's efficacy was tested using the Nuclear Question Answering Dataset (NQuAD), comprising 612 questions generated from 181 paragraphs randomly selected from the IGCAR research corpus. NukeBERT demonstrated superior performance compared to traditional BERT models, validating the novel approach. Despite its computational demands, the pretrained weights of NukeBERT and the NQuAD dataset will be made publicly accessible to encourage further exploration and development within the nuclear domain. This research marks a significant step toward leveraging NLP for advanced applications in nuclear science, fostering an understanding of complex domain-specific knowledge.

Những kết quả này cho thấy vật liệu ZnPc pha β có những đặc tính lý hóa ưu việt, phù hợp cho ứng dụng trong các thiết bị quang điện, cảm biến và nghiên cứu năng lượng mặt trời.

Delay-based netcode expands upon the classic lockstep model, where game progress pauses until all inputs are gathered, commonly used in turn-based games due to their strategic nature. This approach introduces input latency, creating a delay between inputs and actions to ensure synchronization across players' local game versions. This combination, known as delay-based networking, has been employed in games like "Age of Empires" and requires minimal modifications to the core game loop. However, it compromises responsiveness and flexibility, as latency spikes or variances can cause prolonged pauses in gameplay.

Delay-based netcode represents an evolution of the traditional lockstep model, wherein game progression is temporarily halted until all player inputs are collected. This model is particularly effective in turn-based games, where strategic decision-making necessitates a brief pause, rendering a half-second delay virtually imperceptible. To adeptly implement lockstep netcode in fighting games, input latency is introduced. This latency engenders a deliberate delay between player inputs and their corresponding in-game actions, guaranteeing that both players have received each other's inputs before game simulations advance. The synchronization achieved across local game versions is the hallmark of delay-based networking, a methodology long employed in video games such as "Age of Empires." Developers benefit from the simplicity of implementing delay-based networking, as it necessitates minimal or no modifications to the game's core loop. Nevertheless, this approach entails trade-offs in terms of responsiveness and flexibility. Specifically, in scenarios of latency spikes or fluctuations due to suboptimal connections, gameplay may experience significant pauses until all inputs are received.

Deep learning models generally require large amounts of labeled data for training. However, obtaining additional data can be costly or unfeasible for many real-world problems. To address this, we introduce semi-supervised deep kernel learning (SSDKL), a semi-supervised regression model that minimizes predictive variance within the posterior regularization framework. SSDKL integrates the hierarchical representation learning power of neural networks with the probabilistic modeling strengths of Gaussian processes. By effectively utilizing unlabeled data, we demonstrate improved performance across a variety of real-world regression tasks compared to supervised deep kernel learning and semi-supervised approaches like VAT and mean teacher adapted for regression.

Effective inventory rotation in logistics warehouses utilizing RFID technology requires the systematic storage of RFID card code information corresponding to each product or goods entry within the system to enable accurate comparison and management. Despite inherent limitations in directly accessing or retrieving comprehensive item information from RFID tags due to tag storage constraints, the reusable nature of RFID cards allows for their continued deployment across multiple inventory cycles. To address management challenges, it is essential to develop robust tools capable of handling the management, search, tracking, and retrieval of data linked to each RFID tag, as well as monitoring the operational status and usage history of each tag. This approach ensures streamlined inventory oversight and enhances the reliability of automated inventory systems in logistics environments.

Một trong những vấn đề của phương pháp San bằng số mũ đơn giản (Simple Exponential Smoothing) là khi mô hình chuỗi thời gian thay đổi theo thời gian, hệ số tùy chọn cố định sẽ không còn phù hợp với mô hình hiện tại, dẫn đến sai số dự báo gia tăng. Để giải quyết vấn đề này, phương pháp San bằng số mũ với hệ số tùy chọn thích ứng được sử dụng nhằm điều chỉnh hệ số tùy chọn dựa trên dữ liệu quá khứ, từ đó phù hợp hơn với mô hình chuỗi thời gian hiện tại. Cụ thể, hệ số tùy chọn được tính toán dựa trên một công thức có chứa một tham số thay đổi theo thời gian, cho phép nó thích nghi với sự biến đổi của chuỗi thời gian. Điều này giúp giảm thiểu sai số dự báo, đặc biệt khi mô hình chuỗi thời gian có sự thay đổi theo thời gian. Một số nghiên cứu đã chứng minh hiệu quả của phương pháp này. Ví dụ, một nghiên cứu được công bố trên tạp chí "International Journal of Forecasting" năm 2008 cho thấy rằng San bằng số mũ với hệ số tùy chọn thích ứng có thể cải thiện độ chính xác của phương pháp San bằng số mũ lên đến 20%.

Siêu âm phổi giữ vai trò quan trọng trong chẩn đoán sớm và phân loại viêm phổi do Covid-19, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh số ca nhiễm tăng nhanh gây quá tải tại các khoa cấp cứu. Mặc dù chụp cắt lớp vi tính ngực được xem là tiêu chuẩn vàng để phát hiện sớm tổn thương phổi ở bệnh nhân Covid-19, nhưng phương pháp này có nhiều hạn chế như thiếu tính linh hoạt, khó thực hiện tại chỗ, tiềm ẩn nguy cơ lây nhiễm chéo do di chuyển bệnh nhân và liên quan tới nhiễm xạ. Phương pháp này còn giúp bác sĩ đánh giá chính xác mức độ tổn thương, phân biệt các kiểu hình hội chứng nguy kịch hô hấp cấp để lựa chọn liệu pháp cung cấp oxy và thông khí phù hợp, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị và giảm thiểu nguy cơ quá tải hệ thống y tế.

The main idea of the paragraph is to explain the concept of cross-entropy, particularly its role as a loss function in machine learning and information theory, and its application in classification tasks such as image recognition and natural language processing. Cross-entropy is a fundamental concept in machine learning and information theory, quantifying the divergence between two probability distributions. In the context of classification problems, including those in image recognition and natural language processing, cross-entropy serves as a widely adopted loss function. Its primary function is to evaluate the discrepancy between the predicted probability distribution generated by a model and the actual, or true, probability distribution of class labels. By minimizing cross-entropy loss during model training, algorithms are able to improve their predictive accuracy, thereby enhancing performance in various classification tasks (see Figure 1). This approach is foundational in contemporary deep learning frameworks and has been extensively validated in related works, underscoring its significance in the design and analysis of software for weld quality assessment using image processing and segmentation deep learning techniques.

The main idea of this paragraph is that Activities in Android applications with unrestricted Intent Filters, such as those accepting any URL or providing overly permissive path support, are susceptible to vulnerabilities from arbitrary external input. 

Activities configured with unrestricted Intent Filters—particularly those that accept any URL or utilize excessively permissive path patterns—present significant security risks by exposing the application to arbitrary external input. This vulnerability can be exploited by malicious actors to trigger unintended behaviors or gain unauthorized access to application components, as discussed in prior research on Android security (Enck et al., 2011; Chin et al., 2011). The contribution of this work lies in systematically identifying and categorizing such dangerous Intent Filter configurations, highlighted in Table 3.5, thereby providing a foundation for the automated detection and mitigation of these vulnerabilities in Android malware scanning frameworks.

This study addresses the performance limitations of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and the constraints on increasing their depth, which are often attributed to intrinsic limitations of GCN layers such as insufficient expressive power. Contrary to this belief, we demonstrate that it is feasible to reduce training difficulties and enhance performance by solely altering the training procedure, without modifying the network architecture. We identify the training challenges of GCNs through an analysis of graph signal energy loss, noting that energy loss during the backward pass undermines the learning of layers proximal to the input. To alleviate these training challenges, we propose modifications to the GCN operator based on energy considerations. Empirical validation confirms that these operator adjustments significantly reduce training difficulties and boost performance, without altering parameter composition. Thus, we conclude that the primary issue lies in training difficulties rather than the inherent limitations of GCN layers.

This paper introduces a novel locally statistical active contour model (ACM) for image segmentation addressing the challenge of intensity inhomogeneity. The motivation stems from the need to accurately segment inhomogeneous objects, which are modeled as Gaussian distributions with varying means and variances. The approach employs a moving window to remap the original image into a new domain, enhancing the separability of Gaussian-distributed inhomogeneous object intensities. In this transformed domain, the means of the Gaussian distributions are adaptively estimated by multiplying a bias field with the original signal within the window. A statistical energy functional is formulated for each local region, integrating the bias field, the level set function, and a constant that approximates the true signal of the respective object. Experimental results on both synthetic and real images demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art and representative segmentation methods, implying its potential for improved segmentation in future research involving images with intensity inhomogeneity.

This paper addresses the limitations of the traditional reinforcement learning paradigm in modeling lifelong reinforcement learning systems, which learn through trial-and-error interactions with their environment over extended periods. The motivation stems from the need for learning systems capable of continuous adaptation and knowledge accumulation throughout their operational lifetime. The author presents arguments highlighting the shortcomings of conventional reinforcement learning approaches in capturing the essence of lifelong learning. To provide further insight, the paper discusses key characteristics of lifelong reinforcement learning and introduces a simplistic prototype lifelong reinforcement learning system as a proof of concept. The results suggest that more sophisticated frameworks are necessary for true lifelong learning capabilities. This work lays the groundwork for future research focused on developing reinforcement learning systems that can learn, adapt, and retain knowledge over a lifetime, with potential implications for the advancement of artificial intelligence and autonomous agents. In the era of big data, enhancing memory and computational efficiency is essential for deploying technologies effectively. Hashing, particularly spectral hashing, is a powerful tool for overcoming big data's computational challenges. However, the binary constraints in spectral hashing make optimization difficult. Existing relaxation methods introduce auxiliary variables to obtain high-quality binary codes, leading to increased computational complexity. This paper challenges the necessity of these variables by proposing a novel relaxed formulation for spectral hashing that avoids additional variables. Instead of operating in the original data space, the problem is solved in a smaller space, reducing memory and computational demands. The binary codes are then derived from this solution. Two optimization techniques, projected gradient and optimization on manifold, are employed to achieve the solution. Experiments on four public datasets demonstrate that the proposed efficient spectral hashing (ESH) algorithm provides competitive retrieval performance with lower complexity compared to state-of-the-art methods. These findings suggest that this approach can significantly influence future research in big data hashing methods by offering a more efficient alternative without sacrificing performance.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology for information storage and transmission, introduced by Satoshi Nakamoto in 2008. It is designed to securely confirm and store transactions and information. A blockchain is essentially a series of data blocks that are interconnected through encryption and arithmetic algorithms, thereby ensuring the integrity of the data. Each individual block holds details about transactions conducted on the network, along with a hash code that links to the preceding block. This hash code is critical as it validates the integrity of the subsequent block in the chain. The decentralized nature of blockchain means that data is stored across numerous nodes in the network, without a centralized control point, thereby preventing unauthorized tampering or modification of the information. Consequently, blockchain technology has significant utility across various sectors, including finance, healthcare, and supply chain management. Potential applications of blockchain encompass numerous domains, demonstrating its versatility and transformative potential.

Hệ thống thủy lợi Quản Lộ - Phụng Hiệp đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc cấp nước phục vụ sản xuất cho các tỉnh Bạc Liêu, Sóc Trăng, Cà Mau, Kiên Giang và Hậu Giang thuộc Đồng bằng Sông Cửu Long. Trong giai đoạn 2015-2022, chất lượng nước tại hệ thống này có xu hướng suy giảm với biểu hiện rõ nét là sự gia tăng ô nhiễm phèn sắt tại nhiều cống như cầu Sập, Vĩnh Mỹ, Láng Trâm, Cà Mau và Đá, cùng với sự sụt giảm lượng phù sa, tăng ô nhiễm hữu cơ và dinh dưỡng ở tất cả các điểm lấy mẫu. Tuy nhiên, mức độ ô nhiễm vi sinh lại có dấu hiệu giảm tại khu vực này. Phân tích mối quan hệ giữa độ mặn và các chỉ tiêu chất lượng nước cho thấy độ mặn ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến các thông số như pH, oxy hòa tan, nhu cầu oxy hóa học, amoni và sắt, đồng thời có tác động qua lại với photphat nhưng không liên quan đến tổng chất rắn lơ lửng, nitrat, nitrit và Coliform. Kết quả này nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của việc tăng cường giám sát và quản lý nhằm bảo vệ nguồn nước phục vụ phát triển kinh tế - xã hội khu vực.

Trong bài toán hiện tại, môi trường được xây dựng dưới dạng một mô phỏng ngã tư đơn giản với bốn hướng đi, mỗi hướng bao gồm hai làn đường. Khoảng cách giữa các lần ra quyết định của agent được cố định là 5 giây nhằm làm rõ ý nghĩa của từng hành động. Nếu tần suất ra quyết định quá cao, chẳng hạn như 50 lần mỗi giây, thì mỗi hành động riêng lẻ sẽ trở nên không đáng kể, buộc agent phải lặp lại nhiều lần để duy trì một pha đèn xanh hoặc đèn đỏ liên tục, từ đó gây khó khăn cho quá trình học hỏi. Trước mỗi lần đưa ra quyết định, agent tiếp nhận trạng thái của môi trường, được biểu diễn thông qua dữ liệu từ các cảm biến đặt trên đường. Các cảm biến này trả về giá trị 1 nếu phát hiện có xe đang dừng và 0 nếu không có xe. Bên cạnh đó, tổng thời gian dừng tích lũy của các phương tiện trong vòng 5 giây trước đó được sử dụng làm điểm thưởng (reward) cho agent đối với hành động vừa thực hiện. Cách tiếp cận này cho phép đánh giá hiệu quả của từng quyết định dựa trên mức độ giảm thiểu thời gian chờ đợi của các phương tiện tại ngã tư, qua đó hỗ trợ quá trình học tăng cường của agent trở nên hiệu quả và thực tế hơn.

Supervised learning applied to molecular data holds significant promise for advancing chemistry, drug discovery, and materials science. Fortunately, several related neural network models that are invariant to molecular symmetries have been documented in the literature. These models employ a message passing algorithm alongside an aggregation procedure to compute a function over the entire input graph. The subsequent step involves identifying an especially effective variant of this general methodology and applying it to chemical prediction benchmarks until such benchmarks are either resolved or the limitations of the approach are reached. In this study, we unify existing models within a common framework termed Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) and investigate further novel variations within this framework. Utilizing MPNNs, we achieve state-of-the-art performance on a key molecular property prediction benchmark; these results are sufficiently robust to suggest that future research should concentrate on datasets featuring larger molecules or more precise ground truth labels.

Machine learning, particularly deep learning, is significantly transforming approaches to optical thin-film inverse design. Most existing studies have concentrated on optimizing parameters such as layer thickness and structural dimensions in optical thin-films. However, automating the material search process remains a challenging issue. In this work, we introduce a novel end-to-end algorithm for inverse design of optical thin-films. Our approach integrates unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning (RL), and a genetic algorithm to enable fully automated design of optical thin-films, eliminating the need for human intervention. Additionally, through several specific examples, we demonstrate how this method can be utilized to optimize the spectral performance of a multi-layer solar absorber device.

A blockchain is a chain of connected blocks secured by cryptographic proofs, functioning as a decentralized ledger in a distributed system. This means that multiple copies of the ledger exist, preventing any single entity from having sole control. Each participant in the blockchain network maintains an electronic copy of the blockchain data, which is updated and synchronized with the latest transactions.

Phần đầu sử dụng mạng VGG với cấu trúc đơn giản, phù hợp cho xử lý ảnh kích thước nhỏ. Phần tiếp theo áp dụng mô hình sequence to sequence (seq2seq).

Đoạn văn trình bày khái niệm topic taxonomy như một nhánh cụ thể của taxonomy, nhấn mạnh vai trò của topic taxonomy trong việc tổ chức chủ đề theo cấu trúc phân cấp, đồng thời điểm qua hai phương pháp xây dựng taxonomy là thủ công và tự động. Đoạn văn cũng nêu bật những thách thức của phương pháp thủ công, lợi ích của phương pháp tự động, và đóng góp của nghiên cứu hiện tại là ứng dụng thuật toán NetTaxo để tự động xây dựng topic taxonomy trong lĩnh vực khoa học máy tính và kinh tế, qua đó hỗ trợ xây dựng Ontology phục vụ hệ thống quản lý thông tin chuyên gia.

Topic taxonomy được xem là một nhánh hoặc một ứng dụng cụ thể của taxonomy, đóng vai trò là hệ thống phân loại các chủ đề hoặc lĩnh vực trong một ngữ cảnh xác định nhằm tổ chức chủ đề theo cấu trúc hệ thống và tạo nên bản phân cấp rõ ràng. Mỗi nút trong taxonomy chủ đề đại diện cho một chủ đề nền tảng, được định nghĩa như một cụm các thuật ngữ có tính nhất quán về mặt ngữ nghĩa. Một topic taxonomy chất lượng cao đem lại nhiều lợi ích thực tiễn cho các ứng dụng như tìm kiếm và lập chỉ mục, đề xuất nội dung cá nhân hóa, cũng như trả lời câu hỏi. Quá trình xây dựng taxonomy chủ đề, còn gọi là topic taxonomy construction, hiện nay chủ yếu theo hai hướng: xây dựng thủ công và xây dựng tự động. Phương pháp thủ công đòi hỏi các chuyên gia trong từng lĩnh vực trực tiếp phân loại và tạo cấu trúc phân cấp cho các thuật ngữ, dẫn đến việc tiêu tốn nhiều thời gian và nguồn lực, đặc biệt khi quy mô lĩnh vực rộng lớn và thông tin liên tục cập nhật. Hơn nữa, mỗi lĩnh vực lại đòi hỏi chuyên môn sâu để đảm bảo chất lượng taxonomy, khiến việc huy động đủ chuyên gia là một thách thức lớn. Để khắc phục hạn chế này, hướng tiếp cận xây dựng taxonomy tự động bằng các phương pháp máy tính được nghiên cứu và ứng dụng nhằm bổ trợ hoặc thay thế cho phương pháp thủ công. Trong phạm vi đồ án này, nghiên cứu tập trung vào việc xây dựng topic taxonomy cho một lĩnh vực cụ thể bằng cách ứng dụng các kỹ thuật học máy. Trọng tâm là nghiên cứu và triển khai thuật toán NetTaxo nhằm tự động xây dựng taxonomy các thuật ngữ phân cấp dựa trên Text-rich Network với dữ liệu được trích xuất từ các bài báo trên Internet thuộc lĩnh vực khoa học máy tính và kinh tế, kết hợp với siêu dữ liệu liên quan. Kết quả taxonomy thu được sẽ được sử dụng làm nền tảng để xây dựng Ontology lĩnh vực phục vụ cho hệ thống quản lý thông tin của các chuyên gia.
Em đã nghiên cứu kỹ lưỡng nhiều nguồn tài liệu cũng như kinh nghiệm thực tiễn từ những người sáng lập các website từ thiện về các hình thức quyên góp thông qua chuyển khoản.

Adaptive normalization of learning targets addresses a fundamental challenge in value-based reinforcement learning, where the scale of value approximations may fluctuate as the agent’s policy evolves. Conventional learning algorithms often lack invariance to changes in target magnitude, making them sensitive to the absolute values encountered during training. This issue is exemplified in prior research on learning to play Atari games, where reward signals are typically clipped to a fixed range to standardize learning dynamics across diverse environments. While reward clipping enables the application of a single algorithm to multiple games, it introduces heuristic constraints that can alter the qualitative behavior of agents and potentially obscure true differences among tasks. Implementing adaptive normalization allows learning algorithms to automatically adjust to the evolving scale of targets, eliminating the need for manual reward clipping and domain-specific heuristics. Such normalization not only preserves the generality and robustness of the learning process but also maintains or enhances overall performance, providing a principled approach to scaling challenges in reinforcement learning across varied tasks and environments.

Bài báo nghiên cứu các yếu tố nguy cơ tử vong ở bệnh nhân xơ gan bị xuất huyết tiêu hóa trên do tăng áp lực tĩnh mạch cửa tại Việt Nam, với tỷ lệ tử vong cao từ 12 - 20%. Nghiên cứu này nhằm xác định tỷ lệ tử vong và các yếu tố nguy cơ trong vòng 3 ngày và 7 ngày sau khi nhập viện. Thực hiện nghiên cứu đoàn hệ tiến cứu với các biến độc lập như tuổi, nguyên nhân xơ gan, sốc, và các chỉ số xét nghiệm khác trên bệnh nhân nhập viện từ 06/2018 - 04/2019. Kết quả cho thấy tỷ lệ tử vong trong vòng 3 ngày và 7 ngày lần lượt là 6,38% và 13,83%. Các yếu tố nguy cơ tử vong trong vòng 3 ngày bao gồm sốc và điểm MELD - Na ≥ 25, trong khi các yếu tố nguy cơ trong vòng 7 ngày bao gồm sốc, rối loạn tri giác, báng bụng trung bình đến nhiều, và điểm Child - Turcotte - Pugh ≥ 12. MELD - Na có giá trị tiên lượng tử vong trong vòng 3 ngày, trong khi Child - Turcotte - Pugh tiên lượng tử vong trong vòng 7 ngày. Những phát hiện này cung cấp cơ sở cho các nghiên cứu trong tương lai nhằm cải thiện hiệu quả điều trị và tiên lượng cho bệnh nhân xơ gan bị xuất huyết tiêu hóa trên.

The main idea of the paragraph is the exploration of Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) for Semantic Segmentation, which is challenging due to the need for large amounts of labeled data. The study utilizes synthetic images from the game Grand Theft Auto V as training data to improve model performance on the Cityscapes dataset, which lacks accessible labels in the UDA setup. This work advances the field by leveraging synthetic images to address the challenge of acquiring labeled data in UDA tasks.

Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) possesses significant potential, particularly in tasks requiring substantial amounts of labeled images, which are often difficult to obtain. This research focuses on UDA for Semantic Segmentation, a task that typically demands large datasets with pixel-wise annotations. To address this challenge, synthetic images are utilized, which are readily accessible and easy to produce. Specifically, images depicting urban scenes are sourced from the realistically generated computer game Grand Theft Auto V, serving as the training domain source data. The primary goal of this project is to enhance the performance of model M on the real-world Cityscapes dataset. This dataset comprises images of urban environments captured across 50 cities in Germany and its neighboring countries. It is important to note that within the UDA configuration, the labels for the Cityscapes dataset are not accessible. By employing synthetic images, this work contributes to overcoming the labeling challenges inherent in UDA tasks, advancing the field of Semantic Segmentation.

Trong bối cảnh Lớp học Cầu Vồng tiếp tục duy trì và mở rộng quy mô hoạt động trong tương lai, việc chỉ dựa vào các dịch vụ như Google, cũng như các nền tảng mạng xã hội như Zalo, Facebook để quản lý công việc đã bộc lộ nhiều hạn chế, đặc biệt là trong khâu tổ chức, sắp xếp nhân sự và phân bổ lịch giảng dạy cho ban quản lý cũng như các tình nguyện viên. Những công cụ này không được thiết kế chuyên biệt cho nhu cầu quản lý tổ chức phi lợi nhuận, dẫn đến tình trạng thiếu hiệu quả, tốn thời gian và khó kiểm soát, nhất là khi quy mô tổ chức ngày càng lớn. Đây chính là lý do và động lực để em thực hiện đề tài "Hệ thống quản lý dạy học và nhân sự cho Lớp học Cầu Vồng", với mục tiêu hỗ trợ tổ chức vận hành hiệu quả hơn trong giai đoạn phát triển sắp tới.

Algorithm 1, named Entity Pyramid Sentence Selection, is a method for selecting sentences from a document cluster based on the frequency of entities. The process involves sorting entities by descending frequency, identifying candidate sentences that contain the top entities, and using a sentence Score function to rank and select the most important sentences. The algorithm outputs a list of selected sentences, and the sentence score is used to determine sentence importance within the cluster.

Algorithm 1, Entity Pyramid Sentence Selection, operates by taking a document cluster and a list of entities with frequency greater than one as input. It sorts these entities by frequency in descending order, then iteratively identifies all sentences in the cluster containing each top entity. Among these candidate sentences, it selects the one with the highest Score, appending it to the output list of sentences to mask. The process continues until the desired number of sentences is selected. Sentence importance across the cluster is determined using this sentence score.

This paper addresses the limitation of machine learning applications to satellite imagery that depend on visible images and thus lack data during nighttime. To overcome this, the study explores the use of available infra-red observations to generate visible images. Leveraging U-Net based deep learning architectures, the proposed methods demonstrate promising performance, achieving a structural similarity index (SSIM) of up to 86\% on an independent test set and generating visually convincing output images from infra-red data. Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for identifying significant computational paths within randomly wired neural networks prior to training, aiming to enhance efficiency and performance. The method involves pruning the computational graph using a node mass probability function, informed by local graph measures and modulated by hyperparameters generated from a reinforcement learning-based controller neural network. By applying Ricci curvature, edges deemed of low importance are eliminated before constructing the neural network, resulting in a notable reduction of nearly 35% in FLOPs per pass without compromising performance. The approach not only effectively regularizes networks based on structural properties but also demonstrates that favorable traits in one network can be generalized to others. Compared to traditional pruning methods focusing on low-magnitude weights, this technique yields superior network performance under similar compression levels. This study marks the first exploration of pruning randomly wired neural networks and the inaugural use of Ricci curvature as a topological measure in pruning, paving the way for future research in network optimization and topology-based pruning methods.

Class Expert Generative Adversarial Network (CE-GAN) for Imbalance Data Classification

Imbalanced data classification presents significant challenges to conventional artificial intelligence algorithms, as these models often struggle to accurately recognize minority class samples within skewed datasets. Traditional approaches typically involve modifying existing algorithms under the assumption that the training data is imbalanced; however, such alterations can lead to suboptimal outcomes when applied to balanced datasets. The class expert generative adversarial network (CE-GAN) addresses this limitation by introducing a specialized deep learning architecture that does not presuppose data imbalance. CE-GAN operates by incorporating dedicated class experts within the generative adversarial network framework, enabling the model to learn distinguishing features of each class in greater detail prior to the classification phase. This enhanced representation facilitates improved discrimination between minority and majority classes, thereby mitigating the impact of data imbalance. Empirical results demonstrate that CE-GAN achieves superior performance in imbalanced data classification tasks, highlighting its potential as a robust and versatile solution for real-world applications where class distribution is inherently skewed.

Cross-modal learning with pairwise constraints seeks to uncover shared semantic structures between different modalities, such as text and image components within web documents. Addressing the challenge of integrating information from these diverse sources, a compound regularization framework is introduced to effectively manage pairwise constraints and serve as a versatile foundation for cross-modal algorithm development. For unsupervised scenarios, a cross-modal subspace clustering technique is developed to identify underlying commonalities across modalities, while in supervised settings, a cross-modal matching method incorporating compound ℓ21 regularization and an iteratively reweighted optimization algorithm is proposed to mitigate the effects of semantic discrepancies and outliers in the data. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that the joint modeling of text and image data, guided by semantically informed pairwise constraints, significantly narrows the semantic gap between modalities and enhances the performance of clustering and retrieval tasks. These findings underscore the efficacy of the proposed approaches in advancing the accuracy and robustness of cross-modal learning systems.

Early unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) methods achieve domain-invariant feature representation by leveraging the early layers of neural networks, often using adversarial learning to minimize domain differences. Initial feature alignment approaches focus on reducing discrepancies between source and target domains. Hoffman was the first to incorporate domain adaptation (DA) into segmentation by integrating feature alignment with additional category constraints. Various adversarial learning strategies have been proposed to learn domain-invariant features across input, feature, output, or patch space adaptations. For example, Tsai et al. treat segmentation as structured outputs, emphasizing semantic similarity across domains, while Wang et al. enhance discriminator performance by incorporating class information to align features more precisely.

Early unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) techniques generate domain-invariant feature representations by utilizing the neural network’s early layers, facilitated by adversarial learning that reduces domain discrepancies. Hoffman first introduced domain adaptation (DA) into segmentation by considering feature alignment with additional category constraints. Learning domain-invariant features involves various adversarial learning approaches spanning input, feature, output, or patch space adaptations. For instance, Tsai et al. view segmentation as structured outputs, where images from different domains share significant semantic similarity, and Wang et al. incorporate class information into the discriminator to achieve finer feature alignment.

This paper introduces a method for distinguishing foreground objects from the background in a color image. Initially, a color image of any size is processed as input. The algorithm transforms the image into a grayscale format. Subsequently, a Canny edge detector is applied to identify the boundaries of the foreground object. The method focuses on determining the maximum distance between each boundary pixel both column-wise and row-wise, filling the region enclosed by the edges. Consequently, the grayscale values of the pixels within the bounded region are extracted and the grayscale image is reconverted into the original color image containing only the foreground object.

This paper addresses the challenge of learning local discriminative representations in medical image analysis tasks such as lesion sub-type identification and detailed anatomical segmentation, where existing supervised methods demand extensive annotated datasets and unsupervised methods typically yield only global features. To overcome these limitations, we propose an unsupervised representation learning framework that incorporates local discrimination through a dual-branch model: an embedding branch that disperses dissimilar pixels across a low-dimensional hypersphere, and a clustering branch that groups similar pixels into the same cluster. These branches are trained concurrently in a mutually beneficial manner to produce representations that effectively assess local region similarity. The learned representations are transferable for enhancing various downstream tasks and can facilitate the clustering of anatomical structures in unlabeled medical images, leveraging topological priors from simulations or structurally similar entities. Experimental results on retinal and chest X-ray images demonstrate that the proposed method improves downstream performance and enables effective anatomical structure clustering, confirming its utility and effectiveness. Melanôm nguyên phát ở âm hộ - âm đạo là một bệnh lý ác tính hiếm gặp, chiếm chưa đến 10% trong tổng số các khối u ở khu vực này và có tiên lượng xấu với tỷ lệ tái phát cao trong thời gian ngắn. Ngoài việc báo cáo các trường hợp này, bài viết cũng xem xét tổng quan y văn về bệnh lý melanôm âm hộ - âm đạo, cung cấp thông tin quan trọng cho các nghiên cứu và điều trị trong tương lai.

This paragraph introduces the evaluation metrics used to assess the performance of the proposed violence detection method in surveillance cameras. It presents mathematical notations in equations (3.4) and (3.5) to describe certain vectors and matrices relevant to the method. Subsequently, it defines the confusion matrix in Table 4.1, outlining the counts of true positives (TP), false positives (FP), false negatives (FN), and true negatives (TN). Furthermore, it specifies the accuracy metric (ACC) in equation (4.1) as a quantitative measure for evaluating both the state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods and the proposed approach. These metrics serve as standard tools for performance assessment in classification tasks and provide a basis for comparative analysis.

The evaluation of the proposed violence detection framework is conducted using established performance metrics, notably the confusion matrix and accuracy measure. The notation introduced in equations (3.4) and (3.5), where \( L = O \max(O) = [O_1^{\max(O)} O_2^{\max(O)} \ldots O_n^{\max(O)}]^T \) and \( F_b = [fb_1 fb_2 \ldots fb_n]^T = O \cdot R = [o_1 \cdot r_1 \; o_2 \cdot r_2 \ldots o_n \cdot r_n]^T \), underpins the representation of feature vectors pertinent to the detection task. The confusion matrix, as detailed in Table 4.1, categorizes prediction outcomes into true positives (TP), false positives (FP), false negatives (FN), and true negatives (TN), thereby enabling a comprehensive assessment of classification performance. Accuracy (ACC), defined by equation (4.1) as \( \text{ACC} = \frac{TP + TN}{TP + FN + TN + FP} \), quantifies the overall correctness of the classification model. We propose a policy improvement algorithm for Reinforcement Learning (RL) called Rerouted Behavior Improvement (RBI), motivated by the need to address evaluation errors of the Q-function that commonly arise when learning from finite past experience data. Our approach attenuates rapid policy changes for low probability actions that have been less frequently sampled, thereby minimizing the improvement penalty associated with greedy or constrained policy optimization algorithms that ignore Q-function evaluation errors. Results from a two-armed bandit with Gaussian distributed rewards demonstrate that RBI avoids catastrophic performance degradation, reduces regret, and increases data efficiency, particularly when the optimal action has high variance. Further evaluation on two tasks in the Atari Learning Environment—learning from observations of multiple behavior policies and iterative RL—shows that RBI outperforms greedy policies and other constrained optimization algorithms, establishing it as a safer and more data-efficient learning algorithm. These findings suggest that RBI offers a promising direction for future research in safe and efficient policy improvement in batch RL settings. (163 words)

EUENO inherently encrypts data and implements robust security measures throughout all data-related processes. Users perform encryption and decryption directly via non-custodial wallet services such as OWallet. This paper addresses the challenge of autonomously learning effective sets of options in reinforcement learning, which can facilitate hierarchical task decomposition and accelerate learning and planning. The study is motivated by recent advancements in representation learning methods for guiding the option discovery process, focusing specifically on eigenoptions derived from representations that capture diffusive information flow in the environment. The authors extend existing eigenoption discovery algorithms to accommodate environments with stochastic transitions and scenarios lacking handcrafted features. A novel algorithm is proposed to discover eigenoptions by learning non-linear state representations directly from raw pixel data, leveraging developments in deep reinforcement learning and the relationship between proto-value functions and the successor representation. The approach is validated through experiments in traditional tabular domains to build intuition and in Atari 2600 games to showcase its potential. The results suggest promising directions for future research in enhancing option discovery through advanced representation learning techniques.

Một mạng Petri có thời gian là một loại mạng Petri mà mỗi chuyển tiếp trong đó đều có một khoảng thời gian hoạt động xác định. Khi một chuyển tiếp được kích hoạt, nó sẽ hoạt động sau một khoảng thời gian nhất định kể từ khi được kích hoạt. Nghiên cứu của Nsh và Tanaka đã phát triển một phương pháp để tạo ra các mạng Petri cho từng phương tiện dẫn đường tự động (AGV) và từng nhiệm vụ cụ thể. Bằng cách kết hợp các mạng Petri này lại với nhau, một mô hình có thể được xây dựng để phân công và định tuyến không xung đột. Tuy nhiên, phương pháp này khá phức tạp và tốn nhiều thời gian và không gian, do đó hiện nay nó chưa đủ nhanh để định tuyến theo thời gian thực.

Spatiotemporal forecasting is integral to intelligent transportation systems (ITS) for tasks such as route planning, navigation, and traffic management, and deep Spatiotemporal graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown strong performance in these domains by capturing both spatial and temporal dependencies. However, understanding the vulnerability and robustness of GNN-based forecasting models is crucial, as adversarial attacks can have severe real-world consequences such as manipulated traffic predictions leading to congestion or city-scale failures. Existing adversarial research on deep neural networks (DNNs) does not directly translate to spatiotemporal forecasting due to unique causal and spatiotemporal dynamics. To address this, the paper introduces the Spatially Focused Attack (SFA), which targets spatiotemporal GNNs by attacking a single vertex. The approach involves an inverse estimation to tackle causality, uses genetic algorithms with a universal attack method as the evaluation function to pinpoint the weakest vertex, and formulates an inverse estimation-based optimization problem to generate effective perturbations. Experimental results on real-world traffic datasets demonstrate that perturbations focused on one vertex can propagate across a significant portion of the graph, highlighting the need for future research into more robust spatiotemporal forecasting models and defenses against adversarial attacks.

This paragraph introduces matrix factorization collaborative filtering, emphasizing its utility in overcoming the limitations of content-based recommendation methods. The main idea is that matrix factorization eliminates the need for predefined product attribute vectors by learning product and customer representations jointly during training, thereby approximating the utility matrix Y as the product of matrices X and W.

Matrix factorization collaborative filtering is employed in this section to address several inherent limitations of content-based recommendation systems. Unlike content-based approaches, which require the predefinition of explicit vectors to represent product attributes, matrix factorization enables the simultaneous learning of product and customer representations during the training process. Specifically, this technique approximates the utility matrix Y∈RM∗N as the product of two lower-dimensional matrices: X∈RM∗K, which represents the latent feature vectors for products, and W∈RK∗N, which captures the latent feature vectors for customers. By jointly optimizing X and W, the system effectively models user preferences and product characteristics, thereby facilitating more accurate and scalable e-book recommendations. This approach not only reduces the dependency on domain-specific feature engineering but also enhances the recommendation quality, as demonstrated in related works such as Koren et al. (2009) and Hu et al. (2008). The contribution of this section lies in illustrating how matrix factorization can be systematically integrated into the development of an e-book recommendation system to yield a more flexible and effective collaborative filtering framework.

The main idea of this paragraph is the structure and function of the encoder component within a neural network model, focusing on its repetitive nature and the multi-head attention mechanism. The encoder is composed of a feed-forward section and a multi-head attention segment, with residual connections facilitating gradient flow during training. The multi-head attention mechanism processes inputs as queries, keys, and values, allowing the model to assess information relevance and similarity. This mechanism is multi-headed, permitting division into parallel chunks for diverse perspectives in mapping. The multi-head attention blocks are subsequently combined and layer normalized with the residual input.

In the context of this thesis, the encoder component is an integral part of neural network models, characterized by its ability to be identically repeated and stacked N times, with each repetition refining the encoding's precision. This component is comprised of a feed-forward section and a multi-head attention segment. Notably, residual connections—such as those that transfer the original input to the output like in the Add Norm aspect—enhance training performance by facilitating the free flow of gradients during backpropagation. The multi-head attention segment is pivotal as it allows the division of inputs into queries, keys, and values, akin to an "information retrieval" system. For each token in the input sequence, a query is generated and compared to a set of keys that represent the values of interest. The retrieval of information from each value for a given query is contingent on the similarity between the keys and the query. This process is executed using self-attention, especially in encoding specific words within phrases. The term "multi-headed" refers to the ability to divide the combination of queries, keys, and values into N parallel chunks, thus enabling the model to consider multiple perspectives regarding the mappings being constructed. Ultimately, the multi-head attention blocks are amalgamated and layer normalized alongside the residual input.

Việc sử dụng Firebase có một số hạn chế quan trọng cần lưu ý. Đầu tiên, Firebase có thể gây ra sự gắn kết chặt chẽ với nhà cung cấp (vendor lock-in), làm cho việc chuyển đổi sang nền tảng khác trở nên khó khăn. Thứ hai, Firebase hạn chế trong khả năng thực hiện các truy vấn dữ liệu phức tạp và mở rộng đối với các ứng dụng quy mô lớn hoặc có lưu lượng truy cập đồng thời cao. Object pooling is a widely adopted technique in game development aimed at optimizing performance by efficiently managing and reusing game objects to minimize the costly operations of instantiation and destruction during runtime. The core principle involves pre-allocating a pool of objects, which can then be repeatedly activated and deactivated as required, rather than creating and destroying objects dynamically. This approach significantly reduces the computational overhead associated with memory allocation and garbage collection, particularly in use cases involving frequent object lifecycle changes, such as projectiles, particle effects, or enemy spawning. The effective implementation of object pooling contributes to enhanced game performance and resource management, aligning with optimization strategies discussed in the development of the platformer game Pixel.

NMT architectures are generally composed of multiple stacked layers, beginning with the input sequence mapped to word embeddings, which are treated as the 0th layer of the Encoder. Each following layer, whether it is a recurrent layer, convolutional layer, or self-attention layer, applies the same encoding mechanism to the output of the previous layer, as depicted in figure 2.2 with a multi-layer RNN. For instance, some NMT models implement six stacked Transformer layers in both the encoder and decoder, allowing deep NMT systems to utilize extensive parallel data and achieve state-of-the-art results. Despite these advances, deep NMT models face training difficulties due to the vanishing gradient problem, which occurs when the output value in some layer exceeds the activation function's domain. To mitigate this, residual connections are proposed, replacing f(x) with f(x) + x, where x is the lower layer’s output, facilitating gradient propagation to lower layers. Figure 2.2 illustrates this approach in a Recurrent Neural Network. The discussion then shifts to Recurrent Neural Machine Translation (RNMT), the pioneering NMT architecture, consisting of a Recurrent encoder, a Recurrent decoder, and word embedding tables. These typically use RNN layers like GRU and LSTM, which will be detailed later. RNMT is strictly auto-regressive, as each hidden state relies on all previous states, thus retaining ordering information, which is a noted benefit over CNMT and ANMT.

Recent architectures such as BigBird and LongT5 have been developed to effectively handle long document inputs. In studies related to BigBird, the attention mechanism is conceptualized through Boolean attention matrices, where attention is modeled as a graph represented by adjacency matrices A ∈ [0,1]^{n,n}, with n denoting the input size; specifically, A[i, j] equals 1 if token i attends to token j, and 0 otherwise. The authors approach the challenge of reducing the density of ones in the matrix A within self-attentive mechanisms as a graph sparsification problem. By augmenting sliding window and global attention methods with the Erdős-Rényi model, which independently selects edges with a fixed probability, the authors attempt to establish the Turing Completeness of the resultant sparsified attention structure. This approach ensures that the computational complexity scales linearly with respect to the number of tokens, thereby enhancing the efficiency of processing long sequences.

The main idea of the paragraph is to reference the foundational work by Jacob Devlin et al. on BERT, a deep bidirectional transformer model for language understanding, which has significantly influenced natural language processing research and applications, including those applied in smart contract vulnerability detection.

BERT, introduced by Jacob Devlin et al. (Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), 2019), has established a new paradigm in language model pre-training by leveraging deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding. This approach has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness across a wide range of natural language processing tasks, and its architecture serves as a critical foundation for subsequent advancements in the field. The application of BERT and similar models has notably informed recent research directions in enhancing multi-label vulnerability detection within smart contracts, as discussed in this thesis. By building on the robust contextual representations enabled by BERT, this work seeks to advance the state-of-the-art in automated vulnerability identification, thereby contributing to the reliability and security of blockchain-based systems.

Việc chia sẻ dữ liệu camera và micro theo thời gian thực giữa các người dùng trong một cuộc họp trực tuyến là một thách thức kỹ thuật đáng kể. Để đáp ứng yêu cầu truyền tải luồng dữ liệu âm thanh, hình ảnh từ camera, micro và màn hình người dùng, WebRTC được xem là giải pháp tối ưu. WebRTC (Web Real Time Communication) là một tập hợp các web API do World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) phát triển, cho phép các trình duyệt thực hiện giao tiếp thời gian thực thông qua video, âm thanh và truyền tải dữ liệu theo mô hình Peer To Peer (P2P) mà không cần phải cài đặt thêm bất kỳ phần mềm hỗ trợ bên ngoài nào. Hiện nay, WebRTC đã được tích hợp trực tiếp trong ngôn ngữ lập trình JavaScript, giúp trình duyệt có thể truy cập và thu thập dữ liệu hình ảnh, âm thanh từ camera, micro và màn hình người dùng. Các thành phần cơ bản để thực hiện giao tiếp thời gian thực trên nền tảng web được truy cập thông qua JavaScript API, bao gồm nhiều module quan trọng, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả truyền tải và chất lượng trải nghiệm người dùng trong các ứng dụng hội họp trực tuyến.

Khác với các phương pháp dựa trên UNet, kiến trúc PdaNet sử dụng module giải mã từng phần điểm để tích hợp các đặc trưng ở mức ngữ nghĩa cao, tạo ra global feature map, đồng thời áp dụng mô đun attention ngược (reverse attention) nhằm tinh chỉnh đặc trưng và khai thác thông tin về bệnh của polyp, sau đó kết hợp các thông tin này vào global feature map để đưa ra dự đoán cuối cùng. Bên cạnh đó, HarDNess MSEG và CaraNet là các kiến trúc khác được nghiên cứu nhằm cải thiện độ chính xác so với PraNet. HarDNess MSEG đề xuất một kiến trúc encoder-decoder đơn giản hơn, thay thế backbone Res2Net bằng HardNet để nâng cao độ chính xác, đồng thời loại bỏ cơ chế attention để tăng tốc độ suy luận. Tuy đạt tốc độ suy luận thời gian thực trên các thiết bị phổ thông, PlaNet và HarDNess MSEG vẫn còn hạn chế về độ chính xác trên các ảnh polyp nhỏ. CaraNet cải tiến PraNet bằng cách tích hợp mô đun Global Feature Pyramid (GFP) để trích xuất đặc trưng ở nhiều tỉ lệ khác nhau cùng axial attention trong mô đun reverse attention, giúp nâng cao độ chính xác trong phát hiện polyp. Nhờ những cải tiến này, CaraNet đạt độ chính xác vượt trội so với các phương pháp tiên tiến nhất hiện nay trên cả bộ dữ liệu ảnh polyp thông thường lẫn bộ dữ liệu ảnh polyp kích thước nhỏ.

The main idea of the paragraph is to explain the basic structure of CSS syntax, highlighting that it consists of a selector and a declaration block, and describing the roles of each component in styling HTML elements.

The syntax of Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) is fundamentally composed of two main parts: a selector and a declaration block. The selector specifies the HTML elements to which the styling rules will be applied, thereby enabling targeted customization of the webpage's presentation. Following the selector, the declaration block defines the specific styles to be implemented for the selected elements. This block may include one or more declarations, each separated by semicolons, which articulate particular stylistic instructions such as color, font, or layout. Through this structure, CSS facilitates precise and organized control over the visual design of web pages, contributing significantly to the development and maintenance of user interfaces in web applications such as the Helpdesk system developed with OdooErp.

Ban đầu, kiến di chuyển ngẫu nhiên quanh tổ, để lại pheromone đặc trưng trên đường đi, và lượng pheromone này sẽ bay hơi theo thời gian. Các kiến khác cảm nhận pheromone do kiến trước để lại và chọn đi theo những đường có nhiều pheromone, đồng thời tiếp tục để lại pheromone trên đường đi đó. Qua thời gian, pheromone trên các đường ít đi lại sẽ giảm dần, trong khi đường nào được kiến đi nhiều lần (thường là đường ngắn hơn) sẽ có mật độ pheromone cao hơn. Khi đó, xác suất kiến chọn đường ngắn nhất tăng lên, dẫn đến tất cả kiến cuối cùng di chuyển trên đường ngắn nhất.

Do đó, xác suất kiến chọn đường ngắn nhất tăng dần, cuối cùng tất cả kiến sẽ di chuyển trên đường ngắn nhất.

The paragraph discusses how products from the same lot share the same code, name, and maker, but their expiration dates may differ by batch. This is particularly important for items with a fixed shelf life, such as cosmetics, agricultural products, medications, and clothing, where expired goods can cause significant business losses. By grouping products into batches, companies can more effectively monitor and manage the quality and expiration dates of their inventory, thereby minimizing unnecessary risks.

In inventory management systems, items from a single lot typically possess identical information regarding code, name, and manufacturer; however, the expiration date may vary between different batches. This distinction is crucial for goods with predetermined shelf lives, such as cosmetics, agricultural products, medications, or clothing, as the expiration of these products can lead to considerable harm and financial loss for businesses. Effective grouping of products into batches enables organizations to efficiently track, locate, and oversee the quality and expiration status of their inventory, as well as to mitigate potential risks associated with outdated or expired stock. This systematic approach supports proactive inventory rotation and enhances overall warehouse management, as demonstrated in related studies on RFID-based automated inventory systems (see Table 3.5 and Figure 1), thereby contributing to the reduction of avoidable operational hazards.

Current GNN-oriented neural architecture search (NAS) approaches predominantly concentrate on exploring various layer aggregation components within shallow and relatively simple architectures, often encountering the limitation of the 'over-smooth' problem. To address this challenge and harness the advantages of both structural diversity and depth in graph neural network (GNN) architectures, a novel GNN generation pipeline is introduced that utilizes a two-stage search space. This pipeline is designed to automatically generate high-performance and transferable deep GNN models through a block-wise construction process. In order to further mitigate the 'over-smooth' phenomenon, the search space is enhanced by integrating multiple flexible residual connections and implementing identity mapping within the fundamental GNN layers. For the search algorithm, deep Q-learning is employed, incorporating an epsilon-greedy exploration strategy alongside reward reshaping to effectively guide the search process. Comprehensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate that the generated GNN models surpass both manually designed and existing NAS-based models in terms of performance, highlighting the potential of this approach for advancing automated GNN architecture design.

This paper explores the potential of reinforcement learning (RL), a branch of machine learning, to address complex conservation decision problems arising from global environmental change. Motivated by the need for adaptive management strategies in dynamic and uncertain ecological contexts, the authors argue that RL is especially well suited to these challenges because it focuses on designing agents that interact with and learn from their environments, does not require massive datasets, and can leverage existing ecological models and simulations. The paper provides both a conceptual and technical introduction to RL’s relevance for ecology and conservation, with illustrative examples including fisheries quota setting and management of ecological tipping points. Results are supported by four appendices containing annotated code, offering a practical resource for researchers interested in adopting or advancing RL methods in environmental science. The study highlights the promise of RL for improving decision-making in conservation and suggests avenues for future research to further integrate RL with ecological modeling and management. The process of tokenization entails converting a sentence into symbols known as tokens, which are then transformed into sequences of integers to be used as input for the NMT model. The Manifold-Aligning GAN (MAGAN) is introduced as a novel framework designed to align two manifolds by ensuring that corresponding points across different measurement spaces are brought into alignment. This method is exemplified in single-cell biology, where it facilitates the integration of genomic data from single-cell RNA sequencing with proteomic data from mass cytometry—both capturing different aspects of the same cellular populations from a shared tissue source. Experimental results demonstrate that MAGAN achieves superior alignment compared to other contemporary models, as evidenced by improved correlations among known biological markers. This advancement underscores the utility of MAGAN in multi-modal data integration, enabling more accurate and biologically meaningful interpretations across diverse measurement platforms.

The motivation behind this study is to enhance the accuracy of 3-dimensional (3D) coordinate estimation by utilizing multiple 2-dimensional (2D) images of an object, which are then used to calibrate the camera. The approach involves detailed calibration steps, including the calculation of intrinsic and extrinsic parameters to remove lens distortion, as well as computations for determining the object's size and the camera's position. A transformation strategy is proposed to accurately estimate the 3D pose from 2D images. This method is implemented using MATLAB, and validation experiments confirm its effectiveness for both pose estimation and camera calibration. The results suggest that this approach could significantly improve precision in various applications requiring accurate object localization. Future research may explore the adaptation of this technique to different environments and its integration with real-time processing systems.

The paragraph discusses the Mt.Gox attack, which was a significant security breach in the history of blockchain and cryptocurrency exchanges. It highlights the scale of the loss, the vulnerability exploited, and the broader implications for the perceived safety of cryptocurrency platforms. 

The Mt.Gox attack represents one of the most catastrophic incidents in the history of blockchain security, underscoring the critical importance of robust vulnerability detection in smart contract and exchange platforms. Once the world’s largest bitcoin exchange, Mt.Gox suffered a devastating breach in 2014, during which attackers exploited a vulnerability within the platform’s software to steal over 850,000 Bitcoins—valued at approximately $450 million at that time. The scale and impact of this attack, as documented in related works, have fueled considerable controversy and debate regarding the overall security of cryptocurrency exchanges, emphasizing the urgent need for advanced detection mechanisms and the development of more resilient smart contract systems (see Table 3.5). The present thesis builds upon these lessons, aiming to enhance multi-label vulnerability detection by leveraging language models, thereby contributing to the ongoing efforts to fortify blockchain infrastructures against similar large-scale attacks.

The paragraph discusses the concept of Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information (NPMI) and its application in measuring coherence by integrating it with an indirect cosine measure and a boolean sliding window mechanism. The main idea is that the boolean sliding window approach adjusts the probability calculation of word co-occurrence (P(wi, wj)) to account for their proximity within a predefined window size, rather than just their presence in the same document. 

In the context of measuring linguistic coherence, the Normalized Pointwise Mutual Information (NPMI) between two words, wi and wj, is defined as NPMI (wi, wj) = (log(P(wi,wj)+ϵ P(wi)·P(wj)) −log(P(wi, wj)) +ϵ). This metric is enhanced by combining it with an indirect cosine measure alongside a boolean sliding window cv. The innovative aspect of the boolean sliding window lies in its modification of the probability calculation for the co-occurrence of words, P(wi, wj). Instead of simply determining the probability that wi and wj appear in the same document, it refines this probability to consider the likelihood that these words occur together within a specified window size. For instance, in the segmented sentence “Manchester_City thành_công chiêu_mộ Erling_Haaland”, while the terms “Erling_Haaland” and “Manchester_City” might be present in the same document, they would not be considered within the same window if the window size is set to less than four words. This approach adds a layer of precision in assessing the contextual relationship between words, thereby enhancing the coherence measure.

The main idea of the paragraph is to discuss the significance of context-aware representations in the extraction of relations from knowledge bases, as explored by Sorokin and Gurevych. The authors conducted a study presented at the 2017 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, focusing on enhancing the accuracy of knowledge base relation extraction through context-aware methods. This contribution is pivotal in advancing natural language processing techniques for more precise information retrieval from structured databases.

In their seminal work presented at the 2017 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, Sorokin and Gurevych (2017) explore the development of context-aware representations to enhance the process of relation extraction from knowledge bases. Their research, documented on pages 1784-1789 of the conference proceedings, underscores the importance of integrating contextual information to improve the precision and accuracy of information retrieval in natural language processing. The study provides a significant contribution to the field by demonstrating how context-aware techniques can effectively bridge the gap between raw data and structured databases, thereby facilitating more accurate and meaningful extraction of relations. This work represents a critical advancement in computational linguistics, particularly in the domain of knowledge base management and retrieval systems, as it offers a sophisticated approach to overcoming the challenges inherent in traditional relation extraction methodologies.

This paper introduces DeepV2D, an end-to-end deep learning architecture designed to predict depth from video, motivated by the need to integrate the powerful representation learning capabilities of neural networks with established geometric principles of image formation. The authors approach this by transforming classical geometric algorithms into trainable modules, which are then incorporated into a differentiable architecture that facilitates joint optimization. DeepV2D operates by interleaving motion estimation and depth estimation stages, alternating between them during inference until convergence is achieved, resulting in accurate depth predictions. The results demonstrate that this architecture effectively leverages both data-driven learning and geometric constraints to enhance depth estimation from video. These findings suggest promising directions for future research in combining deep learning with geometric reasoning for robust 3D scene understanding. (124 words)

Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD), characterized by progressive renal cyst growth, is the most prevalent and potentially lethal monogenic kidney disease, affecting 1 in 500–100 people. Total Kidney Volume (TKV) and its growth, measured from Computed Tomography images, serve as essential prognostic markers for renal function loss. Due to the large variation in kidney shape and size in ADPKD, existing TKV computation methods, including 2D convolutional neural networks, lack sufficient accuracy for clinical use. We propose multi-task 3D Convolutional Neural Networks to segment ADPK, achieving a mean DICE score of 0.95 and a mean absolute percentage TKV error of 3.86%. To address class imbalance, we introduce bootstrapped cross-entropy loss and compare it with the commonly used dice loss in medical image segmentation.

Many buyers remain unsatisfied with discovered products despite significant effort, partly because users often do not fully or accurately specify their search criteria until prompted by system recommendations or displayed information. Search engines are unable to solve this problem. Additionally, best-selling products constitute only a small fraction of the total offerings, while the extensive list of less popular products generates minimal revenue, a phenomenon referred to as the "long tail" in commerce.

Despite considerable effort, buyers frequently find themselves dissatisfied with the products they discover, largely because users tend to provide incomplete or imprecise search criteria, often adjusting their preferences only after seeing system-generated recommendations or information. In such situations, search engines are unable to address these challenges effectively. Các biến số O (open), C (close), H (high), L (low), và V (volume) lần lượt thể hiện giá mở cửa (giá tham chiếu), giá đóng cửa, giá cao nhất, giá thấp nhất, và khối lượng giao dịch trong phiên giao dịch hàng ngày. Trong số các chỉ báo kỹ thuật được sử dụng để phân tích thị trường, chỉ số On-Balance Volume (OBV) đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc đánh giá mối liên hệ giữa biến động giá và khối lượng giao dịch. OBV được xác định bằng cách cộng dồn khối lượng giao dịch trong các phiên: nếu giá đóng cửa tăng so với phiên trước, khối lượng giao dịch của phiên đó sẽ được cộng vào tổng OBV; ngược lại, nếu giá đóng cửa giảm, khối lượng sẽ bị trừ khỏi tổng OBV. Ý nghĩa cốt lõi của OBV là phản ánh sức mạnh tăng hoặc giảm của giá thông qua động thái của khối lượng giao dịch thực tế, từ đó cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về xu hướng thị trường tiềm năng dựa trên hành vi của dòng tiền. Các nghiên cứu trước đây đã khẳng định hiệu quả của OBV trong dự đoán xu hướng giá và hỗ trợ ra quyết định đầu tư (Hình A). Tuy nhiên, nghiên cứu hiện tại tiếp tục làm rõ hơn vai trò của OBV trong bối cảnh cụ thể của thị trường Việt Nam, đồng thời phân tích sâu sắc mối quan hệ giữa chỉ báo này với các biến động giá ngắn hạn và dài hạn.
