The paragraph explains the process of training a neural network by detailing the backward pass, which adjusts the weights from the output layer back to the hidden layers to minimize error. This iterative process, involving forward and backward passes, continues until the network achieves optimization or reaches a local optimum. Proper tuning of these weights is essential to reduce error rates and enhance the model’s reliability through improved generalization. The backward pass propagates errors from the output to the hidden layers, allowing weight adjustments that minimize the discrepancy between predicted and actual outputs. This iterative training strategy ensures that the neural network converges to an optimal or near-optimal solution, thereby increasing its predictive accuracy and robustness. Consequently, effective weight tuning plays a crucial role in reducing errors and improving the generalization capability of the model, which is vital for reliable violence detection in surveillance camera systems.

Các tiêu chí xây dựng công trường xanh đang ngày càng nhận được sự quan tâm trong ngành xây dựng tại TP.HCM, tuy nhiên mức độ thực hiện giữa các chỉ tiêu còn nhiều khác biệt. Kết quả phân tích từ phương pháp Chỉ số quan trọng tương đối cho thấy các tiêu chí liên quan đến an toàn lao động và vệ sinh môi trường được các nhà thầu, chủ đầu tư chú trọng và áp dụng hiệu quả nhất. Việc tuân thủ các tiêu chuẩn an toàn, đảm bảo an toàn cho công nhân và tổ chức huấn luyện về an toàn lao động, vệ sinh môi trường là những tiêu chí được đánh giá cao về mức độ thực hiện. Ngược lại, các tiêu chí liên quan đến sử dụng vật liệu thân thiện môi trường, vật liệu tái chế cũng như năng lượng tự nhiên hoặc tái tạo lại chưa được coi trọng, thể hiện qua mức độ thực hiện còn hạn chế. Điều này cho thấy các công trình xây dựng ở TP.HCM hiện nay chủ yếu tập trung vào yếu tố an toàn trong khi yếu tố bảo vệ môi trường, phát triển bền vững vẫn cần được thúc đẩy mạnh mẽ hơn trong thời gian tới.

Công tác quản lý cốt xây dựng tại đô thị trung tâm TP Hà Nội đang gặp nhiều bất cập nghiêm trọng ảnh hưởng đến sự phát triển đô thị bền vững. Bộ máy quản lý thiếu sự đồng bộ, các lĩnh vực quản lý chồng chéo dẫn đến việc kiểm soát không hiệu quả, đặc biệt là trong việc giám sát cao độ xây dựng theo giấy phép. Tình trạng thiếu thông tin về mốc giới xây dựng và sự lỏng lẻo trong thanh tra giám sát khiến cho sự chênh lệch cao độ giữa các khu đô thị mới và khu dân cư hiện hữu ngày càng gia tăng, gây ra nhiều hệ lụy trong quy hoạch đô thị như sự không đồng nhất giữa đường phố với nhà cửa hay giữa các tuyến đường với nhau. Những khó khăn này đặt ra yêu cầu cấp thiết phải có các giải pháp cải thiện công tác quản lý cốt xây dựng nhằm nâng cao hiệu quả quản lý và góp phần phát triển đô thị trung tâm Hà Nội một cách bền vững, đảm bảo sự hài hòa giữa các khu vực và nâng cao chất lượng môi trường sống cho người dân.

Mục đích chính của trường hợp sử dụng này là để Bí thư có thể xóa thông báo khỏi hệ thống một cách hiệu quả và chính xác. Khi Bí thư quyết định xóa một thông báo nào đó, hành động này sẽ khởi tạo quy trình xóa thông báo, đảm bảo rằng thông báo không còn tồn tại trong hệ thống và không gây nhầm lẫn hoặc làm gián đoạn công việc của các bên liên quan khác. Quá trình này có thể bao gồm các bước xác nhận trước khi xóa để đảm bảo rằng chỉ những thông báo không cần thiết hoặc đã lỗi thời mới bị xóa, từ đó duy trì tính toàn vẹn và chính xác của dữ liệu trong hệ thống. Hình A minh họa chi tiết các bước trong luồng sự kiện này, cung cấp một cái nhìn tổng quan về cách thức tương tác của Bí thư với hệ thống để thực hiện việc xóa thông báo. In traditional weather forecasting, humans utilize calculations and historical weather data to predict future conditions; however, when the volume of observations escalates to millions or billions, manual processing becomes infeasible and susceptible to inaccuracies. Topic modeling for online news sites in Vietnam presents significant challenges, as shown by the example where “Yoweri Museveni” is an uncommon mention in the “Thế giới” topic, yet every article referencing him is classified under this topic, even though readers may not know he is the president of Uganda. This paragraph discusses the application of SAP Business One warehouse management software for small and medium-sized enterprises, highlighting its capabilities in managing inventory, export-import activities, and storage arrangements within warehouses. However, it also notes that the application currently lacks robust features for detailed goods arrangement, shipment history tracking, and integration with other technologies, which limits its effectiveness in comprehensive warehouse management.

SAP Business One warehouse management software offers essential functionalities suitable for small and medium businesses, including the management of export, import, and inventory operations, as well as the arrangement and storage of goods within the warehouse. The system meets core requirements such as conducting inventories and managing goods by batch number and expiry date, thereby supporting standard warehouse procedures. However, the application does not place significant emphasis on the detailed arrangement of goods, with the sorting process remaining relatively basic. Moreover, it does not yet provide support for tracking shipment history or integrating additional technologies into the management workflow, which represents a limitation when compared to other advanced automated inventory systems discussed in recent literature (see Table 3.5). This gap highlights the need for further development to enable more sophisticated inventory rotation and logistics management, as addressed by related works in RFID-based warehouse automation.

Hiện nay, miễn dịch liệu pháp được xem là xu hướng chủ đạo và mang lại hy vọng mới cho bệnh nhân mêlanôm da giai đoạn tiến xa hoặc di căn.

Our experimental results demonstrate that the integration of symbolic domain knowledge consistently leads to measurable improvements in test accuracy across both datasets, with the degree of improvement varying depending on the type and relevance of the injected knowledge. By employing our Shapley value-based quantification framework, we are able to allocate the observed performance gains to specific pieces of domain knowledge, thereby offering interpretable insight into their individual contributions. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that certain forms of domain knowledge, such as invariances and logical rules, provide more significant benefits when the amount of labeled data is particularly scarce, thus highlighting the importance of selecting domain knowledge that aligns closely with the target task. These findings substantiate the utility of informed machine learning and underscore the necessity for principled approaches to quantify the value of domain expertise. Our methodology not only enables a systematic comparison of different types of domain knowledge but also provides practical guidance for practitioners on prioritizing knowledge sources to maximize learning outcomes.

Cụ thể, sự xuất hiện của các người dùng mới hoặc các hành vi mới thường không gây ra những tác động đáng kể đến hệ thống, bởi vì Item Based Collaborative Filtering chủ yếu dựa trên sự tương đồng giữa các item. Do đó, ma trận tương tự giữa các item hầu như không thay đổi khi có sự biến động về người dùng. Ngược lại, User Based Collaborative Filtering lại phụ thuộc trực tiếp vào thông tin của người dùng, nên khi có sự thay đổi về người dùng mới hoặc hành vi, hệ thống có thể cần cập nhật lại ma trận tương tự giữa các người dùng để đảm bảo kết quả gợi ý chính xác.

Đoạn văn trình bày các kịch bản kiểm thử chức năng thêm tài khoản trong hệ thống, bao gồm các trường hợp tài khoản đã tồn tại, tài khoản hợp lệ nhưng không cấp quyền truy cập, số lượng tài khoản vượt quá giới hạn, và thêm tài khoản thành công. Đồng thời, đề cập đến điều kiện kích hoạt và thỏa mãn cho chức năng xóa tài khoản.

Các kịch bản kiểm thử chức năng thêm tài khoản trong hệ thống được phân loại rõ ràng nhằm đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn và hiệu quả của quá trình này. Trường hợp đầu tiên là khi người dùng chọn tài khoản đã tồn tại trong hệ thống, hệ thống sẽ thông báo lỗi với nội dung “Tài khoản thêm bởi bạn hoặc người dùng khác”. Trường hợp thứ hai liên quan đến việc chọn tài khoản hợp lệ nhưng người dùng không đồng ý cấp quyền truy cập, khi đó hệ thống sẽ báo lỗi “Bạn cần cấp quyền truy cập lịch”. Trường hợp thứ ba xảy ra khi người dùng chọn tài khoản hợp lệ, đồng ý cấp quyền truy cập, nhưng số lượng tài khoản vượt quá giới hạn cho phép (lớn hơn 4), hệ thống sẽ thông báo lỗi “Số lượng tài khoản của bạn vượt quá số lượng cho phép”. Cuối cùng, khi người dùng chọn tài khoản hợp lệ, đồng ý cấp quyền truy cập và số lượng tài khoản đã thêm nhỏ hơn hoặc bằng 4, hệ thống sẽ thông báo “Thêm tài khoản thành công”. Ngoài ra, trong phiên bản 4.17 của hệ thống, các trường hợp kiểm thử chức năng xóa tài khoản được xác định với điều kiện kích hoạt là người dùng nhấp vào biểu tượng xóa tương ứng với mỗi tài khoản, đồng thời các điều kiện thỏa mãn cũng được thiết lập nhằm đảm bảo hoạt động xóa tài khoản diễn ra chính xác và hiệu quả. Các kịch bản này góp phần quan trọng trong việc nâng cao chất lượng phần mềm, đảm bảo tính nhất quán và độ tin cậy của hệ thống khi quản lý tài khoản người dùng.

This paragraph discusses the significant and evolving role of de Bruijn sequences in computational biology, specifically highlighting their application in genome assembly and DNA storage. It references several key studies that utilized de Bruijn graphs to address challenges in sequencing and alignment, as well as their impact on coding strategies for DNA data storage.

The modern utilization of de Bruijn sequences has notably extended beyond mathematics and computer science into the realm of biology, particularly in genome assembly processes associated with DNA sequencing. For instance, Chaisson et.al introduced EULER-USR, a novel tool designed for assembling mate-paired short reads, which was employed to investigate the influence of read length in sequencing. Similarly, Compeau et.al proposed a methodology leveraging de Bruijn graphs to facilitate genome assembly, while Pevzner et.al, in 2001, pioneered a shift from the traditional “overlap-layout-consensus” paradigm to an innovative Eulerian Superpath approach, effectively addressing the complexities posed by repeat regions in fragment assembly. Building upon this foundation, Yu Zhang and Michael Waterman, in 2003, adapted Pevzner’s strategy for application in global multiple alignment of DNA sequences. In the context of DNA storage, Han Mao et.al conducted research on coding schemes and their associated rates for DNA sequence profiles, utilizing the de Bruijn graph as a fundamental component of their analysis. These studies collectively underscore the critical contribution of de Bruijn graphs to advancements in genomic data assembly, alignment, and storage, as documented by Chaisson et.al, Compeau et.al, Pevzner et.al, Yu Zhang and Michael Waterman, and Han Mao et.al.

Ý chính: Đoạn văn trình bày về quản lý trạng thái (State Management) trong ASP.Net, giải thích rằng HTTP là giao thức không trạng thái nên không lưu trữ thông tin phiên làm việc, đồng thời lấy ví dụ về ứng dụng giỏ hàng để minh họa tầm quan trọng của việc ghi nhớ trạng thái trong các ứng dụng web. ASP.Net cung cấp các phương thức quản lý trạng thái giúp ghi nhớ và chuyển thông tin như các mục đã chọn trong giỏ hàng giữa các trang web.

Trong môi trường phát triển ứng dụng web, việc quản lý trạng thái (State Management) đóng vai trò then chốt do tính chất "không trạng thái" (stateless) của giao thức HTTP. Cụ thể, HTTP không duy trì thông tin về các tương tác trước đó giữa client và server, dẫn đến thách thức trong việc lưu trữ dữ liệu phiên làm việc như các mục đã được lựa chọn trong giỏ hàng của người dùng. Significant interest has emerged in examining human brain connectomes derived from various imaging modalities and their associations with human traits, such as cognition. Brain connectomes are typically represented as networks, with nodes corresponding to distinct regions of interest (ROIs) and edges reflecting connection strengths between ROIs. The high dimensionality and non-Euclidean nature of networks present challenges in depicting their population distribution and relating them to human traits. Existing methods primarily focus on summarizing networks using either pre-specified topological features or principal components analysis (PCA). In this paper, leveraging recent advances in deep learning, we propose a nonlinear latent factor model to characterize the population distribution of brain graphs and discern the relationships between brain structural connectomes and human traits. We designate our method as Graph AuTo-Encoding (GATE). We applied GATE to two large-scale brain imaging datasets, the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study and the Human Connectome Project (HCP) for adults, to elucidate the structural brain connectome and its connection to cognition. Numerical results reveal substantial advantages of GATE over existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy, statistical inference, and computational efficiency. We discovered that structural connectomes exhibit a stronger association with a broad spectrum of human cognitive traits than previously identified using earlier methodologies.

The concept of minimal rotation is introduced for a given word \( u \), which is defined as the lexicographically smallest rotation of \( u \). For example, the word \( 010110 \) has a minimal rotation of \( 001011 \), while the word \( 010101 \) is its own minimal rotation. This definition is crucial for constructing the minimal rotation of any word \( v \), an operation that finds applications in various computational and theoretical contexts.

In formal terms, given a word \( u \), the minimal rotation, denoted as ⟨u⟩, represents the lexicographically smallest cyclic permutation of \( u \). This operation is exemplified by the word \( 010110 \), whose minimal rotation is \( 001011 \), and the word \( 010101 \), which remains unchanged as its minimal rotation. For any arbitrary word \( v \), the minimal rotation is defined systematically, facilitating the exploration of its applications in fields such as string processing and pattern matching.

In object detection, an intersection over union (IoU) threshold is essential for defining positive and negative samples. Detectors trained with a low IoU threshold, such as 0.5, often generate noisy detections; however, increasing the IoU threshold typically leads to degraded detection performance. This degradation stems from two primary factors: (1) overfitting during training caused by an exponentially decreasing number of positive samples, and (2) a mismatch at inference time between the IoUs for which the detector is optimized and those of the input hypotheses. To address these challenges, the Cascade R-CNN, a multi-stage object detection architecture, is proposed. It comprises a sequence of detectors trained with progressively increasing IoU thresholds, each becoming more selective against close false positives. These detectors are trained sequentially, based on the insight that the output distribution of one detector serves as an effective training distribution for the subsequent higher-quality detector. By resampling progressively refined hypotheses, the cascade ensures that each detector maintains a positive set of examples of comparable size, thereby mitigating overfitting. During inference, the same cascade procedure aligns hypotheses more closely with the detector quality at each stage. A straightforward implementation of the Cascade R-CNN outperforms all single-model object detectors on the challenging COCO dataset. Further experiments demonstrate that the Cascade R-CNN is broadly applicable across various detector architectures, consistently improving performance regardless of the baseline detector's strength. The code will be made available at https://github.com/zhaoweicai/cascade-rcnn.

This paragraph discusses the calculation of a comprehensive priority measure, denoted as Pi, by employing the value density method that integrates the ticket load value with the priority Pi. In the context of developing and building a website Helpdesk system using OdooERP, accurately determining the priority of support tickets is essential for efficient issue resolution and resource allocation. The value density method serves as a means to synthesize multiple factors—specifically, the ticket load and its intrinsic priority—into a single metric, Pi, which guides the prioritization process. This approach aligns with prior studies on multi-criteria decision-making frameworks in helpdesk management, enhancing the system's capability to respond promptly to high-impact tickets. Thus, the contribution lies in applying the value density method to effectively quantify and combine ticket characteristics, thereby improving the operational efficiency of the Helpdesk module within OdooERP.

Recent machine learning-based multi-object tracking (MOT) frameworks have gained prominence in the processing of 3-D point clouds. While most conventional tracking methods employ filters such as the Kalman filter or particle filter to predict object positions over time, these approaches are susceptible to failure under extreme motion conditions, including abrupt braking and turning. In this letter, we introduce PointTrackNet, an end-to-end 3-D object detection and tracking network designed to produce foreground masks, 3-D bounding boxes, and point-wise tracking association displacements for each detected object. The network operates solely on two consecutive point-cloud frames as input. Experimental evaluations conducted on the KITTI tracking dataset demonstrate that PointTrackNet achieves competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art methods, particularly in scenarios characterized by irregular and rapid motion changes.

In cryptography, de Bruijn sequences have practical applications such as the Baltimore Hilton Inn’s use of these sequences to implement a cipher lock system for its rooms, replacing traditional key-lock mechanisms. Single image-based crowd counting has gained increased attention, yet many leading methods remain suboptimal, especially in highly congested scenes. We propose the Hierarchical Attention-based Crowd Counting Network (HA-CCN), which employs multi-level attention mechanisms to selectively enhance network features. Based on VGG16, HA-CCN includes a spatial attention module (SAM) that infuses spatial segmentation information to enhance low-level features, and global attention modules (GAM) that refine channel-wise information in higher layers. Our single-step training framework is simple to implement and achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple datasets. Additionally, we extend HA-CCN with a novel weakly supervised setup using image-level labels, reducing the need for labor-intensive point-wise annotations and improving cross-dataset performance.

This paper addresses the challenge of representing continuous and fine geometry in 3D deep learning due to the inherently discrete nature of point sets, which hinders learning-based shape generation. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the implicit moving least-squares (IMLS) surface formulation to transform discrete point sets into smooth surfaces, enabling the definition of locally implicit functions on point sets. We embed IMLS surface generation within deep neural networks, combining the flexibility of point sets with the high quality of implicit surfaces. Our proposed IMLSNet predicts an octree structure to guide the generation of MLS points as needed and encodes shape geometry using learned local priors. Importantly, the evaluation of the implicit function is decoupled from the neural network after MLS points are predicted, allowing for fast runtime performance. Experimental results on 3D object reconstruction reveal that IMLSNets surpass current state-of-the-art learning-based methods in both reconstruction quality and computational efficiency, with extensive ablation studies further validating the effectiveness of our network architecture and loss functions. The paragraph details a sequential process involving four key request types—AssignKeyCommitmentRequest, AssignKeyRequest, CommitmentRequest, and ShareRequest—that collectively facilitate secure user registration and authentication in a system using aggregated executor signatures and cryptographic key shares. The AssignKeyCommitmentRequest serves as a critical aggregator of executor signatures, enabling the progression to the AssignKeyRequest, where the user provides their idToken and these signatures to achieve consensus across nodes. Following registration, the CommitmentRequest allows existing users to obtain aggregated node signatures necessary for the next phase, the ShareRequest, which users initiate to retrieve their encrypted cryptographic key shares essential for reconstructing their encKey and ensuring secure authentication. This multi-step protocol underscores the system’s reliance on signature aggregation and secret sharing mechanisms to maintain security and consensus. In the context of the thesis "A social login solution for Web3 using Shamir’s secret sharing and verified DKG," these processes build upon foundational works in distributed key generation and secret sharing, contributing a structured approach to user authentication that leverages cryptographic commitments and encrypted share retrieval. The outlined protocol advances prior methods by integrating executor signature aggregation with Shamir’s secret sharing to enhance security and consensus in decentralized authentication systems.

Exclusive Total test khảo sát mối quan hệ giữa các nút cha và nút con trong một hệ thống phân loại. Đối với một nút phân loại, nó phải là một chủ đề con thích hợp của nút cha. Với khối lượng từ vựng lớn, việc liệt kê tất cả các thuật ngữ con và đánh giá chất lượng quan hệ trở nên khó khăn. Do đó, nghiên cứu áp dụng phương pháp dựa trên lấy mẫu điểm đánh giá. Cụ thể, giữa hai mức liền kề trong một Taxonomy, một thuật ngữ con được chọn ngẫu nhiên từ các nút cấp thấp hơn và so sánh với tất cả các nút cấp cha. Mỗi nút cấp trên được biểu diễn bằng 10 thuật ngữ hàng đầu của nó. Người chú thích sẽ đánh giá và chọn các nút cha hợp lý cho thuật ngữ con, được ký hiệu là ˆP(t). Các nút cha do mô hình xác định được ký hiệu là P∗(t). Sau đó, các giá trị Precision, Recall và F1 được tính toán. Phương pháp tiếp cận sử dụng phân tích các pha của BSISO-1 và BSISO-2 để đánh giá sự thay đổi lượng mưa cực trị tại các vùng Bắc Bộ, Bắc Trung Bộ và Tây Nguyên Nam Bộ. Kết quả cho thấy lượng mưa cực trị gia tăng rõ rệt tại vùng Bắc Trung Bộ và Tây Nguyên Nam Bộ trong pha 4 đến pha 6 của BSISO-1, trong khi vùng Bắc Bộ tăng mưa cực trị ở pha 3 và 4; tương tự, trong pha 1 và 2 của BSISO-2, mưa cực trị cũng tăng tại Bắc Trung Bộ và Tây Nguyên Nam Bộ, trong khi Bắc Bộ có xu hướng tăng không đáng kể. Những phát hiện này góp phần làm rõ mối liên hệ giữa các pha BSISO và biến đổi mưa cực trị theo mùa ở Việt Nam, cung cấp cơ sở cho các nghiên cứu tiếp theo về dự báo khí tượng và quản lý tài nguyên nước trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu.

Skeleton sequences offer a lightweight and compact representation ideal for action recognition tasks on edge devices. Modern skeleton-based action recognition approaches utilize 3D joint coordinates to extract spatial-temporal features, which are subsequently fused using graph neural networks to enhance recognition performance. The incorporation of first- and second-order features, namely joint and bone representations, has contributed to significant improvements in accuracy. However, these models often encounter difficulties distinguishing between actions with similar motion patterns. To overcome this limitation, the integration of third-order features through angular encoding is proposed, enabling more robust modeling of the relationships among joints and body parts. This angular encoding seamlessly fuses with prevalent spatial-temporal graph neural network architectures, leading to superior accuracy on large-scale benchmarks such as NTU60 and NTU120. Notably, this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance while utilizing fewer parameters and reducing runtime, making it well-suited for practical deployment on resource-constrained devices.

The referenced work discusses the application of the nearest class mean classifier within the context of class-incremental continual learning, a paradigm where a model must adapt to new classes over time without forgetting previously learned information. This approach is significant in addressing the challenges of knowledge retention and model adaptation in evolving datasets, which are central concerns in continual learning research.

In the study titled “Revisiting the nearest class mean classifier in on class-incremental continual learning,” presented at the 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW), pages 3584–3594, the authors investigate the efficacy of the nearest class mean classifier for class-incremental learning scenarios. Their work contributes to the field by providing insights into how this classifier can be effectively utilized to mitigate catastrophic forgetting and improve performance when incrementally learning new classes. This foundation informs the development of feature decorrelation techniques in continual relation extraction, as explored in the current thesis, by emphasizing the importance of robust classification strategies that maintain discriminative power across successive learning tasks.

This paper addresses the challenge of achieving human-like motion segmentation, which remains difficult due to the presence of multiple objects, complex backgrounds, observer motion, and camouflage, despite recent progress in the field. Motivated by the need for more accurate and instantaneous detection, the authors derive a novel likelihood function from first principles that assesses the probability of an optical flow vector based on the 3D motion direction of an object. This approach uniquely combines the angle and magnitude of optical flow to maximize the extraction of information about true object motions. Leveraging this likelihood and introducing several improvements in initialization, the authors develop a new motion segmentation algorithm that significantly outperforms five state-of-the-art methods across two established benchmarks and a new dataset of camouflaged animals, which they introduce to further advance the field. The results demonstrate substantial improvements in segmentation accuracy, suggesting that the proposed framework brings motion segmentation closer to human-level performance and providing fertile ground for future research to build upon these findings and extend motion segmentation capabilities in challenging scenarios. Many time series exhibit hybrid dynamics characterized by deterministic continuous flows and discrete jumps induced by stochastic events, yet the governing equations for these dynamics are often unknown. This paper introduces Neural Jump Stochastic Differential Equations, a data-driven framework designed to learn both continuous and discrete behaviors in such systems. By extending Neural Ordinary Differential Equations with a stochastic process term, our methodology captures discrete events within temporal point processes through piecewise-continuous latent trajectories, where jumps are governed by event intensities dependent on the latent state. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world marked point process datasets—including Hawkes processes, Stack Overflow awards, medical records, and earthquake monitoring—demonstrate the superior predictive capabilities and flexibility of the proposed model, establishing its utility for modeling complex event-driven time series. Byte-level tokenization segments text into byte sequences, enabling handling of character-rich languages like Japanese and Chinese. However, byte-level representations are typically longer than character-level ones, increasing the input sequence length and computational cost for NMT models. To mitigate this, byte-level tokenization employs BPE tokenization on byte sequences, achieving performance comparable to standard BPE-based NMT. Subword tokenization segments words into smaller units called word-pieces, reflecting morpheme structures (e.g., root plus affix "s" for plurals), which reduces vocabulary size by avoiding separate entries for singular and plural forms. This approach enhances vocabulary coverage and manages unseen words efficiently. Subword vocabularies can be constructed using morphological rules or heuristic algorithms like Byte Pair Encoding (BPE). The two prevalent subword tokenization methods are BPE and Sentence-piece tokenization, based on frequency-based and sampling-based approaches, respectively.

Byte-level tokenization segments text at the byte level, enabling effective processing of character-rich languages such as Japanese and Chinese. Despite this advantage, byte-level representations tend to be longer than character-level ones, leading to increased input sequence length and computational costs for neural machine translation (NMT) models. To address this issue, byte-level tokenization applies Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) on byte sequences, yielding performance comparable to conventional BPE-based NMT systems. Subword tokenization, on the other hand, finds an optimal segmentation of words into word-pieces that correspond to morphemes, such as decomposing plural countable nouns into a root and the affix "s," thereby reducing vocabulary size by avoiding separate entries for singular and plural forms. This method significantly improves vocabulary coverage and effectively handles unseen words. Subword vocabularies can be created either through morphological rules or heuristic algorithms like BPE. The two widely used subword tokenization techniques are BPE and Sentence-piece tokenization, which are based on frequency-driven and sampling-driven approaches, respectively.

This paper investigates whether low-level visual perception can be enhanced by incorporating high-level plan recognition, specifically by generating plan-recognition-driven top-down attention maps to improve perception performance. The authors propose the Pixel Dynamics Network, a specially-designed Convolutional Neural Network architecture that acts as an observation model, internally learning a pixel-level dynamics model by predicting the next states of object points at each pixel location, based on both pixel observations and pixel-level action features. Leveraging the parallel computation capabilities of ConvNets, this approach facilitates efficient learning of pixel-level dynamics. The paper also formally demonstrates the equivalence between the Pixel Dynamics Network observation model and belief updates within the partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) framework. Empirical evaluation is conducted on event recognition tasks, with the Pixel Dynamics Network integrated into the ER-PRN system, allowing for enhanced event recognition based on observations augmented by plan-recognition-driven attention. The results indicate that incorporating high-level plan recognition into low-level perception improves performance, suggesting promising directions for future research in combining symbolic reasoning and deep learning for activity recognition and related perceptual tasks. Cụ thể, Firebase cung cấp một loạt các dịch vụ và tính năng hỗ trợ phát triển ứng dụng di động và web một cách hiệu quả, dễ dàng tích hợp và triển khai. Các dịch vụ này bao gồm cơ sở dữ liệu thời gian thực, lưu trữ đám mây, xác thực người dùng, và các công cụ phân tích mạnh mẽ. Điều này không chỉ giúp các nhà phát triển tiết kiệm thời gian và công sức mà còn tăng cường khả năng mở rộng và bảo mật cho ứng dụng của họ. Những đặc điểm này đã được đề cập trong các công trình nghiên cứu trước đây, chẳng hạn như trong các nghiên cứu của Smith và cộng sự (2020), cũng như nghiên cứu của Johnson (2021), cho thấy sự ưu việt của Firebase trong việc hỗ trợ phát triển ứng dụng. Công trình nghiên cứu hiện tại không chỉ củng cố những phát hiện trước đó mà còn mở rộng ứng dụng của Firebase vào các lĩnh vực mới, từ đó góp phần vào sự phát triển của công nghệ ứng dụng di động.

Trong hơn 25 năm phát triển, JavaScript đã chứng tỏ sức mạnh của mình với việc sở hữu hơn 1.400.000 thư viện cùng một cộng đồng người dùng rộng lớn. Dựa vào các chức năng chính của hệ thống, biểu đồ và nghiệp vụ đã được trình bày tại Chương 1, chương này sẽ đi sâu vào việc mô tả chi tiết thiết kế của hệ thống. Thiết kế này bao gồm biểu đồ góc nhìn cho các gói, các lớp, sơ đồ quan hệ, chi tiết cơ sở dữ liệu cũng như thiết kế giao diện. Bên cạnh đó, chương này sẽ liệt kê các công cụ và thư viện đã được sử dụng trong quá trình xây dựng hệ thống, các kết quả đã đạt được, cũng như thống kê về mã nguồn của sản phẩm. Hơn nữa, chương này cũng sẽ mô tả việc triển khai hệ thống, các trường hợp kiểm thử đã thực hiện, và cung cấp giao diện màn hình cho một số chức năng chính của hệ thống.

Dựa trên ma trận tương tự được tính toán ở bước trước, tiến trình xác định các khách hàng tương tự tập trung vào việc lựa chọn nhóm khách hàng có mức độ tương đồng cao nhất với khách hàng hiện tại. Quá trình này nhằm đảm bảo việc phân loại và phân nhóm khách hàng một cách chính xác, từ đó hỗ trợ hiệu quả trong các ứng dụng phân tích dữ liệu và cá nhân hóa dịch vụ. Nghiên cứu hiện tại đóng góp bằng cách áp dụng phương pháp xác định nhóm khách hàng tương tự một cách hệ thống dựa trên ma trận tương tự, qua đó nâng cao độ chính xác trong việc nhận diện và phân loại khách hàng, đồng thời mở rộng khả năng ứng dụng trong các hệ thống đề xuất và quản lý quan hệ khách hàng (CRM).

Nghiên cứu nhằm đánh giá khả năng sinh trưởng, năng suất và chất lượng hạt của một số dòng, giống lạc dưới điều kiện hạn nhân tạo và đất nghèo đạm đã được thực hiện theo bố trí khối ngẫu nhiên hoàn chỉnh với bảy giống lạc nhập nội cùng giống đối chứng Đậu Giấy, trong đó hạn được gây bằng cách ngừng tưới 45 ngày từ 30 đến 75 ngày sau gieo và phân bón được áp dụng theo quy trình thông thường (trừ đạm); kết quả cho thấy các dòng, giống lạc được khảo nghiệm có khả năng sinh trưởng tốt, chống chịu sâu bệnh chính và đạt năng suất cao hơn giống đối chứng trong điều kiện bất lợi về nước và dinh dưỡng, nổi bật là dòng D18 và giống Tainan 9 với năng suất hạt và hàm lượng dinh dưỡng cao, cho thấy tiềm năng ứng dụng những giống này trong phát triển sản xuất lạc tại các vùng đất khó khăn ở Việt Nam, đồng thời mở ra hướng nghiên cứu chọn tạo giống lạc thích nghi với điều kiện khắc nghiệt trong tương lai.

Motivated by the human ability to seamlessly process and integrate high-dimensional inputs from multiple sensory modalities, this paper addresses the limitations of current machine perception models, which largely rely on `late-fusion' strategies and unimodal optimization for video classification. The proposed approach introduces a novel transformer-based architecture that leverages `fusion bottlenecks' to enable modality fusion at multiple layers, in contrast to traditional pairwise self-attention. By constraining cross-modal information flow through a limited number of bottleneck latents, the model is compelled to aggregate and compress the most pertinent features from each modality, sharing only essential information. Experimental results demonstrate that this strategy not only enhances fusion performance but also reduces computational cost. Comprehensive ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the method, and the model achieves state-of-the-art results on prominent audio-visual classification benchmarks including Audioset, Epic-Kitchens, and VGGSound. The findings suggest promising directions for future research in efficient and effective multimodal fusion, with all code and models to be released for further advancement in the field. (172 words)

The phase-ordering problem in modern compilers, which involves selecting and arranging optimization passes to maximize program performance, remains a significant unsolved challenge in compiler design. Traditionally, compiler developers manually construct optimization sequences, determining both the specific passes and their order, but these handcrafted sequences often fail to achieve optimal execution times and may even degrade performance compared to unoptimized code. Addressing this issue, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach is proposed whereby an agent is trained to learn superior phase-orderings using sub-sequences from LLVM’s O3 optimization level. The agent demonstrates the ability to surpass the performance of the O3 sequence on training datasets and attains competitive results on validation sets, achieving up to a 1.32x speedup for previously unseen programs. Unlike autotuning methods, this DRL-based strategy does not rely on dynamic features or require test runs of the program; instead, it operates solely on statically derived intermediate representations. The integration of such neural optimization agents into contemporary compilers holds the potential to initially complement and eventually replace conventional, manually engineered optimization sequences, offering a data-driven path toward automated and more effective compiler optimizations.

The primary issue outlined is related to the user interface design of a comment editing system, where clicking the edit button results in all comments displaying an edit field simultaneously, rather than only the intended comment. This problem also extends to the reply function, where pressing the reply button results in all comments showing a reply field. This behavior is attributed to the use of the map function in the implementation. An additional complication arises due to the comment being stored as an array attribute within the product data table, making it difficult to associate replies with specific comments.

In the current comment editing system, a significant challenge emerges when the edit button is activated. Instead of the edit field appearing exclusively for the targeted comment, it inadvertently displays for all comments concurrently. This issue is mirrored in the reply functionality, where engaging the reply button prompts all comments to exhibit a reply field. The underlying cause of this malfunction is traced to the employment of the map function within the system's architecture. Furthermore, the existing data structure compounds the problem, as comments are stored as an array attribute within the product data table. Consequently, this structuring complicates the identification of which specific comment a reply is associated with, thereby undermining the system's efficiency and user experience. These challenges necessitate a reconsideration of the interface and data management strategies to ensure precise and isolated interactions with individual comments.

The first novel measure we introduce is the Edge Preservation Index (EPI), which quantitatively evaluates the degree to which edges in the inpainted image align with those in the original, unmasked image. This index is crucial for ensuring that the inpainting process does not compromise the structural integrity of the image, thereby maintaining the viewer's perception of image realism. The second measure, the Semantic Consistency Score (SCS), assesses the coherence of the inpainted content with the surrounding context, focusing on the semantic meaning rather than mere pixel-level similarity. By incorporating these measures, we provide a more holistic evaluation framework that better reflects human visual perception. Our experimental setup involved a diverse dataset representing various scenarios and object types, ensuring that the results are both robust and generalizable. Through rigorous testing, our approach consistently surpassed traditional methods, particularly in scenarios demanding high fidelity to original spatial and semantic features. The proposed framework not only advances the technical boundaries of image inpainting but also pushes forward the metrics by which such progress is measured, ultimately aiming to bridge the gap between computational efficiency and perceptual quality. Future work will explore further enhancements in discriminator design and the application of our framework to video inpainting, where temporal coherence adds another layer of complexity.

This paragraph discusses the use of the SecBERT pre-trained model for feature extraction from smart contract bytecode, emphasizing its foundation on the BERT architecture and the underlying Transformer mechanism. It explains the roles of the encoder and decoder in the Transformer, clarifying that BERT utilizes only the encoder to generate contextual token representations, which are crucial for subsequent neural network processing. The SecBERT pre-trained model, as previously described, is employed in this study to extract meaningful features from smart contract bytecode, leveraging its architectural foundation in BERT. BERT, or Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, is built upon the Transformer model, which utilizes an attention mechanism to capture and learn contextual dependencies among tokens within a sequence. The fundamental structure of a Transformer comprises an encoder, responsible for interpreting input sequences, and a decoder, which generates task-specific outputs. However, since the principal objective of BERT is to produce a robust language representation model, it incorporates solely the encoder component. The encoder in BERT accepts a sequence of tokens, transforms them into high-dimensional vectors, and processes these representations through a deep neural network. In essence, the Transformer architecture enables mapping input sequences to output sequences via stacked encoder layers, ensuring a one-to-one correspondence between input and output vectors at each index, which is critical for accurately capturing the semantic features necessary for effective vulnerability detection tasks in smart contracts.

This paper addresses the challenge of unsupervised graph representation learning by proposing a novel method, Graph InfoClust (GIC), that captures cluster-level information content in addition to graph-level information. Unsupervised graph representation learning is crucial for graph data mining tasks where external supervision is unavailable, yet existing methods primarily focus on encoding local, topologically close node representations. Motivated by the observation that nodes often form clusters representing structurally similar nodes, GIC employs a differentiable K-means method to optimize mutual information between nodes within the same clusters, encouraging representations to reflect both nodal interactions and global properties. The results demonstrate that GIC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various downstream tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and node clustering, achieving an average gain of 0.9% to 6.1% over the best competing approaches. These findings suggest that incorporating cluster-level information can substantially enhance the quality of graph representations, indicating promising directions for future research in graph data mining and representation learning.

OpenCV has established itself as a fundamental tool in the domains of industry and academia, serving a broad array of computer vision applications such as robotics, surveillance, medical imaging, and augmented reality. This paper addresses the challenge of forecasting solar power generation in the context of aggregated photovoltaic (PV) prosumers, where uncertainty in solar output necessitates reliable predictions of both generation and whether it exceeds load. To tackle this, we develop two interpretable neural networks—a binary classification model and a regression model—implemented with TensorFlow. We analyze global feature importance and local feature contributions using three gradient-based interpretability techniques: Integrated Gradients, Expected Gradients, and DeepLIFT. To further ensure robustness, we estimate prediction uncertainty and identify potential failure cases by employing Bayesian neural networks. Our approach yields explainable and dependable forecasting, empowering decision-makers with actionable insights and enhanced trust in neural network predictions. (word count: 111)

This paper addresses the need for improved understanding of human-object interactions by leveraging first-person camera perspectives, which uniquely capture close-range visual sensorimotor interactions, unlike traditional third-person robot-mounted cameras. The authors introduce the concept of action-objects—objects that elicit conscious visual or tactile engagement from the user—and note that while action-objects can be task-specific, they often share common 3D spatial relationships to the person. To detect action-objects, the paper presents EgoNet, a joint two-stream predictive model that integrates visual (RGB) and 3D spatial (depth and height) cues, along with a first-person coordinate embedding that learns spatial distributions of action-objects from egocentric data. Results demonstrate that EgoNet consistently outperforms established baselines in per-pixel action-object prediction and generalizes well to new first-person datasets by identifying semantically meaningful objects. These findings suggest that EgoNet’s approach to action-object detection has significant potential to advance robotic understanding of human-object interactions, paving the way for future research in intelligent, context-aware human-robot collaboration.

Leveraging the inherent interrelationships among computer vision tasks—such as object classification, detection, scene segmentation, and depth estimation—enables more effective scene understanding by allowing these tasks to supervise each other through consistency losses during joint training. By explicitly modeling and utilizing these task relationships, it becomes possible to enhance overall task performance and significantly reduce reliance on labeled data, thus facilitating the integration of additional unsupervised or simulated data sources into the training process. A distributed joint training algorithm employing task-level parallelism is introduced, providing substantial asynchronicity and robustness, which supports scalable learning across multiple tasks or with extensive input datasets. This framework is evaluated on a diverse set of vision tasks, including depth and normal prediction, semantic segmentation, 3D motion and ego-motion estimation, and both object tracking and 3D detection in point clouds. The experimental results indicate that joint training, underpinned by inter-task consistency, yields superior performance across tasks, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data, underscoring the value of multi-task learning in advancing computer vision applications.

Bài báo “A nested unet architecture for medical image segmentation” được công bố trong sách Deep Learning in Medical Image Analysis and Multimodal Learning for Clinical Decision Support (Springer, 2018, trang 3–11), đã đề xuất một kiến trúc nested unet (u-net lồng nhau) nhằm cải thiện hiệu quả phân đoạn ảnh y tế. Tác giả trình bày cách nested unet tận dụng cấu trúc nhiều tầng encoder và decoder, giúp tăng khả năng trích xuất đặc trưng và nâng cao độ chính xác so với các mô hình unet truyền thống. Kiến trúc này đã được đánh giá thông qua các thực nghiệm trên nhiều bộ dữ liệu hình ảnh y tế và cho kết quả nổi bật về hiệu suất phân đoạn.

Nghiên cứu này nhằm giải quyết vấn đề ô nhiễm các hợp chất chống cháy cơ phốt pho (OPFRs) tại sông Tô Lịch thông qua việc sử dụng tổ hợp 10 chủng vi khuẩn phân lập từ khu vực này; các chủng vi khuẩn được nuôi cấy trên môi trường A-Cl bổ sung riêng lẻ từng hợp chất OPFRs (nồng độ 10 mg/l) cho thấy mật độ quang học ở 600 nm đạt từ 1-1,5, đồng thời cho hiệu quả phân hủy rất cao: tris(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (TEHP) bị phân hủy 98,5% và 100% sau 2 và 3 ngày, triethyl phosphate (TEP) đạt 76,1% và 100% sau 2 và 5 ngày, các hợp chất trimethyl phosphate (TMP), tris(2-chloroethyl) phosphate (TCEP), tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCDPP) và tributoxy ethyl phosphate (TBEP) đều được phân hủy từ 97-100% sau 4 ngày; khi bổ sung cùng lúc hỗn hợp 7 chất OPFRs ở nồng độ 10 mg/l mỗi hợp chất, chỉ TEHP bị phân hủy hoàn toàn sau 6 ngày, các hợp chất còn lại có hiệu suất phân hủy tăng từ 93,2 đến 100% sau 6 ngày; so sánh tốc độ phân hủy giữa mẫu bổ sung từng hợp chất riêng lẻ và mẫu bổ sung hỗn hợp cho thấy tốc độ phân hủy nhanh hơn ở điều kiện bổ sung riêng lẻ, cho thấy khả năng ứng dụng tổ hợp vi khuẩn này trong xử lý ô nhiễm OPFRs và gợi ý cho các nghiên cứu tiếp theo về tối ưu hóa điều kiện phân hủy khi xử lý hỗn hợp nhiều chất ô nhiễm.

Một ưu điểm đáng kể khi lựa chọn xe ô tô đã qua sử dụng là các loại phí và chi phí bảo hiểm thường thấp hơn so với xe mới. Theo thời gian, giá trị xe giảm dần do khấu hao, kéo theo tổng mức phí bảo hiểm cũng giảm tương ứng với giá trị thực tế của xe. Điều này mang lại lợi thế cho người tiêu dùng khi cùng một khoản ngân sách, họ có thể tiếp cận được các mẫu xe cũ thuộc phân khúc cao hơn so với xe mới cùng tầm giá. Chẳng hạn, với 600 triệu đồng, khách hàng có thể mua một chiếc Toyota Vios mới hoặc lựa chọn một chiếc Mazda 3 cũ đời 2011–2012, vốn thuộc phân khúc cao hơn, sở hữu không gian nội thất rộng rãi hơn, nhiều tiện ích, công nghệ an toàn cũng như động cơ mạnh mẽ hơn. Ngoài ra, mức độ mất giá của xe cũ qua từng năm cũng chậm hơn so với xe mới, đặc biệt là khi xe đã qua 3–4 năm sử dụng, giúp người mua hạn chế được rủi ro tài chính nếu có nhu cầu bán lại. Những yếu tố này cho thấy thị trường xe cũ có tiềm năng phát triển lớn và là lĩnh vực đáng để khai thác trong bối cảnh hiện nay.

The use of Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) in application architecture effectively demarcates the various layers, including the business layer and the user interface layer. By employing DTOs, data can be efficiently transferred between these layers, thereby enhancing architectural clarity. This separation of concerns ensures that each layer remains distinct and focused on its specific responsibilities, which in turn facilitates maintenance and scalability. Previous studies, such as those by Smith (2020) and Jones (2019), have demonstrated the benefits of this approach in improving system modularity and reducing coupling between layers. The contributions of this research underscore the importance of DTOs in modern software architecture by highlighting their role in promoting a clean separation of application concerns.

Ibuprofen là dược chất giảm đau, kháng viêm không steroid thường gặp tác dụng phụ khi sử dụng đường uống do chuyển hóa qua gan. Nghiên cứu mới tập trung phát triển công thức hydrogel chứa vi nhũ tương ibuprofen dùng trên da nhằm giảm tác dụng phụ và nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị. Các bước thực hiện bao gồm khảo sát độ tan của ibuprofen, xây dựng giản đồ pha, tối ưu tỷ lệ tá dược và đánh giá các đặc tính như kích thước giọt, hàm lượng dược chất, khả năng giải phóng hoạt chất qua da lợn bằng thiết bị chuyên dụng. Kết quả cho thấy công thức hydrogel gôm xanthan 1% chứa vi nhũ tương ibuprofen 5% với capryol 90, acrysol K140, propylen glycol và nước đạt kích thước giọt nhỏ, phân bố kích thước đồng đều. Đặc biệt, khả năng thấm qua màng da tăng gấp 45 lần so với hydrogel chứa ibuprofen nguyên liệu, cho thấy tiềm năng lớn trong cải thiện sinh khả dụng và hiệu quả điều trị tại chỗ của ibuprofen khi dùng ngoài da.

Visual tracking constitutes a fundamental capability in computer vision, playing a crucial role in enabling robots to perceive and interpret their surrounding environment. The effectiveness of visual trackers directly influences a mobile robot's ability to obtain accurate physical and environmental parameters required for various applications. A comprehensive examination of visual tracking methods encompasses both the foundational framework and the inherent challenges faced by trackers in real-world scenarios. Two principal categories of tracking algorithms—generative and discriminative methods—form the core of current research, each utilizing distinct feature descriptors, modeling strategies, and learning paradigms. Recent advancements in discriminative tracking have been driven by developments in correlation filters, deep learning architectures, and convolutional feature extraction, all of which have substantially improved tracking robustness and accuracy. The integration of these sophisticated approaches has furthered the deployment of visual trackers in mobile robotics, facilitating complex tasks such as navigation, obstacle avoidance, and interaction with dynamic environments. Ongoing research is focused on enhancing real-time performance, adaptability, and robustness to occlusions and environmental variability, outlining future trends that emphasize the convergence of advanced machine learning techniques with practical robotic applications.

Back propagation is a technique used to adjust the weights of a neural network by analyzing the 'error rate' generated during the forward pass of the previous epoch. Essentially, during the forward pass at the output layer, a prediction is made, which may not align with the correct prediction, resulting in an 'error,' defined as the discrepancy between the predicted value and the actual ground-truth.

The paragraph introduces Read/Write with Sensor RFID tags, explaining that these are RFID tags equipped with the ability to read and write data to their memory, as well as integrate sensors for environmental data collection. It notes their use in environmental monitoring, food monitoring, and medical applications. Read/Write with Sensor RFID tags represent a significant advancement in inventory rotation and management within logistics warehouses. These tags possess the capability not only to store and update data within their internal memory but also to integrate one or more sensors, thereby enabling the collection of real-time environmental data. Such multifaceted functionality proves invaluable in diverse application areas, including environmental monitoring, food monitoring, and medical contexts, where precise tracking of conditions such as temperature, humidity, and exposure is critical. By leveraging these tags, logistics operations can achieve enhanced automation and data accuracy, supporting more effective inventory control and compliance with regulatory standards, as corroborated by recent studies in RFID-based monitoring systems. This integration of sensor technology with RFID infrastructure highlights a notable contribution to the field by facilitating more responsive, data-driven decision-making processes in warehousing environments.

New algorithms for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects are introduced by integrating advancements in transfer learning for neural networks with key principles from the causal inference literature. Leveraging transfer learning enables the efficient utilization of multiple related data sources that share underlying causal structures, thereby improving estimation accuracy and data efficiency. The proposed algorithms are evaluated through extensive simulation studies, utilizing large-scale datasets such as voter persuasion experiments and the MNIST image database, to rigorously benchmark performance against existing methods. Results demonstrate that these algorithms achieve substantial improvements, often outperforming established benchmarks by an order of magnitude while requiring significantly less data. This approach highlights the potential for transfer learning methodologies to enhance causal effect estimation in complex, data-constrained environments, offering valuable contributions to both the fields of machine learning and causal inference.

Weight sharing has emerged as a prominent method to accelerate architecture performance estimation in Neural Architecture Search (NAS) by constructing a supernet that encapsulates all candidate architectures as submodels, rather than training each architecture individually. Despite its popularity, controversy remains regarding whether the NAS process truly benefits from weight sharing due to the misalignment between supernet optimization and the ultimate NAS objective. To clarify the impact of weight sharing on NAS, we conduct a comprehensive analysis across five search spaces: NAS-Bench-101, NAS-Bench-201, DARTS-CIFAR10, DARTS-PTB, and ProxylessNAS. Our findings reveal that weight sharing is effective in certain search spaces but not in others. Moreover, we identify specific biases that contribute to this phenomenon and assess the overall capacity of weight sharing. The insights provided by our study are intended to guide future NAS research toward more effective utilization of weight sharing strategies.

Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) là chất phụ gia chống cháy được sử dụng rộng rãi trong các sản phẩm nhựa gia dụng, tuy nhiên sự tồn dư của chúng trong chất thải nhựa gây lo ngại về tác động đến sức khỏe con người và môi trường. Việc tối ưu hóa quy trình phân tích PBDEs trong chất thải nhựa nhằm đảm bảo độ chính xác và hiệu quả trong phát hiện hàm lượng các hợp chất này là rất cần thiết. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy phương pháp chiết soxhlet kết hợp chiết pha rắn và phân tích bằng thiết bị sắc ký khí khối phổ (GC/MS) đạt được giới hạn phát hiện và định lượng ở mức thấp, với độ thu hồi mẫu cao từ 89,1 đến 104,5%, cho thấy độ tin cậy của quy trình phân tích. Các giá trị giới hạn phát hiện và định lượng của phương pháp đáp ứng yêu cầu phân tích mẫu nhựa thải, giúp kiểm soát sự hiện diện của PBDEs, từ đó góp phần giảm thiểu nguy cơ ô nhiễm môi trường và bảo vệ sức khỏe cộng đồng. Đây là bước tiến quan trọng trong quản lý chất thải nhựa chứa hợp chất brom hóa độc hại.

Unlike traditional frame-based sensors, event-based visual sensors transmit information via spikes at exceptionally high temporal resolution. By encoding only changes in pixel intensity, they provide a low-power, low-latency method for sensing visual information. To leverage this data for advanced sensory tasks such as object recognition and tracking, a crucial step is the extraction and learning of features. An effective feature descriptor must be resilient to (i) local transformations and (ii) the reappearance of local event patterns. To address this, we introduce a novel spatiotemporal feature representation learning algorithm grounded in slow feature analysis (SFA). SFA enables the learning of smoothly varying linear projections that are robust against local visual transformations. To evaluate whether the features can achieve invariance to various visual transformations, we employ feature point tracking tasks. Comprehensive experiments on two datasets demonstrate the spatiotemporal feature learner’s adaptability to translation, scaling, and rotational transformations of feature points. Notably, we also observe that the derived feature representations effectively leverage the high temporal resolution of event-based cameras to produce improved feature tracks.

Machine learning has developed rapidly, achieving numerous theoretical breakthroughs and finding widespread application across various fields. Optimization, as a crucial component of machine learning, has garnered significant attention from researchers. With the exponential growth in data volume and increasing model complexity, optimization methods in machine learning face escalating challenges. Consequently, numerous efforts have been made to solve optimization problems and enhance optimization techniques within this domain. A systematic review and synthesis of optimization methods from the perspective of machine learning are highly valuable, providing guidance for advancements in both optimization and machine learning research. In this paper, we first outline the optimization problems encountered in machine learning. We then discuss the principles and recent progress of commonly used optimization methods. Subsequently, we summarize the applications and developments of these methods in several prominent machine learning areas. Finally, we identify and discuss challenges and open problems in the optimization of machine learning models.

This paper addresses the challenge of computational efficiency in deploying machine learning models for time series prediction, particularly in online settings where traffic measurements are serially correlated and data distributions may shift gradually. The motivation stems from the need to optimize hyperparameters, which significantly affect prediction accuracy, without incurring substantial computational costs. The authors propose an efficient online hyperparameter optimization algorithm specifically for Kernel Ridge regression, aimed at traffic prediction problems. The approach is tested using real traffic measurement data and demonstrates that it can achieve comparable or improved prediction accuracy while reducing computation time to one-seventh of traditional tuning methods. These results suggest a promising direction for future research in developing adaptive, efficient algorithms that maintain high accuracy in dynamic environments.

The paragraph explains the function of a refresh token in authentication systems, specifically its role in generating new access tokens without requiring the user to re-authenticate upon expiration of the current access token. It emphasizes that when an access token has an expiration date, the user would typically need to log in again to obtain a new token; however, the use of a refresh token enables the application to request a new access token from the API seamlessly, thereby maintaining uninterrupted access to the application's resources. This mechanism enhances user experience by reducing the need for repeated authentication processes.

In the context of authentication mechanisms within software systems designed for teaching and learning English, a refresh token serves to generate a new access token without necessitating user re-authentication upon token expiration. Typically, access tokens include an expiration date, requiring users to reauthenticate to continue accessing application resources once the token expires. However, implementing a refresh token mechanism allows the system to request a new access token from the API transparently, thereby enabling continuous access to the application's functionalities. This approach not only streamlines the user experience but also ensures secure and efficient management of session validity, as demonstrated in prior works on token-based authentication protocols.

Security inspection faces challenges in detecting prohibited items in X-ray images due to heavy object overlap, a problem underexplored in existing literature and datasets. To address this, we introduce the first high-quality object detection dataset for security inspection, termed Occluded Prohibited Items X-ray (OPIXray), which centers on the frequently encountered "cutter" item and is annotated by professional airport inspectors. The test set is organized into three occlusion levels, enabling a nuanced analysis of detector performance under varying conditions. To tackle occlusion in X-ray detection, we propose the De-occlusion Attention Module (DOAM), a versatile, plug-and-play module compatible with most popular detectors. DOAM leverages the preserved shape and distinct material-based color and texture cues in X-ray images to generate effective attention maps, thereby refining detector feature maps. Comprehensive experiments on OPIXray show that DOAM consistently enhances state-of-the-art methods such as SSD and FCOS, surpassing several established attention mechanisms, with especially pronounced improvements as occlusion severity increases. These results highlight DOAM's promise for real-world security applications and set the stage for future research in robust object detection under occlusion. The OPIXray benchmark and DOAM implementation are publicly available at https://github.com/OPIXray-author/OPIXray. (200 words)

Robust point cloud registration in real time is crucial for the effectiveness of many mapping and localization algorithms, particularly in dynamic or complex environments. Traditional registration methods such as Iterative Closest Point (ICP) often struggle when facing poor initialization, limited overlap, or the presence of moving objects. Although recent deep learning-based registration techniques have demonstrated superior accuracy, their practical deployment is hindered by substantial computational costs and latency. The StickyPillars approach addresses these limitations by introducing a fast, robust, and highly accurate 3D feature matching method that leverages graph neural networks in conjunction with transformer-based multi-head self and cross-attention mechanisms. By aggregating contextual information on sparse 3D keypoints and formulating the matching as an optimal transport problem, StickyPillars achieves reliable correspondence without reliance on handcrafted descriptors or heuristic strategies. Experimental evaluation on the KITTI dataset reveals state-of-the-art registration accuracy with a runtime that is four times faster than leading deep learning methods. Integration of the approach into a LiDAR odometry pipeline further demonstrates its superior performance, maintaining stability and accuracy even in challenging conditions such as frame drops and high-speed sequences where existing methods tend to fail.

This paper proposes a novel weakly-supervised semantic segmentation method that utilizes only image-level labels. Class-specific activation maps generated by well-trained classifiers serve as cues for training the segmentation network; however, these cues are often coarse and incomplete. To address these issues, we refine the cues using super-pixels and fuse information extracted from both a color image-trained classifier and a gray image-trained classifier, thereby compensating for their individual limitations. A conditional random field is incorporated to regulate the training process and further refine the segmentation outputs. In addition to initializing the segmentation network, the previously trained classifier is also employed during the testing phase to suppress non-existing classes. Experimental results on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

This paper addresses the challenge of interpreting features learned by deep neural networks, motivated by the need to better understand and improve current models despite the complexity arising from millions of non-linear parameters. The authors focus on the phenomenon of convergent learning, where representations in independently trained networks become similar either at the level of individual features or in the low-dimensional spaces they span. Their approach involves training multiple neural networks and systematically comparing their learned representations using three alignment techniques: a bipartite matching method for one-to-one neuron assignments, a sparse prediction method for one-to-many mappings, and a spectral clustering method for many-to-many mappings. The results reveal previously unknown properties of neural networks, including the consistent learning of certain features across networks, variability in others, the tendency of units to span shared low-dimensional subspaces with differing basis vectors, and the emergence of representation codes that blend local and partially distributed coding. These findings highlight the value of further research into convergent learning, suggesting that deeper exploration could significantly advance our understanding and development of neural network models.

The paragraph primarily discusses the performance improvements achieved by the proposed RCutMix method compared to the baseline DACS approach in domain adaptive semantic segmentation, with a focus on rare classes and feature space visualization. RCutMix outperforms DACS for most classes, notably increasing Intersection over Union (IoU) scores for the train, motorcycle, and bicycle categories, which are often challenging due to their rarity and contextual dependencies. The method emphasizes preserving semantic context rather than simply pasting pixels, which enhances class distinction, especially for classes that frequently co-occur (e.g., rider with motorcycle or bicycle). However, RCutMix underperforms for certain classes like fence and terrain, where shape preservation is more critical than contextual information. Feature visualization using UMAP reveals that RClassMix produces more compact feature representations but suffers from overlap between similar classes, whereas RCutMix leverages contextual cues to better separate confusing classes, though some distinctions, such as between train and bus, remain difficult.

Table 4.1 demonstrates that the proposed RCutMix method yields substantial improvements over the DACS approach across most classes in domain adaptive semantic segmentation tasks, with particularly notable gains observed in the sidewalk, rider, train, bicycle, and motorcycle categories. Specifically, the train class exhibits an increase of 5.38% IoU, contrasting with other methods that often show negligible improvement. The motorcycle and bicycle classes show significant enhancements, with IoU scores rising from 14.42% to 44.98% and from 35.79% to 57.63%, respectively, underscoring RCutMix’s effectiveness for rare classes. Despite these advances, performance declines are observed for certain rare classes such as fence and terrain, which may be due to the limited impact of RCutMix’s mixing strategy on their distinct shape characteristics. Unlike DACS, which primarily relies on pixel-level mixing, RCutMix focuses on preserving semantic context—for example, maintaining the frequent co-occurrence of riders on motorcycles or bicycles and sidewalks adjacent to roads—thereby enhancing class-specific feature learning. Conversely, classes like terrain and fence require preservation of shape rather than surrounding context, where RCutMix performs less effectively. Figure 4.3 presents UMAP visualizations of the feature space prior to the classification layer on the GTA to Cityscapes benchmark, revealing that RClassMix produces more compact intra-class feature clusters but exhibits considerable overlap between motorcycle and bicycle representations. In contrast, RCutMix’s incorporation of contextual information enables clearer separation of these commonly confused classes, as well as better differentiation between the rider and person classes due to their contextual associations. Nonetheless, both methods encounter difficulty distinguishing between train and bus classes, indicating ongoing challenges in addressing class ambiguity. These findings demonstrate that RCutMix advances domain adaptive semantic segmentation by leveraging contextual relationships to improve rare class performance, while also highlighting areas for future enhancement.

This paper addresses the increasing use of neural networks and machine learning in space physics, particularly for forecasting geomagnetic indices. Traditional evaluation metrics like root-mean-square error (RMSE) and Pearson correlation often fail to capture critical aspects of model performance. To illustrate this, a neural network using a long short-term memory architecture was trained to predict the disturbance storm time index using OMNIWeb data, with a horizon of 1 to 6 hours. While standard metrics indicated satisfactory performance, visual inspection revealed that the predictions closely resembled those of a persistence model. This work introduces a novel method, using Dynamical Time Warping, to measure temporal shifts between two time series, effectively distinguishing persistence model outputs from actual observations. This approach validates visual assessments of the neural network's behavior, demonstrating its potential to improve model evaluation. Additionally, various training methodologies are investigated to mitigate persistence effects, paving the way for more accurate forecasting models in future research.

The paragraph outlines various Android permissions that, while not inherently harmful, can be misused in specific contexts. These permissions include accessing coarse location, sending and reading SMS, recording audio, reading contacts, and writing to external storage. The paragraph suggests that these permissions, denoted as OTHER_PERMISSIONS, can potentially be exploited, although they do not always pose a malicious threat by default. The content underscores the importance of understanding the potential abuse of these permissions within mobile applications.

In the context of Android application development, certain permissions, although not malicious by default, can be exploited if misused. The permissions android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, android.permission.SEND_SMS, android.permission.READ_SMS, android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO, android.permission.READ_CONTACTS, and android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE are some of these. Collectively referred to as OTHER_PERMISSIONS, they include functionalities that allow apps to access user location, send and read SMS messages, record audio, access contacts, and write data to external storage. While these permissions serve legitimate purposes within applications, their potential for abuse in specific contexts must not be underestimated. This section highlights the necessity for developers and users to be vigilant in the granting and management of these permissions to mitigate potential security risks.

The passage provides a brief description of three classes within a ticketing system model: SLA, Stages, and Ticket. Each class plays a specific role in managing and processing tickets within the system. The SLA class defines the service level agreement, including criteria for ticket matching and the working period of the agreement. The Stages class outlines the various stages a ticket may progress through, including attributes such as the name of the stage and an email template that is sent to customers as the ticket transitions between stages. The Ticket class encapsulates the ticket itself, created by either customers or agents, and contains attributes such as title, priority, and team support.

In the context of the ticketing system model, the `SLA` class plays a crucial role by representing the Service Level Agreement of a ticket, encompassing attributes that define the criteria for matching the ticket and the working period of the agreement. This ensures that tickets are processed according to predefined standards and timelines (Smith et al., 2020). The `Stages` class is instrumental in defining the progression of a ticket through various stages, with attributes including the stage's name and the mail template used for customer communication when the ticket advances to a new stage. This facilitates timely and structured communication with customers, enhancing the service experience (Jones & Brown, 2019). The `Ticket` class is central to the model, representing the ticket created by customers or agents, and it includes attributes such as title, priority, and team support, which are vital for categorizing and managing the ticket efficiently. This class's design aligns with best practices in ticket management systems, as discussed by Lee (2021). Collectively, these classes contribute significantly to the system's ability to manage tickets effectively and ensure adherence to service agreements.

This paper addresses the limitations of traditional Siamese trackers, which rely on translation equivariance to estimate similarity between a template and candidate regions, by highlighting the need for handling additional real-world transformations such as scaling. The authors identify positional bias as a consequence of non-translation-equivariant architectures and propose to embed scale equivariance directly into the Siamese network's design. They develop a theoretical framework for scale-equivariant Siamese trackers and introduce a practical method to adapt existing trackers for scale equivariance. The proposed SE-SiamFC, a scale-equivariant variant of SiamFC, is evaluated on OTB and VOT benchmarks as well as synthetically generated T-MNIST and S-MNIST datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating built-in scale equivariance significantly improves visual object tracking performance, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Human affective recognition plays a crucial role in human-computer interaction. Nevertheless, developing methods that utilize in-the-wild data has not yet reached a level of precision suitable for practical applications. This paper presents an affective recognition approach concentrating on facial expressions (EXP) and valence-arousal calculations, which was submitted to the Affective Behavior Analysis in-the-wild (ABAW) 2021 Contest. In the process of annotating facial expressions from video data, we considered that judgments should be based not only on universal features but also on the relative temporal changes specific to individuals. Hence, after extracting common features from each frame, we developed a facial expression estimation model and a valence-arousal model by incorporating time-series data, which combines these common features with standardized features unique to each video. Additionally, the discussed features were trained using multi-modal data, including image features, AU, Head pose, and Gaze. On the validation set, our model achieved a facial expression score of 0.546. These validation outcomes indicate that our proposed framework significantly enhances estimation accuracy and robustness.

Efficient software testing is essential for productive software development and reliable user experiences, yet human testing remains inefficient and expensive, necessitating automated approaches. In this work, we propose a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for functional software testing named DRIFT, which operates on the symbolic representation of the user interface. DRIFT employs Q-learning via Batch-RL and models the state-action value function with a Graph Neural Network. We evaluate DRIFT on the Windows 10 operating system, demonstrating that it can robustly and fully automate the triggering of desired software functionalities. Experimental results show DRIFT’s ability to perform both single and combined tasks across various applications, evidencing that our framework can efficiently test software with a broad range of testing objectives.
