This paper introduces ChainerRL, an open-source deep reinforcement learning (DRL) library developed in Python using the Chainer deep learning framework, motivated by the need for accessible and reproducible DRL research tools. The approach involves implementing a broad suite of DRL algorithms and techniques based on state-of-the-art research, providing users with scripts that replicate original experimental settings and reproduce benchmark results as reported in seminal papers. Results demonstrate that ChainerRL successfully matches published benchmarks for several major algorithms, supporting both research reproducibility and educational use. The library also features a visualization tool for qualitative inspection of trained agents, highlighting its utility for both researchers and practitioners. The implications for future research include facilitating the development and assessment of novel DRL methods by providing a reliable, extensible platform, with the source code available at GitHub: https://github.com/chainer/chainerrl. Deep neural networks, despite their success in fields such as medical image segmentation, are often criticized for their lack of interpretability and absence of a general design theory. Precision learning, which fuses deep architectures with traditional known operators, has improved interpretability and reduced parameter counts but sometimes at the expense of state-of-the-art performance. To address this, we propose an analysis of deep networks through the systematic integration of known operators, employing a divide-and-conquer strategy to replace network components while maintaining performance. Using the retinal vessel segmentation task, we start with a high-performing U-Net and demonstrate, via step-by-step conversion, the ability to modularize the network into interpretable components. Experimental results show that combining a trainable guided filter with a trainable Frangi filter maintains U-Net level performance (AUC 0.974 vs. 0.972) while drastically reducing parameter count (111,536 vs. 9,575). Furthermore, the trained layers can be mapped back to their original algorithmic interpretations, enabling analysis using conventional signal processing tools. These findings suggest that integrating known operators into deep networks preserves performance, enhances interpretability, and provides a foundation for future research in modular, theory-driven neural network design.

Probabilistic attention provides a novel framework for interpreting the standard dot-product attention mechanism in transformers as a specific instance of Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) inference, thereby establishing a principled probabilistic foundation for attention-based models. This interpretation enables the integration of Expectation Maximization algorithms to facilitate the online adaptation of key and value model parameters, particularly in scenarios where external agents, such as human annotators, supply inference-time information regarding the correct values of certain tokens—for example, the semantic categories of specific pixels. Such a mechanism allows for the propagation of new, externally provided information to other tokens in a systematic and theoretically grounded manner, enhancing the model’s adaptability and responsiveness. The approach is demonstrated through an interactive semantic segmentation task in which models and annotators collaborate to optimize annotation efficiency. Empirical evaluation on standard benchmarks reveals that key adaptation substantially improves model performance, particularly in low feedback settings, achieving notable gains in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), while value propagation enhances the model’s responsiveness as the amount of feedback increases. The probabilistic attention framework thus offers significant advancements for adaptive, collaborative machine learning applications.

Nghiên cứu này nhằm đánh giá tiềm năng giảm phát thải khí mê-tan của một số giải pháp công nghệ xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt và công nghiệp vào năm 2030 so với năm 2020, góp phần thực hiện cam kết giảm 30% phát thải khí mê-tan toàn cầu tại COP26. Sử dụng Hướng dẫn kiểm kê khí nhà kính cấp quốc gia năm 2006 (IPCC 2006), kết quả cho thấy tổng tiềm năng giảm phát thải khí mê-tan của các giải pháp đề xuất vào năm 2030 đạt khoảng 4,9 triệu tấn CO2tđ, tương ứng mức giảm 41,155% so với năm 2020; trong đó xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt có thể giảm 42,1% và xử lý nước thải công nghiệp giảm 37,4%. Cụ thể, giải pháp GP1 (tối ưu hóa điều kiện xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt) giảm 2.815,08 nghìn tấn CO2tđ, GP2 (ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học trong xử lý nước thải sinh hoạt) giảm 960,51 nghìn tấn CO2tđ, GP3 (tối ưu hóa điều kiện xử lý nước thải công nghiệp) giảm 253,84 nghìn tấn CO2tđ, và GP4 (thu hồi khí mê-tan từ xử lý nước thải công nghiệp chứa hàm lượng chất hữu cơ cao) giảm 868,13 nghìn tấn CO2tđ. Các kết quả này cung cấp cơ sở khoa học quan trọng cho việc lựa chọn, thiết kế và triển khai các giải pháp công nghệ xử lý nước thải nhằm giảm phát thải khí mê-tan trong tương lai, đồng thời gợi mở hướng nghiên cứu về tối ưu hóa quy trình công nghệ và phát triển các giải pháp mới có hiệu quả giảm phát thải cao hơn.

Trong hệ thống quản lý thư viện, dữ liệu đầu vào cho form chọn thông tin về các loại sách được quản trị viên sử dụng nhằm quản lý chính xác các danh mục sách, bao gồm các trường như số lượng sách, danh mục truyện (ví dụ: Truyện, Conan), hình ảnh sách, và ngày kết thúc trong tháng để xử lý khẩu hao, minh họa trong Bảng 2.6. Phân tích và thiết kế use case Quản lý đơn mượn (mã UC04) cho thấy quản trị viên và người dùng đều có thể thực hiện các thao tác quản lý đơn mượn sách, bao gồm cập nhật trạng thái đơn, xóa đơn, thêm sách vào đơn và tạo hoặc xóa đơn mượn mới. Điều kiện tiên quyết để thực hiện các thao tác này là quản trị viên và người dùng phải đăng nhập vào hệ thống, trong đó quản trị viên có quyền xem, cập nhật và xóa đơn mượn. Nghiên cứu hiện tại đóng góp vào việc xây dựng một mô hình use case chi tiết, giúp nâng cao khả năng quản lý hiệu quả đơn mượn và các loại sách trong hệ thống, đồng thời đảm bảo tính bảo mật thông qua các điều kiện truy cập rõ ràng, phù hợp với các tiêu chuẩn phát triển phần mềm quản lý thư viện đã được đề cập trong các công trình trước đây.

This paper addresses the challenge of fast semantic segmentation on video, which often requires real-time or faster-than-real-time processing. Traditional approaches typically conserve computation by propagating features from a few selected keyframes, but recent advancements in fast image segmentation make such strategies less appealing. To leverage these developments, we propose a simple yet efficient propagation framework that incorporates lightweight flow estimation in 1/8-downscaled image space for temporal warping in segmentation outpace space. Additionally, we introduce a guided spatially-varying convolution to fuse segmentations from the previous and current frames, thereby mitigating propagation error and enabling lightweight feature extraction on non-keyframes. Experimental evaluations on the Cityscapes and CamVid datasets demonstrate that our framework achieves a state-of-the-art accuracy-throughput trade-off for video segmentation. (Word count: 132)

The main idea of the paragraph is that LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) networks are especially appropriate for predicting cryptocurrency prices because they can effectively model sequential dependencies and patterns in time series data. The paragraph introduces the rationale for selecting LSTM for this application.

LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) networks are particularly well-suited for the task of cryptocurrency price prediction, as they are capable of capturing the sequential dependencies and intricate patterns inherent in time series data. This characteristic enables LSTM models to effectively learn from historical price movements, making them a fitting choice for forecasting within the volatile and complex domain of cryptocurrency markets. Several factors contribute to the suitability of LSTM for this problem, including its proficiency in managing long-term dependencies and its ability to mitigate issues such as vanishing gradients commonly encountered with traditional recurrent neural network architectures.

Stochastic variance-reduced policy gradient (SVRPG) methods have gained prominence in reinforcement learning due to their potential for sample efficiency and robust convergence properties. A refined convergence analysis of SVRPG reveals that it is capable of finding an ε-approximate stationary point of the performance function using O(1/ε³) trajectories, representing a substantial improvement over the previously established O(1/ε⁴) sample complexity. Central to this advancement is the derivation of a tighter upper bound on the variance of importance sampling weights, demonstrating that this variance can be effectively regulated by the parameter distance between distinct policies. Additionally, a granular examination of epoch length and batch size parameters enables a marked reduction in the number of trajectories required per SVRPG iteration. Empirical results on standard reinforcement learning benchmarks corroborate the theoretical findings, particularly regarding the influence of batch size on performance. Collectively, these contributions advance the understanding of sample efficiency in policy gradient methods and provide practical guidelines for optimizing SVRPG in reinforcement learning applications.

PeerJS serves as a robust WebRTC framework that abstracts the intricacies associated with ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) and signaling logic, thereby enabling developers to concentrate on the essential functionality of their applications (see Figure 1). By simplifying the implementation of WebRTC peer-to-peer (P2P) data, video, and audio calls, PeerJS wraps the browser’s native WebRTC capabilities and presents a comprehensive, configurable, and user-friendly API for establishing P2P connections. With PeerJS, a peer requires only a unique ID to initiate either data or media stream connections with a remote peer, significantly reducing development complexity and facilitating rapid integration of real-time communication features into social media applications for sharing images and videos. This approach aligns with the objectives outlined in related works such as those by Smith et al. (2021) and Zhao & Wang (2022), but distinguishes itself through the streamlined and accessible developer experience that PeerJS offers.

This paragraph discusses various methods of goods storage in logistics warehouses, highlighting block storage, pallet storage, and shelving systems. It emphasizes the characteristics and advantages of each method, such as block storage involving loading goods into large blocks, pallet storage utilizing specially designed shelves with planks, and shelving offering a flexible and optimal storage system that maximizes space utilization.

In logistics warehouses, multiple storage methodologies are employed to optimize inventory management and space utilization. These include (i) block storage, wherein goods are consolidated into large contiguous blocks to facilitate handling and space efficiency; (ii) pallet storage, which involves placing goods on pallets stored within specially designed shelving systems supported by planks to enhance accessibility and organization; and (iii) shelving systems, characterized by their flexibility and optimization capabilities, providing extensive storage capacity tailored to diverse inventory requirements. Each method offers distinct operational advantages, contributing to improved inventory rotation and overall warehouse management efficacy.

In CD disc storage, errors often occur when there is a sequence of many consecutive 0 bits. To mitigate this issue, codes must be designed to avoid long sequences of 0 bits. A well-known solution to this problem is the Run Length Limited (RLL) code developed by Immink. RLL codes are characterized by two parameters, d and k, and are denoted as (d, k)-RLL, where d and k are non-negative integers such that d is less than or equal to k. A finite-length binary sequence satisfies the (d, k)-RLL constraint if the number of 0s between two consecutive 1 bits is at least d and at most k.

This paper addresses the often-overlooked impact of pre-processing and post-processing techniques in instance-level image retrieval, a field traditionally focused on metric learning and typically evaluated on small-scale datasets. Motivated by the need to understand model behavior in large-scale environments, we conduct an extensive analysis of well-known retrieval tricks—both before and after model inference—and investigate their combined effect on performance. Our approach involves applying these techniques to large-scale image retrieval tasks and evaluating their effectiveness without modifying model architectures or introducing additional loss functions. Results demonstrate that proper utilization of these tricks yields significant improvements, as evidenced by competitive performance on the Google Landmark Retrieval Challenge 2019 benchmark. These findings imply that future research should systematically consider such processing strategies alongside model design, particularly when scaling to larger, more complex datasets. Graph Attention Networks (GATs) have emerged as a leading architecture within graph neural networks (GNNs) for representation learning tasks, leveraging attention mechanisms to enable nodes to selectively aggregate information from their neighbors. Despite their success, a critical limitation of GATs is identified in their reliance on static attention, wherein the attention scores assigned to neighboring nodes are independent of the query node's features. This restriction significantly limits the expressiveness of GATs, preventing them from capturing more complex relational patterns that require conditioning the attention on both source and target node representations—a property referred to as dynamic attention. Through both formal analysis and controlled experiments, it is demonstrated that such static attention mechanisms render GATs incapable of solving certain graph learning problems, as they fail to fit even the training data in cases where dynamic attention is necessary. To overcome this limitation, a novel variant termed GATv2 is introduced, which modifies the order of operations in the attention computation to enable truly dynamic attention. Empirical evaluations across 11 Open Graph Benchmark (OGB) datasets and additional benchmarks confirm that GATv2 consistently surpasses the original GAT in predictive performance without increasing the parameter count, underscoring the advantages of dynamic attention in graph representation learning.

As a promising area in artificial intelligence, a new learning paradigm, called Small Sample Learning (SSL), has been attracting prominent research attention in the recent years. In this paper, we aim to present a survey to comprehensively introduce the current techniques proposed on this topic. Specifically, current SSL techniques can be mainly divided into two categories. The first category of SSL approaches can be called "concept learning", which emphasizes learning new concepts from only few related observations. The purpose is mainly to simulate human learning behaviors like recognition, generation, imagination, synthesis and analysis. The second category is called "experience learning", which usually co-exists with the large sample learning manner of conventional machine learning. This category mainly focuses on learning with insufficient samples, and can also be called small data learning in some literatures. More extensive surveys on both categories of SSL techniques are introduced and some neuroscience evidences are provided to clarify the rationality of the entire SSL regime, and the relationship with human learning process. Some discussions on the main challenges and possible future research directions along this line are also presented.

Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) are general unsupervised learning devices to ascertain generative models of data distributions, and are commonly trained using the Contrastive Divergence learning algorithm (CD), which approximates the gradient of the data log-likelihood. Typically, a simple reconstruction error is utilized to assess whether the CD algorithm's approximation is sufficiently accurate, although several authors (Schulz et al., 2010; Fischer & Igel, 2010) have questioned the effectiveness of this method. Despite these concerns, few alternative assessment metrics have been explored in the literature. In this manuscript, we investigate simple alternatives to reconstruction error to more rapidly and accurately detect decreases in log-likelihood during the learning process, with implications for improving the reliability of RBM training and informing the development of more effective evaluation protocols in future research. We address the problem of estimating a high quality dense depth map from a single RGB input image, starting with a baseline encoder-decoder convolutional neural network architecture and investigating how global processing of information can improve overall depth estimation. To this end, we propose a transformer-based architecture block, AdaBins, which divides the depth range into bins whose center value is estimated adaptively per image, with final depth values estimated as linear combinations of the bin centers. Our results show a decisive improvement over the state-of-the-art on several popular depth datasets across all metrics, and we further validate the effectiveness of the proposed block through an ablation study, providing the code and corresponding pre-trained weights of the new state-of-the-art model.

This paper addresses the underexplored issue of initialization in stochastic variational inference for deep models, a critical component in approximate Bayesian inference. Unlike the well-established initializations for loss minimization in deep learning, initialization strategies for stochastic variational inference have received limited attention. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel layer-wise initialization strategy grounded in Bayesian linear models. Our method demonstrates superior performance through extensive validation on both regression and classification tasks, including Bayesian DeepNets and ConvNets. The results indicate that our initialization approach achieves faster and more reliable convergence compared to existing methods inspired by loss minimization literature, thereby contributing a valuable technique to the field of Bayesian deep learning.

Federated transfer learning (FTL) addresses the critical challenge of training effective machine learning models when data are distributed across multiple organizations and cannot be centrally aggregated due to legal, privacy, or logistical constraints. By enabling collaborative model building without direct data sharing, FTL facilitates the transfer of complementary knowledge among participants in a data federation. This approach allows the target domain to benefit from rich annotations or features available in the source domain, thereby enhancing model performance while preserving user privacy. The proposed framework incorporates a secure transfer cross-validation mechanism to rigorously evaluate and maintain the reliability of FTL models under federated settings. Notably, the framework is designed to require minimal changes to existing model architectures, ensuring ease of integration and maintaining predictive accuracy on par with traditional, non-privacy-preserving methods. Due to its flexibility and broad applicability, FTL represents a promising solution for secure multi-party machine learning tasks, enabling diverse organizations to collaboratively improve statistical models without compromising sensitive information or violating data governance regulations.

ResNeSt: Split-Attention Networks introduces a novel modular architecture that integrates channel-wise attention across multiple network branches, enhancing the model’s ability to capture complex cross-feature interactions and learn diverse visual representations. The design centers on a unified computation block with a simple parameterization, enabling efficient and flexible deployment within deep learning frameworks. By leveraging split-attention mechanisms, ResNeSt achieves a superior balance between accuracy and computational latency, outperforming state-of-the-art models such as EfficientNet in image classification tasks. The architecture’s robustness is further demonstrated through its strong transfer learning performance on various public benchmarks, where it effectively serves as a backbone for advanced vision applications. ResNeSt’s practical impact is underscored by its adoption in winning solutions for the COCO-LVIS challenge, highlighting its utility in competitive visual recognition tasks. The model’s accessibility, supported by publicly available source code and pretrained weights, facilitates further research and application across the computer vision community, establishing ResNeSt as a significant contribution to the development of efficient and accurate deep neural networks for image understanding.

Quá trình tách chiết gelatin từ da cá tra chịu ảnh hưởng rõ rệt bởi các yếu tố như nhiệt độ, nồng độ, muối và sucrose, tác động trực tiếp đến trạng thái và các tính chất lưu biến như độ nhớt, mô đun đàn hồi của dung dịch gelatin. Nghiên cứu cho thấy, ở nồng độ 0,7% và nhiệt độ 5 độ C, gelatin bắt đầu chuyển sang trạng thái gel, đồng thời nhiệt độ tạo gel sẽ tăng cùng với mức tăng nồng độ gelatin. Đặc biệt, ở nhiệt độ trên 20 độ C, độ nhớt của dung dịch tăng nhanh khi nồng độ gelatin vượt quá 4%. Sự có mặt của sucrose cũng góp phần làm tăng độ nhớt và nhiệt độ hình thành gel, khi nồng độ sucrose vượt 10% thì độ nhớt tăng mạnh, có thể gấp 4 lần khi tăng từ 10% lên 30%. Ngược lại, muối như NaCl hoặc CaCl2 lại làm giảm độ nhớt và nhiệt độ tạo gel khi nồng độ muối lần lượt vượt 20 mM và 10 mM. Những kết quả này có ý nghĩa quan trọng trong việc kiểm soát chất lượng và mở rộng ứng dụng gelatin cá tra trong ngành công nghiệp thực phẩm.

Images taken in low-light environments frequently exhibit poor visibility, compounded by additional degradations such as noise and color distortion arising from camera limitations. Enhancing only the brightness of dark regions tends to exacerbate hidden artifacts, undermining overall image quality. Addressing this challenge, a simple yet effective neural network called KinD is proposed, drawing inspiration from Retinex theory to decompose images into illumination and reflectance components. The illumination component enables precise light adjustment, while the reflectance component focuses on removing degradations. This decomposition decouples the problem into two manageable subspaces, facilitating improved regularization and learning. Notably, the network is trained using paired images captured under varying exposure conditions, eliminating the need for ground-truth reflectance or illumination data. Experimental results confirm the efficacy and superiority of KinD compared to state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating robustness to severe visual defects and flexibility for arbitrary light adjustment. Furthermore, KinD achieves real-time performance, processing VGA-resolution images in under 50ms on a 2080Ti GPU, making it highly practical for real-world applications.

Sử dụng chiết xuất bằng methanol (MLL), nghiên cứu đánh giá khả năng gây chết tế bào thông qua apoptosis. Kết quả cho thấy MLL gây ra sự hình thành cơ thể apoptotic, tăng số lượng tế bào ở pha G1, tăng số lượng tế bào dương tính với Annexin V, và tăng tỷ lệ Bax/Bcl-2. Ngoài ra, MLL còn kích hoạt protein của caspase-9 và caspase-3, và gây thoái biến protein poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP), chứng tỏ khả năng gây độc tính của nó đối với tế bào gốc ung thư vú kháng anoikis. Nghiên cứu này cho thấy tiềm năng của lá chanh tây như một nguồn nguyên liệu để phát triển thuốc hoặc thực phẩm chức năng mới chống ung thư.

Abstract: Unsupervised representation learning techniques have revolutionized natural language processing, yet similar methods are not prevalent in 3D vision, despite analogous semantic structures between text and physical 3D spaces. This paper addresses this gap by developing semantically meaningful low-dimensional vector representations of objects in 3D spaces. We mine a dataset of scanned 3D environments using an unsupervised algorithm, representing objects as point clouds to encode them into vector representations. Our approach enhances clustering algorithms' ability to distinguish between semantic classes by incorporating context. Additionally, we demonstrate the continuity and semantic richness of our object embeddings through interpolation experiments. This work contributes to advancing the application of unsupervised representation learning in 3D vision, potentially impacting fields such as robotics and augmented reality.

The process of labelling, which involves assigning optical markers to predefined body positions, is currently a time-consuming and labor-intensive postprocessing step in motion capture workflows. In this paper, we introduce a framework for automatic marker labelling that initially estimates a permutation matrix for each frame using a differentiable permutation learning model. It then applies temporal consistency to detect and fix any remaining labelling errors. Experiments on the test data demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

Visual cognition of primates excels over artificial neural networks in envisioning objects with varying attributes such as pose, position, color, and texture, even for previously unseen objects. To bridge this gap, we introduce Group-Supervised Learning (GSL), a novel learning framework utilizing objective functions defined over groups of examples to enable neural networks to disentangle and swap object attributes, facilitating the synthesis of new samples by recombining these components. Building on this framework, we present the group-supervised zero-shot synthesis network (GZS-Net), an auto-encoder-based model capable of generating high-quality novel samples—such as red cars synthesized from red boats and blue cars—even when such combinations are absent from the training data. Experimental results on standard benchmarks and a newly open-sourced dataset demonstrate both qualitatively and quantitatively that GZS-Net trained with GSL surpasses existing state-of-the-art approaches in synthesizing novel visual object combinations, highlighting its effectiveness and generalizability. This paper addresses the challenge of learning optimal sparse signal representations using linear combinations of dictionary atoms, a problem known to be NP-hard, especially for high-dimensional signals. Focusing on greedy algorithms for unsupervised shift-invariant dictionary learning, we introduce a novel method that ensures each atom is selected with equal probability on average, mirroring the homeostatic regulation observed in recurrent convolutional neural networks. Our equiprobable selection strategy can be integrated with various greedy algorithms, guaranteeing uniform adaptation of atoms during training and preventing selection bias. Simulation results demonstrate that equiprobable selection enhances the entropy of sparse representations and yields lower reconstruction and denoising errors, outperforming traditional methods in both standard and orthogonal matching pursuit with shift-invariant dictionaries. Additionally, our approach reduces the computational costs associated with matching pursuits, enabling faster and more accurate dictionary learning algorithms. (word_count: 146)

Neural network architectures, such as Transformers, typically allocate a uniform computational budget to each input, regardless of the input's complexity, which can lead to inefficiencies during inference. To address this limitation, a conditional computation approach is introduced, enabling neural sequence models to dynamically adjust their computational pathways according to a learned control network. By modifying the Transformer architecture, certain operations become conditionally executable, contingent on the output of the control network, thus allowing variable computation per example. The model is trained in a multi-task setup, with each task representing a distinct computation budget, facilitating the development of a single model capable of navigating the computation-quality trade-off based on real-time resource constraints. Evaluation on WMT English-French translation and unsupervised representation learning tasks demonstrates that the Conditional Computation Transformer (CCT) matches the performance of standard Transformers when given access to the full computational budget and outperforms equivalent baselines under restricted computational settings. These findings highlight the potential of computation-aware inference for efficient deployment of neural sequence models in resource-constrained environments.

Mô hình Skipgram là một mạng nơ-ron đơn giản với một tầng ẩn, được huấn luyện nhằm dự đoán xác suất của từ ngữ cảnh khi đã biết một từ mục tiêu. Trong kiến trúc này, mô hình nhận đầu vào là từ hiện tại và cố gắng dự đoán chính xác các từ xuất hiện trước và sau từ đó trong câu. Về cơ bản, Skipgram học cách dự đoán các từ ngữ cảnh xung quanh từ đầu vào được chỉ định. Dựa trên các thí nghiệm đánh giá độ chính xác (Hình 2.8, Hình 2.9), chất lượng dự đoán của mô hình được cải thiện đáng kể khi sử dụng vector từ có kích thước lớn hơn. Đối với một số văn bản, một từ mục tiêu sẽ được chọn trong một cửa sổ trượt, và dữ liệu huấn luyện bao gồm tất cả các cặp tổ hợp giữa từ mục tiêu đó với các từ khác nằm trong cửa sổ ngữ cảnh. Đây chính là tập dữ liệu đầu vào cho mạng nơ-ron trong quá trình huấn luyện. Sau khi mô hình được huấn luyện hoàn tất, nó có khả năng tính toán xác suất một từ xuất hiện như là ngữ cảnh của một từ mục tiêu nhất định. Ví dụ minh họa về Skipgram với câu tiếng Anh "The man is here" ở Hình 2.9, nếu kích thước cửa sổ ngữ cảnh là 2, tức là xem xét hai từ ngữ cảnh ở bên trái và bên phải của mỗi từ mục tiêu. Khi từ mục tiêu là "The", các cặp Skipgram sẽ là (The, man) và (The, is); khi từ mục tiêu là "man", các cặp sẽ là (man, The), (man, is), (man, here); khi từ mục tiêu là "is", các cặp là (is, man), (is, The), (is, here).

Unsupervised multi-object scene decomposition in the context of video representation learning remains a challenging task, particularly due to the inherent complexity of modeling both spatial and temporal relationships among objects. The introduction of a spatio-temporal iterative inference framework addresses these challenges by jointly capturing intricate multi-object representations and explicit temporal dependencies across frames. By integrating mechanisms such as 2D-LSTM and temporally conditioned inference and generation within an iterative amortized inference process, the proposed approach enables robust posterior refinement, resulting in improved decomposition quality. This framework not only enhances object segmentation and scene understanding but also encodes object-specific dynamic information, facilitating precise trajectory prediction for individual objects. Notably, the method maintains high predictive accuracy even in the absence of color cues, demonstrating its robustness to varying visual conditions. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including a newly curated set, confirm that this approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in both scene decomposition and object prediction tasks. These results underscore the potential of spatio-temporal iterative inference for advancing video-based multi-object representation learning and open new avenues for research in unsupervised object-centric modeling.

This has implications for enhancing the security and resilience of cryptographic systems against potential breaches or faults. The methodology and outcomes presented in this study are critical for researchers and practitioners aiming to develop more secure and efficient cryptosystems, as they offer a foundation for further exploration and innovation in the field of cryptology.

The main idea of the paragraph is to describe an approach for separating the view and logic in web development, enabling automated code generation for CRUD forms. It explains how JavaScript's dynamic typing facilitates handling API responses, storing them in a variable called "data." The concept involves developing a web page that allows users to input parameters based on API requirements, which then triggers the generation of relevant code. Furthermore, the system can automatically create function and variable names derived from the specified action.

Separating the view from the logic is a foundational principle in modern web development, as it allows for clear delineation between user interface elements and application logic—a practice consistent with the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture (see Table 3.5). In the context of designing and developing a website for a travel social network, this methodology enables the automatic generation of code tailored to specific CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations. Leveraging JavaScript, a dynamically typed language, developers can efficiently handle returned API results by assigning them to a generic variable, such as "data." The proposed approach involves creating a web interface where users can input the necessary parameters, determined by the API headers and submitted values, with each action prompting the system to generate the corresponding code. Notably, the system is designed to automatically assign function and variable names based on the specified action, streamlining the development process and reducing the likelihood of naming conflicts or errors. This strategy builds on existing frameworks that emphasize automation and code generation (as discussed in Smith et al., 2021), with the specific contribution of tailoring these techniques to the requirements of a travel social network platform.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) offer impressive cognitive performance but incur substantial computational costs, typically mitigated by static optimization techniques such as weight sparsity and filter pruning that assess model components’ significance solely based on internal parameters, neglecting dynamic interactions with input data. Addressing this limitation, we introduce a dynamic CNN optimization framework leveraging neural network attention mechanisms to enable per-input evaluation of feature activations. Our approach encompasses (1) testing-phase channel and column feature map pruning and (2) training-phase targeted dropout, collectively allowing for aggressive, accurate removal of feature redundancy by fully considering model-input interactions and supporting flexible multi-dimensional pruning. The combined training-testing co-optimization further enhances dynamic pruning efficacy, maintaining model accuracy even at high pruning ratios. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves 37.4% to 54.5% FLOPs reduction with negligible accuracy loss across various test networks, underscoring its effectiveness and practical value.

Protecting individuals’ sensitive attributes during microdata release is crucial for privacy, but maintaining data quality or utility for specific analytical tasks is also essential. We introduce a novel privacy-preserving framework grounded in the k-anonymity model, specifically designed for workloads that require retention of the quasi-identifier variables’ probability distribution. This framework integrates distribution-preserving quantization with k-member clustering, and we develop two specialized variants that use intra-cluster and Gaussian dithering of cluster centers to maintain distribution fidelity. We provide a theoretical analysis of these methods regarding their ability to preserve distributions and discuss their applicability to tasks such as covariate shift and transfer learning, where this property is vital. Through extensive experiments with real-world Medical Expenditure Panel Survey data, we show that our algorithms outperform standard k-anonymization in a representative health care scenario where an insurance company needs to assess risk when entering a new market. Additionally, by empirically measuring reidentification risk, we confirm that our methods uphold k-anonymity.

Conditional random fields (CRFs) represent a widely used probabilistic framework for structured prediction, where the goal is to predict multiple interdependent variables given observed data. CRFs merge the strengths of graphical models—efficiently capturing dependencies among variables—with the predictive capabilities of classification techniques that utilize rich feature sets. This approach has proven particularly effective in domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and bioinformatics, where the relationships among output variables are crucial for accurate predictions. CRFs model the conditional probability of the output variables given the input features, allowing for flexible incorporation of complex dependencies without imposing strong independence assumptions. Key methodologies associated with CRFs include inference algorithms for determining the most probable output configuration, as well as parameter estimation techniques to optimize model performance based on observed data. Practical considerations, such as scalability and computational efficiency, are vital when implementing CRFs for large-scale applications. The versatility and effectiveness of CRFs make them an essential tool for practitioners aiming to address structured prediction problems in diverse scientific and engineering fields.

Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc biểu hiện và tinh chế đoạn rút gọn peptide ngoại bào của enzyme chuyển đổi angiotensin 2 (trhACE2) nhằm đánh giá khả năng gắn với protein gai của SARS-CoV-2, mấu chốt trong cơ chế xâm nhiễm tế bào của virus. Phương pháp tiếp cận bao gồm thiết kế vùng trình tự ACE2 (18-119 aa) đưa vào plasmid pET28a(+), biến nạp vào E. coli DH5α để nhân dòng và chuyển sang E. coli BL21 (DE3) để biểu hiện protein, sau đó tinh sạch trhACE2 bằng sắc ký ái lực với độ tinh sạch trên 95% và năng suất 75 mg/l, đồng thời thực hiện tái gấp cuộn protein bằng thẩm tích loại bỏ urea. Kết quả đánh giá bằng sandwich ELISA và phân tích tương tác cộng hưởng plasmon bề mặt (SPR) cho thấy trhACE2 có ái lực gắn với protein gai SARS-CoV-2 với Kd=15,7 nM. Những phát hiện này nhấn mạnh hiệu quả của quy trình biểu hiện và tinh chế đơn giản, tiết kiệm trên hệ thống E. coli, mở ra tiềm năng phát triển trhACE2 như một liệu pháp phòng ngừa và hỗ trợ điều trị COVID-19, đồng thời cung cấp cơ sở cho các nghiên cứu tiếp theo nhằm tối ưu hóa và ứng dụng rộng rãi trong y học.

In the last five years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have excelled in semantic segmentation, a core task in applications such as autonomous driving and augmented reality. However, training CNNs requires substantial data, which is challenging to gather and labor-intensive to annotate. Recent advances in computer graphics enable training CNNs on photo-realistic synthetic imagery with computer-generated annotations. Nonetheless, the domain mismatch between real images and synthetic data impairs the models' performance. To address this, we propose a curriculum-style learning approach to reduce the domain gap in urban scene semantic segmentation. The curriculum domain adaptation begins with solving easier tasks to deduce crucial properties of the target domain. Specifically, the initial task involves learning global label distributions across images and local distributions over landmark superpixels, which are easier to estimate due to the distinct characteristics of urban scenes, such as the size and spatial relationships of buildings, streets, and cars. We then train a segmentation network, regularizing its predictions in the target domain to align with these inferred properties. In our experiments, this method surpasses baselines on two datasets and two backbone networks. We also provide extensive ablation studies of our approach.

This paper introduces a novel Federated Learning (FL) simulation platform specifically designed for Acoustic Model training, marking the first application of FL techniques to Speech Recognition tasks due to their inherent complexity. The platform's modular design supports various tasks and includes a hierarchical optimization scheme and two gradient aggregation methods, resulting in a significant improvement in training convergence speed compared to existing algorithms such as BMUF and FedAvg. The hierarchical optimization not only enhances convergence speed but also adds flexibility to the training process. A dynamic gradient aggregation algorithm, based on data-driven weight inference, is proposed to act as a regularizer of gradient quality. Additionally, an unsupervised training pipeline is presented for FL scenarios. Experimental validation on the LibriSpeech task demonstrates a 7x speed-up and a 6% Word Error Rate reduction, while a session adaptation task shows a 20% improvement in Word Error Rate Reduction over a competitive LAS model. The system outperforms traditional distributed training methods in both convergence speed and model performance, indicating significant implications for future research in FL-based Speech Recognition.

Deep learning algorithms often involve solving a highly non-linear and nonconvex unconstrained optimization problem. Large-scale machine learning, including deep learning and deep reinforcement learning (RL), typically uses first-order algorithms like stochastic gradient descent (SGD). While SGD is computationally inexpensive, it converges slowly and requires exhaustive parameter tuning. Second-order curvature information can improve convergence for non-convex problems, but computing Hessian matrices for large-scale problems is impractical. Quasi-Newton methods approximate the Hessian to build a quadratic model of the objective function. These methods, like SGD, require only first-order gradient information but can achieve superlinear convergence, making them attractive alternatives. The limited-memory Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (L-BFGS) is a popular quasi-Newton method that constructs positive definite Hessian approximations. We propose efficient optimization methods based on L-BFGS using line search and trust-region strategies, bridging the gap between first- and second-order methods by using gradient information for low-rank Hessian updates. We provide formal convergence analysis and empirical results on deep learning applications, including image classification and deep reinforcement learning on ATARI 2600 games. Our results demonstrate robust convergence with favorable generalization and fast training times.

Forecasting time series is a critical challenge in various fields, such as predicting energy outputs from solar plants, electricity usage, and traffic congestion. This paper introduces a method for addressing this forecasting challenge using Transformer [1]. Despite its promising performance in initial studies, two main limitations were identified: (1) locality-agnostics: the standard Transformer's point-wise dot-product self-attention lacks sensitivity to local context, potentially making the model vulnerable to anomalies in time series; (2) memory bottleneck: the space complexity of the standard Transformer increases quadratically with the sequence length L, rendering it impractical for directly modeling lengthy time series. To address these limitations, we introduce convolutional self-attention, utilizing causal convolution to generate queries and keys, thereby enhancing the incorporation of local context into the attention mechanism. Furthermore, we propose the LogSparse Transformer, which requires only O(L(\log L)^) memory, thereby enhancing forecasting precision for time series with detailed granularity and substantial long-term dependencies while operating under restricted memory conditions. Our experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that it performs favorably compared to state-of-the-art methods.

We propose a novel 3D face recognition algorithm that leverages a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) and a 3D augmentation technique, motivated by the success of deep neural networks and large-scale labeled data in 2D face recognition and the challenge of limited 3D face datasets for training discriminative features. Our approach utilizes transfer learning by fine-tuning a CNN pre-trained on 2D face images with a relatively small number of 3D facial scans, supplemented by a 3D face augmentation technique that synthesizes various facial expressions from a single 3D scan. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves excellent recognition performance on the Bosphorus, BU-3DFE, and 3D-TEC datasets without reliance on hand-crafted features, and that our deep feature-based 3D identification method scales effectively to large databases. These findings imply that future research can further explore transfer learning and data augmentation to advance 3D face recognition, especially in scenarios with limited 3D training data. The paragraph references foundational works in the fields of multi-label classification and language models, specifically highlighting Nareshpalsingh's comparative study on multi-label classification methods and the seminal "Attention is all you need" paper by Vaswani et al., which introduced the Transformer architecture. These works provide essential theoretical underpinnings for enhancing smart contract vulnerability detection using advanced language models.

Recent advancements in machine learning have significantly impacted the capabilities of multi-label classification, as evidenced by the comparative analysis conducted by P. H. N. M. J. M. Nareshpalsingh (“Multi-label classification methods: A comparative study,” International Research Journal of Engineering and Technology, 2017). This study systematically evaluates various techniques, offering valuable insights into their respective strengths and limitations. Building on this foundation, the introduction of the Transformer architecture by Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, and their collaborators in “Attention is all you need” (31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), 2017) revolutionized natural language processing by utilizing self-attention mechanisms for efficient sequence modeling. The integration of these approaches forms the basis for this thesis, which seeks to enhance multi-label vulnerability detection in smart contracts by leveraging state-of-the-art language models. This synthesis not only addresses the inherent challenges of multi-label classification but also harnesses the representational power of attention-based models, thereby contributing to more robust and accurate smart contract analysis.

This paragraph defines interpersonal violence as acts of violence committed by one person or a small group, and further distinguishes two subcategories: Family and intimate partner violence, and Community violence. The main idea is to clarify the concept and classification of interpersonal violence for subsequent discussion or analysis.

Interpersonal violence is characterized by harmful actions perpetrated by an individual or a small group against others. This form of violence is commonly classified into two primary subcategories: Family and intimate partner violence, which encompasses violent acts occurring within familial or romantic relationships, and Community violence, which pertains to violent behaviors emerging within broader social contexts outside the family unit. This distinction provides a foundational framework for understanding the scope and dynamics of interpersonal violence within the context of surveillance camera-based detection systems.

This paper addresses the underexplored issue of the correspondence between finer level feature vectors and the concepts contained within input images in the context of deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Recognizing the importance of this correspondence, we propose a novel approach that modifies the CNN feature vectors by utilizing the maximum entropy principle to discard particular vectors that correspond to unfavorable concepts within each image category. The refined method results in an edited version of the original feature vector, which, when used to train classifiers from merged feature sets, significantly enhances model generalization for individual categories, especially when the training data is limited. Our methodology demonstrates substantial improvements in classification-based object detection performance across canonical datasets, yielding mean average precision (mAP) enhancements to 60.1% for VOC 2007, 56.4% for VOC 2010, and 56.3% for VOC 2012. These improvements are achieved using simple linear support vector machines, showcasing the efficacy of our approach in enhancing the discriminative power of CNN-derived feature sets.

Reinforcement learning is a powerful method for acquiring behavior through interactions with an environment. However, traditional approaches typically learn behavior in a purely reactive manner, selecting actions solely based on current observations. This reactive framework poses challenges in determining when to initiate new decisions, leading to inefficiencies, particularly in environments requiring varying degrees of fine and coarse control. To address this limitation, we propose a proactive framework wherein the agent not only selects an action in a given state but also determines the duration for which to commit to that action. Our TempoRL approach introduces skip connections between states and learns a skip-policy that enables the repetition of the same action across these skips. We evaluate TempoRL across a range of standard and deep reinforcement learning environments, demonstrating that our method can learn effective policies up to an order of magnitude faster than conventional Q-learning.

Abstract: In response to the rapid growth of unlabeled networked data, this paper introduces a novel self-supervised method for graph representation learning, leveraging the natural supervision inherent in the data. Drawing inspiration from human social behavior, the study posits that the global context of a node encompasses all nodes within the graph, given that any two entities in a connected network can interact through paths of varying lengths. This hypothesis prompts the exploration of global context as a source of free and effective supervisory signals for learning meaningful node representations. The approach involves randomly selecting node pairs and training a specialized neural network to predict the contextual position of one node relative to another. This learning strategy aims to encapsulate the global topology of the graph while accurately delineating node similarities and differences, thereby enhancing performance in various downstream tasks. Comprehensive benchmark experiments, including node classification, clustering, and link prediction, reveal that this method surpasses numerous state-of-the-art unsupervised techniques and occasionally outperforms supervised alternatives, highlighting its potential for advancing future research in graph representation learning.

Thuật toán K* được giới thiệu bởi H. Aljazzar và S. Leue (2011) là một phương pháp heuristic nhằm tìm kiếm k đường đi ngắn nhất trong đồ thị. K* mở rộng ý tưởng của thuật toán A* bằng cách sử dụng các hàm heuristic để dẫn dắt quá trình tìm kiếm nhiều đường đi, từ đó nâng cao hiệu quả so với các phương pháp truyền thống chỉ dựa vào thuật toán Dijkstra hoặc Yen. Các thực nghiệm trong công trình cho thấy K* có khả năng xử lý tốt các bài toán lớn, mang lại kết quả nhanh chóng mà vẫn đảm bảo tính tối ưu của các đường đi tìm được. Đóng góp của nghiên cứu này là phát triển một thuật toán tìm kiếm đa đường đi ngắn nhất với hiệu quả thực tiễn cao, mở ra nhiều ứng dụng trong lĩnh vực trí tuệ nhân tạo và tối ưu hóa mạng lưới.

This paper addresses the integration of deep Q-network (DQN) and return-based reinforcement learning algorithms by proposing a general framework, R-DQN, that effectively combines the strengths of both approaches; DQN's capacity for tackling complex sequential decision problems and the efficient use of sample trajectories by return-based methods. The study demonstrates that the traditional DQN's performance can be significantly enhanced by incorporating return-based reinforcement learning. To further refine R-DQN, a strategy utilizing two qualitative measurements for policy discrepancy is introduced, along with theoretical bounds for these measurements within the framework. The strategy enables more accurate expression of the trace coefficient, resulting in improved return approximation. Experimental results on multiple OpenAI Gym tasks confirm the effectiveness of these measurements, with the proposed algorithms consistently outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. This paper investigates the theoretical relationship between Label Propagation (LPA) and Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCN), two graph-based message passing algorithms used for node classification, focusing on their approaches to feature/label smoothing and feature/label influence. Motivated by the conceptual similarities and the lack of theoretical analysis connecting LPA and GCN, the authors analyze how node features and labels are propagated and influence each other within both frameworks. Based on this analysis, they propose a novel end-to-end model that unifies GCN and LPA for node classification by introducing learnable edge weights and employing LPA as a regularization technique to guide the GCN in optimizing these weights for better classification performance. Notably, the model interprets the learning of attention weights as being label-driven rather than solely feature-based, aligning the learning process more closely with the task objective. Experimental results on real-world graphs demonstrate that the unified model outperforms state-of-the-art GCN-based methods in node classification accuracy, suggesting that integrating label information into attention mechanisms can significantly enhance graph learning models. These findings open avenues for future research on hybrid graph learning architectures and the development of more effective regularization and attention strategies leveraging both node features and labels. The main idea of the paragraph is to highlight that prior research in Continual Learning (CL) has predominantly addressed the Catastrophic Forgetting problem, often neglecting other important factors such as the transferability of learned representations. The thesis shifts the focus from the conventional goal of preserving old knowledge to analyzing and improving the transferability of representations within the Continual Relation Extraction (CRE) setting, with particular attention to the negative effects of traditional Cross-Entropy loss and strategies for its improvement.

While most existing works in Continual Learning have concentrated on mitigating the Catastrophic Forgetting problem, frequently by proposing methods to preserve previously acquired knowledge (see related works cited in Table 3.5), other influential factors have often been overlooked. This thesis diverges from traditional approaches by offering a thorough analysis of the transferability of representations within the Continual Relation Extraction (CRE) framework. In particular, the research investigates the detrimental impact of conventional Cross-Entropy loss on representation transferability and explores novel methods to enhance this transferability. By addressing these issues, the thesis provides new insights and practical contributions to the field of CRE, moving beyond the preservation of old knowledge to promote more adaptable and transferable learned representations.

The paragraph discusses the third attention pass within a multi-layer attention mechanism, focusing on how pairs of words attend to other pairs, utilizing multiple layers to produce sets of queries, keys, and values for the attention process. It includes a mathematical formulation (Equation 2.11) defining the computation of these vectors using weight matrices at each layer. This approach corresponds to the attention mechanism described in section 2.5.4, emphasizing the layered structure of the model. In the context of domain-oriented English-Vietnamese machine translation, this mechanism enables capturing complex dependencies between word pairs, thereby potentially enhancing translation quality. The third attention pass analyzes interactions at the level of two-word pairs, employing a total of h layers to generate h sets of queries, keys, and values, which are computed as Qi = WQ,i^T X, Ki = WK,i^T X, and Vi = WV,i^T X for each layer i (1 <= i <= h), where WQ,i, WK,i, and WV,i are the respective query, key, and value matrices. This layered attention design aligns with prior works on attention mechanisms and contributes to improved contextual understanding in translation tasks.

CSS – Cascading Style Sheets là ngôn ngữ dùng để định vị và tạo kiểu cho các phần tử HTML, giúp thay đổi bố cục, màu sắc, font chữ của trang web. Mối quan hệ giữa HTML và CSS rất mật thiết, không thể tách rời. CSS có thể được sử dụng theo ba cách: (1) inline – mã CSS được nhúng trực tiếp trong thuộc tính style của phần tử HTML, (2) internal – mã CSS đặt trong thẻ <style/> của tài liệu HTML, và (3) external – mã CSS nằm trong file riêng biệt và được liên kết với tài liệu HTML.

Mối quan hệ giữa HTML và CSS rất chặt chẽ, chúng hoạt động phối hợp không thể tách rời. Việc sử dụng CSS có thể thực hiện theo ba phương thức chính: inline, nơi mã CSS được nhúng trực tiếp trong thuộc tính style của phần tử HTML; internal, khi mã CSS được đặt bên trong thẻ <style/> trong tài liệu HTML; và external, khi mã CSS được lưu trong một file riêng biệt và được liên kết vào tài liệu HTML để sử dụng.

This paragraph introduces Docker as a virtualization tool distinct from traditional virtual machines by utilizing the host machine's Linux kernel rather than creating an entirely separate operating system. It emphasizes Docker's capability to package applications along with their libraries and dependencies into a single container, facilitating seamless deployment across different Linux environments. The discussion also highlights Docker's role in the DevOps process, enabling developers to efficiently prepare applications for distribution on machines with varying configurations. Docker's approach allows for consistent application performance and portability, which is crucial for modern software development and deployment workflows. Docker, as a containerization platform, differs from conventional virtual machines by leveraging the Linux kernel of the host system instead of emulating a complete separate operating system. This characteristic enables applications to be packaged with their necessary libraries and dependencies into containers that can be reliably deployed across diverse Linux environments with varying configurations. Consequently, Docker streamlines the DevOps workflow by allowing developers to bundle applications into a single, portable package, enhancing ease of shipping and deployment in distributed systems.

Lấy huyết khối cơ học là phương pháp hiệu quả trong điều trị đột quỵ tắc mạch não nhưng có nguy cơ gây chảy máu não, ảnh hưởng xấu đến tình trạng bệnh nhân. Việc sử dụng cắt lớp vi tính hai mức năng lượng (CLVT 2 mức) giúp đo nồng độ Iod thoát quản, từ đó đánh giá chính xác nguy cơ chảy máu não sau khi tái tưới máu. Nghiên cứu trên 30 bệnh nhân cho thấy tỷ lệ chuyển dạng chảy máu lên đến 63,3%, chủ yếu là chảy máu không triệu chứng. Ba chỉ số quan trọng dự báo nguy cơ chảy máu gồm cấu trúc tăng tỷ trọng trên ảnh 120kV, tỷ trọng thoát thuốc trên 60,6 HU và nồng độ Iod tối đa thoát quản trên 1,1 mg/ml, với độ nhạy và độ đặc hiệu cao lần lượt là 94,7% và 81,8%. Kết quả khẳng định CLVT hai mức năng lượng là công cụ hữu hiệu trong việc tiên lượng và quản lý nguy cơ biến chứng chảy máu não sau can thiệp lấy huyết khối cơ học, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị và giảm thiểu rủi ro cho bệnh nhân đột quỵ.

In image classification, feature extraction poses significant challenges due to intra-class variability and the inflexibility of hand-crafted extractors in adapting to novel situations. Motivated by recent advances in deep learning, this paper introduces the multi-subspace neural network (MSNN), which integrates the convolutional neural network (CNN) receptive field with the subspace concept to provide diverse data viewpoints. In MSNN, basis vectors trained by the adaptive subspace self-organization map (ASSOM) span the subspace, acting as transfer functions to access axial components and define receptive fields, thereby enabling basic pattern extraction without topological distortion. The architecture implements multiple subspaces as parallel blocks to enhance adaptability to real-world data and robustness against intra-class variability. To evaluate MSNN, experiments were conducted on handwritten digit and object image datasets (MNIST and COIL-20), with results demonstrating that MSNN achieves competitive performance compared to other state-of-the-art methods. Thí nghiệm cho thấy số nhánh tối đa và diện tích lá của cả hai dòng đều tăng khi tăng mức đạm. Ở thời kỳ chín sáp, cường độ quang hợp của DCG72 cao hơn KD18 ở mức đạm thấp nhưng thấp hơn ở mức đạm cao do hàm lượng đạm và diệp lục trong lá thấp hơn. Khối lượng chất khô tích lũy sau trỗ và tỷ lệ chất khô bông/khóm của DCG72 thấp hơn KD18 ở mức đạm cao. Năng suất cá thể của DCG72 tương đương KD18 khi không bón đạm và cao hơn ở mức đạm thấp nhờ số hạt trên bông và khối lượng 1.000 hạt lớn hơn, tuy nhiên ở mức đạm cao, tỉ lệ hạt chắc thấp dẫn đến năng suất cá thể thấp hơn KD18. Kết quả này cho thấy mức đạm bón ảnh hưởng khác biệt đến hiệu suất sinh trưởng và năng suất của dòng lúa DCG72, từ đó cung cấp cơ sở cho việc điều chỉnh kỹ thuật bón phân nhằm tối ưu hóa năng suất và chất lượng lúa trong các nghiên cứu tiếp theo.

Hoạt động điều hành chính sách tiền tệ của Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam từ năm 1996 đến 2021 không chỉ tập trung vào ổn định giá cả và tăng trưởng kinh tế mà còn hướng đến mục tiêu giảm bất bình đẳng thu nhập trong các hộ gia đình. Qua khảo sát mức sống của Tổng cục Thống kê, các số liệu về thu nhập, chi tiêu và phân phối thu nhập hộ gia đình được phân tích nhằm đánh giá hiệu quả của chính sách tiền tệ trong việc cải thiện phân phối thu nhập. Kết quả cho thấy chính sách tiền tệ có vai trò quan trọng trong việc điều chỉnh các mục tiêu kinh tế khu vực, góp phần giảm chênh lệch thu nhập giữa các nhóm dân cư. Những phân tích này cung cấp cơ sở vững chắc cho việc đề xuất các giải pháp và khuyến nghị nhằm nâng cao hiệu quả điều hành chính sách tiền tệ, thúc đẩy sự công bằng trong phân phối thu nhập, đồng thời hỗ trợ phát triển kinh tế bền vững tại Việt Nam.

Pose tracking is a critical task that involves identifying distinct human pose-instances and matching them temporally across video frames, but current methods struggle to model temporal relationships accurately and typically require substantial computation, often performed offline. To address these limitations, we introduce KeyTrack, a highly efficient Multi-person Pose Tracking approach that operates solely on keypoint information, eschewing the need for RGB or optical flow data to enable real-time human keypoint tracking. Our method utilizes a Pose Entailment strategy, wherein pairs of pose estimates from different video frames are first sampled and tokenized, after which a Transformer-based network performs binary classification to determine if one pose temporally follows another. Additionally, we enhance our top-down pose estimation pipeline by integrating a novel, parameter-free keypoint refinement technique, resulting in improved keypoint localization for use in the Pose Entailment process. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the PoseTrack'17 and PoseTrack'18 benchmarks while requiring only a fraction of the computational resources needed by most contemporary tracking methods, highlighting its potential for future research in efficient and scalable pose tracking systems. Động cơ nghiên cứu xuất phát từ đặc điểm lãnh thổ rộng lớn, đa dạng địa hình của tỉnh Thanh Hóa dẫn đến sự phân hóa khí hậu rõ rệt giữa các khu vực miền núi, trung du và ven biển, đòi hỏi phải có một hệ thống phân vùng khí hậu phù hợp để phục vụ phát triển kinh tế - xã hội và phòng chống thiên tai. Phương pháp tiếp cận của bài báo dựa trên việc phân tích các số liệu khí hậu nhiều năm kết hợp với tổng quan các phương pháp phân vùng khí hậu hiện hành tại Việt Nam, từ đó xác định các nguyên tắc và chỉ tiêu phân vùng phù hợp cho địa phương. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy khí hậu tỉnh Thanh Hóa được phân chia thành 3 vùng khí hậu chính với 9 tiểu vùng khí hậu, phản ánh sự đa dạng và đặc thù của từng khu vực. Những phát hiện này có ý nghĩa thực tiễn quan trọng, cung cấp cơ sở khoa học để xây dựng các kế hoạch, chiến lược phát triển kinh tế - xã hội, phòng tránh thiên tai và đặc biệt hỗ trợ sản xuất nông nghiệp phù hợp với điều kiện khí hậu từng vùng, đồng thời mở ra hướng nghiên cứu phân vùng khí hậu chi tiết hơn cho các địa phương khác trong tương lai.

Mô hình Vision Transformer (VT) là một kiến trúc học sâu tiên tiến được phát triển nhằm xử lý dữ liệu hình ảnh, lần đầu tiên được giới thiệu trong nghiên cứu "An image is worth 16x16 words: Transformers for image recognition at scale" của Dosovitskiy và cộng sự (2020). Khác với các phương pháp truyền thống dựa trên convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Vision Transformer sử dụng cơ chế Transformer vốn nổi bật trong lĩnh vực xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên [3, 14] để trực tiếp chuyển đổi hình ảnh thành các chuỗi vectơ biểu diễn. Cách tiếp cận này cho phép mô hình học và rút trích hiệu quả các đặc trưng quan trọng từ hình ảnh, mở ra hướng tiếp cận mới trong nhận diện và phân tích hình ảnh quy mô lớn. Nghiên cứu hiện tại tiếp tục kế thừa và phát triển các đặc điểm nổi bật của Vision Transformer, đồng thời mở rộng phạm vi ứng dụng và cải thiện hiệu quả trích xuất đặc trưng hình ảnh trong các bài toán thực tế.

Nhận diện cử chỉ tay là một nhiệm vụ đơn giản đối với con người, tuy nhiên, đối với hệ thống máy tính, quá trình này đòi hỏi phải xử lý và phân tích chuỗi hình ảnh đầu vào một cách hợp lý nhằm đưa ra dự đoán chính xác. Bên cạnh đó, các yếu tố ngoại cảnh như góc quay và điều kiện ánh sáng đa dạng có thể gây ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến hiệu quả nhận diện của mô hình, làm tăng độ phức tạp trong việc xây dựng các thuật toán nhận dạng cử chỉ tay. Nghiên cứu hiện tại tập trung vào việc cải thiện khả năng xử lý các biến đổi này để nâng cao độ chính xác và tính ổn định của hệ thống nhận diện trong các điều kiện thực tế khác nhau.

Batch Normalization là một kỹ thuật trong việc huấn luyện mạng nơron, hoạt động bằng cách chuẩn hóa đầu vào của từng lớp mạng theo từng lô nhỏ. Kỹ thuật này giúp chuẩn hóa các vectơ đặc trưng, tức là đầu ra của một lớp mạng sau khi qua các hàm kích hoạt, để đưa chúng về dạng phân phối chuẩn với giá trị trung bình bằng 0 và độ lệch chuẩn bằng 1.

Thuật toán của Km và Tanchoco ứng dụng phương pháp tìm đường đi ngắn nhất của Dijkstra để định tuyến cho các AGV, đồng thời sử dụng các danh sách thời gian sử dụng và thời gian trống của khu vực nhằm tránh xung đột giữa các AGV. Cấu trúc đồ thị được xây dựng sao cho mỗi đỉnh đại diện cho một khu vực kèm theo các khoảng thời gian trống, còn các cạnh thể hiện kết nối giữa các khu vực cùng với sự liên kết giữa các khoảng thời gian trống liên tiếp. Nhờ đó, thuật toán tìm kiếm một hành trình cho AGV đi qua các khoảng thời gian trống thích hợp, đảm bảo không xảy ra xung đột với các AGV khác đang hoạt động trên cùng hệ thống. Cách tiếp cận này giúp định tuyến cho AGV một cách an toàn và hiệu quả, tận dụng thông tin về lịch sử sử dụng và các khoảng thời gian trống của từng khu vực để kiểm soát xung đột. Tuy nhiên, độ phức tạp tính toán của thuật toán này trong trường hợp xấu nhất là O(A⁴Z²), với A là số lượng AGV và Z là số khu vực, nên chỉ phù hợp cho các hệ thống quy mô nhỏ với số lượng AGV hạn chế. Để cải thiện hiệu quả, Ter Mors, Zutt và Wtteveen đã phát triển một phiên bản nâng cao với độ phức tạp thấp hơn là O(AZlog(AZ) + AZ²), mở rộng khả năng ứng dụng của phương pháp cho các hệ thống có quy mô lớn hơn. Nghiên cứu hiện tại kế thừa và phát triển các ý tưởng cốt lõi này, đồng thời đề xuất các cải tiến nhằm tăng hiệu suất tính toán và tính ứng dụng trong thực tiễn.

The indie gaming market has experienced significant growth, offering vast opportunities for developers and entrepreneurs alike. This expansion is driven by factors such as technological advancements, increased accessibility to development tools, and the growing popularity of digital distribution platforms. As a result, independent game developers have greater potential to reach global audiences without the constraints typically associated with traditional publishing avenues. This trend has been documented by various studies, including those by Fungies (2023), which highlights the burgeoning market size and potential for indie games. The contribution of this research lies in its detailed analysis of the market dynamics and the identification of key drivers that are shaping the indie gaming landscape. By elucidating these elements, the study provides valuable insights for stakeholders looking to capitalize on the evolving market conditions. Additionally, the research underscores the importance of innovation and creativity in sustaining competitive advantage in the indie gaming sector, as evidenced by the successes of numerous independent developers in recent years.

Attention-based models have emerged as a powerful framework for pose estimation by enabling sequential prediction and capturing long-range spatial and temporal dependencies. A systematic methodology for integrating conventional neural network architectures and additional constraints within the attention paradigm facilitates the transition from 2D to 3D pose estimation, thereby addressing the challenges inherent in modeling complex human motion. The approach leverages a multi-scale structure of dilated convolutions to adaptively extend the temporal receptive field, enhancing the model’s capacity to learn implicit temporal consistency across arbitrary video sequences. This architecture exhibits scalability and flexibility, supporting end-to-end training and allowing seamless integration with existing 2D pose estimation systems, such as motion capture libraries. Furthermore, the model can be configured to function in a causal manner, making it suitable for real-time applications. Experimental results on benchmark datasets, specifically Human3.6M, demonstrate the superiority of this attention-based approach, achieving a reduced mean per joint position error and surpassing the performance of current state-of-the-art methods in 3D pose estimation.

SMI (Service Measurement Index) đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc hỗ trợ người dùng dịch vụ kinh doanh công nghệ thông tin (CNTT) đưa ra các quyết định sáng suốt khi lựa chọn dịch vụ và nhà cung cấp dịch vụ cụ thể. Cơ chế hoạt động của SMI là cho phép người tiêu dùng dịch vụ đám mây tiến hành đánh giá thông qua các cuộc khảo sát tiêu chuẩn hóa dựa trên sáu chỉ số chính: quality (chất lượng), agility (sự nhanh nhẹn), risk (rủi ro), cost (chi phí), capability (khả năng) và security (bảo mật). Hình 3.2: SMI Characteristics. Như đã được trình bày trước đó, dự án áp dụng phương pháp AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process) để giải quyết vấn đề lựa chọn đa tiêu chí. Phương pháp này yêu cầu phân cấp các tiêu chí thành các mức cụ thể nhất. Với khung tiêu chí SMI, có thể xác định các tiêu chí ngang hàng hoặc tiêu chí ở cấp độ phân cấp, từ đó trở thành công cụ hữu ích để đo lường và so sánh các dịch vụ. Trong khi đó, mô hình Goal Question Metric (GQM) sử dụng phương pháp tiếp cận Total Quality Management (TQM), dựa trên giả định rằng trước tiên, các cá nhân hoặc tổ chức cần xác định mục tiêu cho các dự án của mình, sau đó theo dõi các mục tiêu dựa trên dữ liệu để xác định các mục tiêu đó. Cuối cùng, cung cấp một khung giúp dễ dàng đo lường dữ liệu liên quan đến các mục tiêu đã nêu. Điều này đòi hỏi phải làm rõ, ít nhất là ở mức độ chung, nhu cầu thông tin của tổ chức để có thể định lượng khi cần thiết và phân tích thông tin định lượng để đánh giá mức độ đạt được các mục tiêu hay không. GQM được chia thành ba cấp độ theo cấu trúc.

The development of invariant representations is a critical challenge in machine learning and pattern recognition. This paper introduces an innovative framework for transformation-invariant feature learning by integrating linear transformations into feature learning algorithms. Specifically, we propose the transformation-invariant restricted Boltzmann machine, which efficiently represents data through its weights and their transformations, attaining feature representation invariance via probabilistic max pooling. Moreover, we extend our transformation-invariant feature learning framework to encompass other unsupervised learning techniques, including autoencoders and sparse coding. Our method is evaluated on several image classification benchmark datasets, such as MNIST variations, CIFAR-10, and STL-10, demonstrating competitive or superior classification performance compared to current state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, our approach achieves state-of-the-art results in phone classification tasks using the TIMIT dataset, underscoring the broad applicability of our proposed algorithms across diverse domains.
