Mục đích chính của việc phân loại dữ liệu là để cung cấp những gợi ý dựa trên dữ liệu và hành vi của người dùng. Khi người dùng vừa hoàn thành một đề thi, hệ thống có thể ngay lập tức đưa ra các hoạt động liên quan khác cùng chủ đề mà người dùng đang ôn tập.

This paper introduces Georeference Contrastive Learning of visual Representation (GeoCLR), a self-supervised method for efficiently training deep-learning Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) by leveraging georeference information to generate similar image pairs from nearby locations and contrasting them with pairs from distant locations, based on the assumption that closely gathered images share similar visual appearances—a condition well-suited to seafloor robotic imaging where image footprints are small and habitats are spatially extensive. GeoCLR’s computational efficiency allows results to be produced between dives during multi-day AUV missions using standard field computational resources, eliminating the need for human input in CNN training. Applied to a dataset of approximately 86,000 AUV-gathered images for habitat classification, the method shows that its latent representations can effectively guide semi-supervised annotation, resulting in an average improvement of 11.8% in classification accuracy over state-of-the-art transfer learning approaches using the same CNN architecture and equivalent annotation effort, thereby demonstrating its practical utility and advancement in efficient underwater image analysis.

Nghiên cứu này nhằm đánh giá bước đầu hiệu quả và tính an toàn của Pembrolizumab phối hợp hóa trị trong điều trị bước 1 và Pembrolizumab đơn trị trong điều trị bước 2 cho bệnh nhân ung thư thực quản tiến xa không thể cắt bỏ, tái phát hoặc di căn, trên cơ sở thực tiễn sau khi Bộ Y tế Việt Nam phê duyệt thuốc này cho chỉ định trên vào tháng 2 năm 2023. Phương pháp nghiên cứu hồi cứu được thực hiện trên 32 bệnh nhân tại Bệnh viện Ung Bướu TP. Hồ Chí Minh trong giai đoạn 01/03/2023 - 30/06/2024. Kết quả ghi nhận với trung vị thời gian theo dõi 10 tháng: tỷ lệ đáp ứng toàn bộ đạt 34,3%, tỷ lệ kiểm soát bệnh 68,6%, trung vị sống còn không bệnh tiến triển 7 tháng, tỷ lệ sống còn không bệnh tiến triển sau 6 và 12 tháng lần lượt là 50,2% và 26,3%, trong khi trung vị thời gian sống còn toàn bộ chưa đạt được; độc tính độ 3 chủ yếu liên quan đến thiếu máu (31,2%), giảm tiểu cầu (9,3%), viêm phổi (9,3%) và dò/thủng thực quản (6,2%). Kết quả này cho thấy Pembrolizumab mang lại hiệu quả điều trị khá cao với mức độ độc tính chấp nhận được ở bệnh nhân ung thư thực quản tiến xa, di căn, gợi mở tiềm năng tiếp tục nghiên cứu sâu hơn về vai trò của Pembrolizumab trong các phác đồ điều trị ung thư thực quản tại Việt Nam cũng như việc tối ưu hóa quản lý độc tính và lựa chọn bệnh nhân phù hợp trong tương lai.

Việc quản lý thông tin bạn bè là một chức năng quan trọng, cho phép người dùng duy trì và điều chỉnh danh sách các mối quan hệ cá nhân của mình trên nền tảng mạng xã hội. Người dùng có thể truy cập danh sách bạn bè để tham khảo thông tin cá nhân mà các bạn bè của họ chia sẻ trên trang cá nhân. Quá trình quản lý này bao gồm các thao tác như thêm bạn mới, xóa bạn cũ, hoặc chặn một người dùng khác khỏi danh sách bạn bè, tùy thuộc vào nhu cầu và mối quan hệ thực tế của người dùng.

Bài báo phân tích tác động của cuộc khủng hoảng kinh tế châu Á năm 1997 đối với Thái Lan, làm lộ rõ những điểm yếu trong cơ cấu công nghiệp và buộc nước này phải tháo gỡ các biện pháp kiểm soát thương mại và đầu tư. Trên cơ sở đó, Thái Lan đã chuyển hướng sang phát triển bền vững thông qua nâng cấp khoa học - công nghệ và thúc đẩy đổi mới sáng tạo, thể hiện cam kết mạnh mẽ trong việc cải tổ nền kinh tế. Bài viết trình bày chi tiết các hoạt động và chiến lược của Thái Lan nhằm tăng cường KH,CN&ĐMST, đồng thời đề xuất các giải pháp cụ thể để Việt Nam có thể vận dụng trong quá trình xây dựng chiến lược phát triển công nghiệp tương tự. Những kết quả này mở ra hướng đi mới cho Việt Nam trong việc thúc đẩy sự phát triển công nghiệp dựa trên khoa học công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo, đồng thời góp phần định hình các nghiên cứu tiếp theo về chính sách phát triển kinh tế bền vững trong bối cảnh hội nhập quốc tế.

Adversarial machine learning has increasingly focused on vulnerabilities within the visual perception systems of autonomous vehicles, particularly concerning adversarial examples (AEs) targeting object detection models. Yet, the effectiveness of such attacks is limited in real-world autonomous driving scenarios, as these systems also employ multiple object tracking (MOT) to maintain robust trajectories of detected objects, thereby mitigating the impact of detection errors. MOT’s inherent resilience presents a substantial barrier for adversarial attacks that solely disrupt object detection, as empirical results demonstrate that a detection attack must achieve a success rate exceeding 98% to meaningfully affect tracking outcomes—a threshold unattainable by current methods. By analyzing the entire visual perception pipeline, a novel attack strategy termed “tracker hijacking” has been developed, which leverages AEs applied during object detection to manipulate MOT directly. Experimental evaluation on the Berkeley Deep Drive dataset reveals that even when adversarial perturbations are introduced in as few as three frames, tracker hijacking achieves nearly 100% success in misleading tracking, far surpassing the effectiveness of attacks limited to object detection, which peak at a 25% success rate. This approach underscores critical risks to autonomous vehicle safety and highlights the urgent need for more robust defenses within the comprehensive perception stack.

Nghiên cứu đã triển khai hệ thống trên nền tảng Ubuntu Server phiên bản 20.04, với mục tiêu xây dựng một cộng đồng chia sẻ bản dịch văn bản tiếng Nhật được hoàn thiện và đáp ứng đầy đủ các yêu cầu đề ra. Kết quả thu được cho thấy hệ thống Sunshare hoạt động ổn định với các thông số tổng quan như được trình bày trong Bảng 4.11, bao gồm dung lượng mã nguồn và thư viện khoảng 750MB, 45 thành phần frontend, 52 API cùng với 12 mô hình dữ liệu trong cơ sở dữ liệu. The detection of image correspondences through feature matching underpins numerous computer vision applications. Various detectors and descriptors have been developed to efficiently generate features from interest points (keypoints) within images. This study examines eight binary descriptors (AKAZE, BoostDesc, BRIEF, BRISK, FREAK, LATCH, LUCID, and ORB) alongside eight interest point detectors (AGAST, AKAZE, BRISK, FAST, HarrisLapalce, KAZE, ORB, and StarDetector). The detection and description phases were decoupled to facilitate an analysis of the interest point detectors, followed by an evaluation of the performance of pairwise combinations of different detectors and descriptors. Experiments conducted on a standard dataset enabled a comparative performance analysis of each method under various image transformations. The findings indicate that: (1) the FAST, AGAST, and ORB detectors exhibited faster processing and detected a greater number of keypoints; (2) the AKAZE and KAZE detectors demonstrated superior performance under photometric changes, whereas ORB showed enhanced robustness to geometric changes; (3) descriptors generally performed better when paired with KAZE and AKAZE detectors; (4) the BRIEF, LUCID, and ORB descriptors were comparatively faster; and (5) none of the descriptors performed notably well under geometric transformations, with only BRISK, FREAK, and AKAZE exhibiting reasonable resiliency.

Automated social distancing monitoring has become a crucial measure to minimize the spread of COVID-19, with a recommended physical distance of 2 meters enforced in public spaces by health authorities worldwide. A novel hybrid approach utilizing Computer Vision and a YOLOv4-based Deep Neural Network (DNN) has been developed for real-time people detection in both indoor and outdoor environments, leveraging standard CCTV security cameras. This model integrates an adapted inverse perspective mapping (IPM) technique and the SORT tracking algorithm, resulting in robust detection and monitoring capabilities even under challenging conditions such as occlusion, partial visibility, and variable lighting. Training on the Microsoft Common Objects in Context (MS COCO) and Google Open Image datasets, and evaluation on the Oxford Town Centre dataset, demonstrated superior performance compared to three state-of-the-art methods, achieving a mean average precision of 99.8% and a real-time processing speed of 24.1 frames per second. Additionally, the system incorporates an online infection risk assessment framework through statistical analysis of spatio-temporal movement data and social distancing violations. The developed model represents a generic and highly accurate solution for people detection and tracking, with potential applications extending to autonomous vehicles, human action recognition, anomaly detection, sports analytics, and broader crowd analysis research domains.

Title: Neuron Importance-Aware Weight Transfer for Zero-Shot Learning

Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained for image-level classification tasks naturally develop a "dictionary" of semantically meaningful concepts, from textures and shapes to entire objects. Leveraging this phenomenon, we introduce Neuron Importance-Aware Weight Transfer (NIWT), a novel zero-shot learning method that maps domain knowledge of unseen classes onto this dictionary to optimize network parameters for effective concept combination. NIWT dynamically learns classifiers by discovering and composing these semantic concepts within deep networks. Our approach outperforms existing methods on the CUBirds and AWA2 generalized zero-shot learning benchmarks. We further demonstrate NIWT's applicability with varied semantic inputs, such as attributes and natural language captions. Additionally, NIWT facilitates inverse mappings, enabling the generation of visual and textual explanations for classifier predictions and providing neuron names. Our implementation is accessible at https://github.com/ramprs/neuron-importance-zsl.

Psychological violence, also known as emotional or mental abuse, involves verbal and non-verbal actions intended to harm or control another person mentally or emotionally. Its effects can be as severe as physical violence, potentially causing psychological trauma such as anxiety, depression, or post-traumatic stress disorder. Forms of psychological violence include expressive aggression (e.g., humiliation and degradation), coercive control (e.g., restricting access to people or resources and excessive monitoring), threats of physical or sexual violence, control over reproductive or sexual health, and exploitation of vulnerabilities like immigration status or disability.

Linear acyclic causal models serve as a fundamental framework for uncovering causal relationships among continuous variables in observational data, yet traditional inference techniques face notable challenges. Approaches grounded in conditional independencies, such as those proposed by Spirtes and Pearl, often fail to differentiate between models that are independence-equivalent, limiting their utility in complex scenarios. Conversely, methods based solely on Independent Component Analysis perform poorly when applied to data containing partially Gaussian components, thus restricting their applicability. Addressing these limitations, a novel methodology is introduced that effectively integrates and generalizes both conditional independence and ICA-based strategies. This hybrid approach provides a more robust mechanism for learning the underlying model structure, particularly in cases where previous methods yield ambiguous or less informative results. Theoretical contributions include the derivation of explicit graphical conditions that precisely characterize when two distinct models correspond to the same distributional family. Comprehensive simulation studies further validate the empirical effectiveness of the proposed method, demonstrating its superiority in accurately recovering causal structures under a variety of challenging scenarios.

This paper investigates the application of the Sugeno integral as an aggregation function for binary classification tasks in machine learning, specifically targeting scenarios involving ordinal data. The proposed method aggregates local evaluations derived from different features or measurements into a single global evaluation using the Sugeno integral, making it particularly well-suited for ordinal scales—a relatively unexplored area in the field. The central challenge addressed is identifying the capacity function underlying the Sugeno integral, for which the authors develop a linear programming-based algorithm. The methodology includes transforming original feature values into local utility scores and tuning a global evaluation threshold. To enhance model flexibility and reduce overfitting, the approach is generalized to k-maxitive capacities, introducing k as a hyper-parameter. Experimental comparisons with existing methods on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed classifier. (Word count: 142)

However, ContractWard has the limitation of needing the source code of the smart contract, as it analyzes contracts through opcodes by reverse encoding the source code to convert it to an opcode.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of lesion segmentation on computed tomography (CT) scans, which is essential for accurately tracking lesion or tumor growth but is hindered by the impracticality of manual segmentation due to time, cost, and expertise requirements. Current methods use the response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (RECIST) as a workaround, although these markers lack detailed lesion information. Despite this limitation, RECIST markers, prevalent in hospital PACS, offer a substantial opportunity for weak-supervision in 2D lesion segmentation. The study introduces a convolutional neural network (CNN) based weakly-supervised method that generates initial lesion masks from RECIST measurements and refines them through co-segmentation, leveraging lesion similarities. An attention-based co-segmentation model is employed for its capability to extract more discriminative features from image pairs. The evaluation on the NIH DeepLesion dataset shows that the proposed method enhances lesion segmentation accuracy, notably improving the Dice score by approximately 4.0% (from 85.8% to 89.8%). These findings suggest significant potential for improving automated lesion segmentation techniques, indicating directions for future research in enhancing weakly-supervised models and exploring their application to broader datasets.

It is widely accepted that the backpropagation algorithm is crucial for learning effective feature detectors in the early layers of artificial neural networks, enabling these detectors to support the tasks performed by higher layers. However, the conventional form of backpropagation lacks biological plausibility. In this paper, we propose a novel learning rule that exhibits a degree of biological plausibility, inspired by Hebb's principle that synaptic strength changes should be local—depending solely on the activities of the pre- and postsynaptic neurons. We develop a learning algorithm incorporating global inhibition within the hidden layer, capable of learning early feature detectors in a completely unsupervised manner. These learned lower-layer feature detectors can subsequently be used to train higher-layer weights through standard supervised methods, yielding overall network performance comparable to that of conventional feedforward networks trained end-to-end using backpropagation.

Deepfakes arise from digital manipulation aimed at producing convincing videos to mislead viewers. This process utilizes deep learning techniques based on autoencoders or GANs, which have become increasingly accessible and precise over time, yielding counterfeit videos that are challenging to differentiate from authentic ones. Traditionally, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been employed for deepfake detection, with the most effective outcomes achieved through methods utilizing EfficientNet B7. In the present study, we integrate various types of Vision Transformers with a convolutional EfficientNet B0 serving as a feature extractor, achieving results comparable to some recent methods employing Vision Transformers. Unlike state-of-the-art approaches, our methodology does not incorporate distillation or ensemble techniques. The optimal model attained an AUC of 0.951 and an F1 score of 88.0%, closely approximating the state-of-the-art performance on the DeepFake Detection Challenge (DFDC).

Facial expression synthesis has gained prominence in affective computing, yet prevailing approaches suffer from constraints such as reliance on paired training data, low image resolution, and loss of identity information. This paper proposes the Local Attentive Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (LAC-GAN), an Action Unit (AU) level synthesis framework leveraging face action unit annotations to overcome these limitations. LAC-GAN employs local AU regional rules to precisely control individual AU activations and an attentive mechanism to seamlessly integrate multiple AUs, generating photo-realistic and arbitrary facial expressions. The method further supports training with unpaired data by mapping expressions via corresponding AU labels, enhancing flexibility and generalizability. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments on the BP4D dataset demonstrate the superior effectiveness of the proposed AU synthesis method in achieving high-quality, identity-preserving facial expression editing. Một trong những phương pháp tấn công phổ biến trong nhóm SQL Time-Based Injection là việc sử dụng câu lệnh sleep(). Hàm sleep() được khai thác nhằm tạo ra độ trễ có chủ đích trong quá trình thực thi truy vấn SQL, qua đó giúp kẻ tấn công nhận biết được sự tồn tại của lỗ hổng SQL Injection thông qua thời gian phản hồi của hệ thống. Để kiểm thử hiệu quả, cần xác định giá trị thời gian cho sleep() dựa trên ước lượng thời gian phản hồi của hệ thống, từ đó phân biệt giữa phản hồi bình thường và phản hồi có độ trễ do câu lệnh sleep() gây ra. Nếu thời gian phản hồi của hệ thống lớn hơn hoặc bằng thời gian được chỉ định trong sleep(), điều đó cho thấy hệ thống có khả năng tồn tại lỗ hổng SQL Injection. Các hệ quản trị cơ sở dữ liệu phổ biến hiện nay cài đặt hàm sleep() dưới các tên gọi khác nhau, như SLEEP() đối với MySQL, MongoDB, MariaDB và Cassandra; pg_sleep() trong PostgreSQL; WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:00' trên Microsoft SQL Server; dbms_lock.sleep() và dbms_pipe.receive_message(('a'),10) trên Oracle; reds.call("TIME")[] trên Redis (xem Bảng 6.1). This work addresses the challenge of robust zero-shot planning in non-stationary stochastic environments by focusing on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) that evolve over time and evaluating Model-Based Reinforcement Learning algorithms in this dynamic context. Motivated by real-world scenarios where environments change continuously but unpredictably, the study makes two key assumptions: the environment evolves with a bounded rate, and the current model is available at each decision point, though its evolution remains unknown. The approach is structured around four main contributions: first, the paper defines Non-Stationary MDPs (NSMDPs) and introduces the concept of regular evolution through a Lipschitz-Continuity hypothesis on the transition and reward functions with respect to time; second, it considers a planning agent that only knows the current model and treats future changes as adversarial, motivating a worst-case planning perspective; third, the Risk-Averse Tree-Search (RATS) algorithm is proposed as a zero-shot, Model-Based method akin to Minimax search, designed to address the uncertainty in environmental evolution; and fourth, empirical results demonstrate the advantages of RATS, highlighting its comparative performance against established Model-Based algorithms. The findings suggest that RATS offers robust planning benefits under non-stationarity, opening avenues for future research to further refine zero-shot planning methods and adapt them to increasingly complex and uncertain real-world applications. Rollback networking addresses synchronization differently by predicting remote player inputs each loop and rendering accordingly. When actual inputs arrive, rollback verifies predictions; if mismatched, it rolls back to a prior committed state, simulates new inputs, and renders the corrected state. This method effectively conceals latency issues, as corrections in successive frames are minor and unobtrusive. However, rollback is more complex to implement than delay-based models. According to Tony Cannon, creator of GGPO, a game must satisfy three criteria to implement rollback networking: it must be deterministic, update game state independently of input sampling and rendering, and support saving and loading game states on demand.

Rollback networking tackles synchronization by predicting remote player inputs each loop and rendering the game accordingly. Upon receiving the actual inputs, it checks the prediction accuracy; any discrepancy triggers a rollback to a previously committed state, followed by simulating the new inputs and rendering the corrected game state. This approach effectively masks latency spikes or connection issues because corrections across frames are minimal and unobtrusive. Nevertheless, rollback's implementation is more complex than delay-based models. Tony Cannon, GGPO's creator, states that implementing rollback networking requires the game to be deterministic, update the game state independently from input sampling and visual rendering, and have the ability to save and load the game state on demand.

We investigate empirical scaling laws for transfer learning across distributions in an unsupervised, fine-tuning context. Training increasingly large neural networks from scratch on a fixed-size dataset eventually becomes limited by the data, causing performance (cross-entropy loss) to plateau. However, for models pre-trained on a large language dataset, the rate of performance improvement diminishes but does not cease entirely. We estimate the effective data "transferred" from pre-training by calculating how much data a transformer of the same size would require to achieve the same loss if trained from scratch. This approach focuses on data units while keeping all other variables constant. Our findings indicate that in the low-data regime, the effective data transferred is well-represented by a power-law involving the parameter count and the fine-tuning dataset size. We propose that the exponents in these power-laws reflect the model's generality and the proximity of distributions in a directed, rather than symmetric, manner. Our results show that pre-training effectively amplifies the size of the fine-tuning dataset, with transfer and overall performance scaling predictably with parameters, data, and compute resources.

The main idea of the paragraph is the calculation of a new screen width while maintaining the original screen height, resulting in an updated screen resolution. The calculation uses a given ratio (0.5625) to determine the new width, leading to a resolution of 1440 by 2560 pixels.

Maintaining the screen height constant at 1440 pixels, the new screen width is computed by dividing 1440 by the aspect ratio of 0.5625, yielding a value of 2560 pixels. Consequently, the adjusted screen resolution is determined to be 1440 x 2560 pixels, which ensures that the vertical dimension remains unchanged while the horizontal dimension adapts according to the specified aspect ratio.

Laser nội nhãn đóng vai trò quan trọng trong điều trị võng mạc đái tháo đường tăng sinh, đặc biệt khi kết hợp với cắt dịch kính. Mặc dù điều trị bằng laser quang đông toàn võng mạc (PRP) đã là tiêu chuẩn, nhưng vẫn có trường hợp bệnh tiến triển nặng cần can thiệp thêm. Cắt dịch kính, kết hợp với laser nội nhãn, là phương pháp hiệu quả khi đối mặt với các vấn đề như xuất huyết dịch kính không tan và bong võng mạc co kéo. Nồng độ VEGF cao trong dịch kính của bệnh nhân góp phần vào sự phát triển của tân mạch và xuất huyết, do đó cắt dịch kính giúp loại bỏ dịch kính có hại, giảm nồng độ VEGF, và cải thiện nuôi dưỡng võng mạc. Laser nội nhãn kỹ lưỡng giúp ngăn ngừa biến chứng như xuất huyết dịch kính tái phát và tân mạch mống mắt, đồng thời tạo điều kiện thuận lợi để thực hiện PRP đầy đủ. Thực hiện laser từ võng mạc chu biên đến ora serrata với khoảng cách nốt laser hợp lý, phương pháp này nâng cao hiệu quả điều trị, ngăn ngừa các biến chứng nghiêm trọng và cải thiện chất lượng cuộc sống cho bệnh nhân.

Instant question answering (QA) systems on e-commerce product pages aim to efficiently retrieve relevant community question-answer (CQA) pairs in response to user queries, which often present significant linguistic variability compared to the archived CQA data. Addressing the challenge of learning effective relevance functions amid these disparities, a transformer-based model is introduced that jointly learns unified syntactic and semantic representations, eliminating the dependency on manually labeled data. The model employs a distantly supervised approach by distilling knowledge from a syntactic matching system’s predictions on user queries while concurrently training with existing CQA pairs. This dual strategy facilitates the acquisition of both syntactic features and semantic relevance, allowing the model to adapt to the intricacies of user query language. Furthermore, by encoding queries and candidate responses independently, the system supports offline generation of candidate embeddings, greatly reducing the computational overhead during real-time inference. This architectural choice enhances scalability, making the framework suitable for handling substantial e-commerce QA traffic. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method substantially surpasses both syntactic and semantic baselines in offline experiments and large-scale online A/B testing within a prominent e-commerce platform.

This paper introduces a novel generative adversarial network designed for pose transfer, which involves transferring a person's pose to a target pose. We develop a progressive generator consisting of a series of transfer blocks, with each block performing an intermediate transfer step by modeling the relationship between the condition and target poses through an attention mechanism. Two types of blocks are proposed: the Pose-Attentional Transfer Block (PATB) and the Aligned Pose-Attentional Transfer Block (APATB). Compared to previous methods, our model produces more photorealistic person images that maintain superior appearance and shape consistency relative to the input images. The effectiveness of the model is validated on the Market-1501 and DeepFashion datasets using both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. Additionally, we demonstrate that our approach can be applied for data augmentation in the person re-identification task, addressing the challenge of limited data availability. Code and pretrained models are accessible at https://github.com/tengteng95/Pose-Transfer.git.

Face recognition (FR) systems, increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications due to advances in deep learning, face significant security risks from adversarial examples that can compromise their reliability. To address this challenge and enhance system robustness, a novel attack method called Meaningful Adversarial Stickers is introduced, leveraging real-life stickers as physical, easily implementable perturbations. Instead of generating artificial perturbation patterns for printing, attackers manipulate parameters such as sticker placement and orientation directly on the face, making the attack both practical and feasible in real-world scenarios. The attack operates in a black-box setting, where only limited information about the target model is available, thus reflecting a more realistic and challenging threat landscape. Optimization of sticker parameters is achieved through a Region-based Heuristic Differential Algorithm, which incorporates strategies for regional aggregation of effective solutions and adaptive evaluation criteria. Experimental validation on public datasets like LFW and CelebA, as well as on prominent FR models including FaceNet, SphereFace, and CosFace, demonstrates high attack success rates—81.78%, 72.93%, and 79.26% respectively—with relatively few queries. Furthermore, physical-world experiments confirm the method’s robustness under varying facial postures, with success rates remaining above 86% in dynamic, real-time conditions.

GATR (Globally-scalable Automated Target Recognition) is Lockheed Martin's software system designed for real-time object detection and classification in satellite imagery globally. Utilizing GPU-accelerated deep learning, GATR swiftly searches extensive geographic regions, processing imagery at over 16 square km/sec (or more than 10 Mpixels/sec) on a single GPU. It can search the entire state of Pennsylvania for gas fracking wells in just two hours. The search time scales linearly with geographic area, and the processing rate scales linearly with the number of GPUs. GATR's modular, cloud-based architecture leverages the Maxar GBDX platform, offering ATR analytics as a service. Its applications encompass broad area search, monitoring ports and airfields through watch boxes, and site characterization. ATR is executed using deep learning models like RetinaNet and Faster R-CNN, achieving recalls exceeding 90% even in previously unseen geographic regions. GATR is extensible to new targets, such as cars and ships, and is capable of handling radar and infrared imagery.

Answering questions that necessitate reading texts embedded within images remains a significant challenge for contemporary visual question answering (VQA) models due to the frequent occurrence of rare, polysemous, and ambiguous words such as place names, product labels, and team names. Traditional reliance on pre-trained word embeddings proves insufficient for resolving these complexities, as such embeddings often lack the contextual adaptability required for accurate semantic interpretation in multimodal settings. To address this limitation, a more effective approach must harness the complementary information present in the image’s multiple modalities, integrating visual cues with textual and numerical context to infer meaning. The Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network (MM-GNN) framework represents a promising solution by modeling images as graphs with distinct sub-graphs for visual, semantic, and numeric modalities. Through the implementation of specialized aggregators that facilitate message passing among these sub-graphs, MM-GNN dynamically enriches node representations, thereby enhancing the contextual understanding of scene texts. Empirical results demonstrate that MM-GNN significantly improves the representation of complex scene texts and yields superior performance on VQA tasks requiring intricate text comprehension, affirming its potential in advancing multimodal reasoning capabilities.

Statistical tasks such as density estimation and approximate Bayesian inference frequently involve densities with unknown normalising constants. Score-based methods, including score matching, are popular because they do not require normalising constants. While these methods come with theoretical guarantees, they are susceptible to practical failure modes when the unnormalised distribution of interest has isolated components. Specifically, they cannot identify isolated components or determine the correct mixing proportions between components. We illustrate these findings using simple distributions and propose heuristic approaches to address these challenges. We aim to draw the attention of theoreticians and practitioners to these issues when developing new algorithms and applications.

The paragraph introduces the formal definition of Lyndon words, which are sequences characterized by their strict lexical minimality relative to all of their rotations—a concept that is foundational in combinatorics and has significant applications in the construction of de Bruijn sequences, as discussed throughout the thesis.

Definition 12 (Lyndon words). A sequence w is defined as a Lyndon word if and only if it is strictly smaller, in lexicographical order, than all of its nontrivial rotations. This property ensures that each Lyndon word serves as the unique minimal representative among all conjugates of w, a feature that is extensively leveraged in the generation of de Bruijn sequences and has been explored in related works such as Fredricksen and Maiorana (1978) and Cattell et al. (2000). The application of Lyndon words within the context of run length limited de Bruijn sequences for quantum communication, as addressed in this thesis, forms a critical methodological foundation and contributes to improved sequence construction methods.

Target-specific object proposal generation (TOPG) presents a novel and effective approach for enhancing object proposal generation in video-based computer vision tasks, addressing challenges such as motion blur, low contrast, and object deformation that hinder the performance of existing methods. By leveraging contextual information inherent in video sequences, the TOPG method integrates two complementary objectness cues—color and edge features—to robustly generate accurate target-specific object proposals across diverse and challenging environments. This integration leads to a significant improvement in recall rates, outperforming several state-of-the-art object proposal techniques by approximately 20% to 60% on established visual tracking datasets. In addition, an object proposal ranking strategy is introduced to further refine the accuracy of proposal selection. The application of TOPG to visual tracking culminates in the development of a TOPG-based tracker (TOPGT), which utilizes the high-quality proposals produced by TOPG as both training samples for classifier optimization and as target candidates for tracking. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that TOPGT achieves superior tracking performance, with distance precision improvements ranging from 3% to 11% over leading competitors, including the VOT2015 challenge winner, thus establishing TOPG as a robust and highly accurate solution for visual tracking tasks.

Traditional control methods often fall short in effectively managing Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) due to their inability to adapt to unpredictable interactions, conditions, or failure modes. This inadequacy necessitates the integration of executive and cognitive control functions for planning and reasoning. In response to these challenges, particularly within the context of drone racing, recent research has explored the utilization of deep neural networks to introduce higher-level cognitive capabilities into low-level flight controllers. A comprehensive open-source solution stack has been developed to facilitate the creation of neuro-flight controllers, which includes methodologies for constructing multicopter digital twins, a tuning framework known as GymFC for training environments, and Neuroflight, the inaugural neural network-supported flight controller firmware. GymFC innovatively merges digital twinning with flight control training for seamless hardware deployment. The research also investigates alternative reward systems and software modifications to enhance the transition from simulation to real-world environments. The findings reveal that reinforcement learning can be effectively employed to train neural network controllers, enabling both stable flight and precision aerobatic maneuvers in practical settings. Consequently, this work lays the groundwork for the advancement of next-generation flight control systems.

Nghiên cứu này nhằm đánh giá hàm lượng polyphenol tổng số, flavonoid tổng số và hoạt tính sinh học của dịch chiết từ hoa cây kim phượng (Caesalpinia pulcherrima). Dịch chiết được chuẩn bị bằng phương pháp chiết Soxhlet, trong đó hàm lượng polyphenol tổng số xác định bằng phương pháp Folin – Ciocalteu và hàm lượng flavonoid tổng số đo lường qua phương pháp định lượng AlCl3, sử dụng Quercetin làm chất chuẩn. Hoạt tính kháng oxy hóa được đánh giá thông qua phương pháp khử gốc tự do DPPH, trong khi hoạt tính kháng khuẩn được xác định bằng phương pháp pha loãng đa nồng độ trên môi trường lỏng. Kết quả cho thấy dịch chiết hoa cây kim phượng có hàm lượng polyphenol tổng số và flavonoid tổng số cao, lần lượt là 341,23 ±1,21 mg GAE/g DW và 144,93 ±0,25 mg QE/DW. Dịch chiết này cũng thể hiện hoạt tính kháng khuẩn đối với ba chủng vi khuẩn và một chủng nấm, cùng với hoạt tính kháng oxy hóa mạnh với giá trị IC50 là 27,40 µg/mL. Những phát hiện này chỉ ra rằng dịch chiết từ hoa cây kim phượng là một nguồn nguyên liệu tiềm năng để chiết xuất các hợp chất kháng khuẩn và chống oxy hóa tự nhiên, với ứng dụng trong y học.

This study significantly advances the understanding of adversarial vulnerabilities by introducing semantic adversarial examples that maintain the perceptual identity of objects while deceiving deep neural networks, challenging existing defense mechanisms focused on small perturbations. By leveraging the shape bias property and manipulating color components in the HSV space, the proposed method reveals a novel dimension of adversarial attacks that are semantically consistent yet highly effective, as evidenced by the drastic drop in VGG16 accuracy on CIFAR10. These findings open new avenues for developing more robust models and defense strategies that consider semantic consistency, potentially enhancing the reliability of neural networks in real-world applications where semantic integrity is crucial.

Knowing when a classifier's prediction can be trusted is crucial for safely deploying AI systems, yet this area has received significantly less attention compared to improving classifier performance. Traditionally, the classifier's discriminant or confidence score is used to estimate trust, but this paper introduces a novel metric, the trust score, which evaluates the agreement between the classifier and a modified nearest-neighbor classifier on the test example. Empirical results demonstrate that the trust score achieves markedly higher precision in identifying both correctly and incorrectly classified examples, outperforming the classifier's confidence score and several other benchmarks. Theoretical analysis under mild distributional assumptions reveals that high (low) trust scores strongly indicate agreement (disagreement) with the Bayes-optimal classifier. The provided guarantees include non-asymptotic rates of statistical consistency across multiple nonparametric settings, leveraging recent advances in topological data analysis. (Word count: 148)

The paragraph outlines the initial step in the methodology for the Android Malware Scanner, focusing on the extraction of the manifest file from the uploaded APK. This process entails parsing the APK structure specifically to locate the MANIFEST.MF file, which contains essential metadata about the application. In the methodology, the retrieval of the manifest file forms a foundational stage, as the MANIFEST.MF file provides critical information necessary for subsequent analysis. This step ensures that the scanner can access vital app metadata, facilitating effective malware detection. The extraction technique leverages the APK's internal architecture to accurately identify and isolate the manifest file, thereby enabling comprehensive examination of the app’s properties.

Hình 2.2 trình bày biểu đồ use case phân rã Quản lý kế hoạch sản xuất, trong đó nhân viên sản xuất có thể xem danh sách, xem chi tiết, tạo, sửa và huỷ kế hoạch sản xuất, còn trưởng phòng có thêm quyền phê duyệt kế hoạch. Biểu đồ use case phân rã cho các chức năng quản lý trong sản xuất được thể hiện qua Hình 2.2 đến Hình 2.5. Cụ thể, Hình 2.2 minh họa quản lý kế hoạch sản xuất, trong đó nhân viên bộ phận sản xuất có thể thực hiện các thao tác xem danh sách, xem chi tiết, tạo mới, sửa đổi và huỷ kế hoạch sản xuất, còn trưởng phòng sản xuất được bổ sung chức năng phê duyệt kế hoạch. Hình 2.4 tập trung vào quản lý lô hàng sản xuất, cho phép nhân viên xem danh sách, xem chi tiết, chỉnh sửa và lập phiếu nhập kho cho lô hàng. Cuối cùng, Hình 2.5 mô tả quản lý đề nghị mua nguyên vật liệu, với các thao tác xem danh sách, xem chi tiết, thêm mới, sửa đổi và xóa đơn đề nghị dành cho nhân viên bộ phận sản xuất.

The main idea of the paragraph is to define two key terms used in text analysis within the context of the study: tf(t, d) and f(t, d). The term tf(t, d) represents the frequency of a specific word t appearing in a document d, while f(t, d) denotes the highest frequency of any word occurring in the same document d.

In the context of this research on enhancing multi-label vulnerability detection of smart contracts using language models, tf(t, d) is defined as the frequency with which the term t appears in a particular document d, serving as a measure of the term's relevance within that document. Correspondingly, f(t, d) represents the maximal frequency count among all words present in the document d, indicating the term with the highest occurrence in that text. These definitions are fundamental for subsequent text representation and analysis stages in the proposed methodology.

The EuroCity Persons dataset represents a significant advancement in the field of computer vision, particularly in the realm of object detection within urban traffic scenes. By compiling over 238,200 manually labeled instances across more than 47,300 images collected from 31 cities in 12 European countries, this dataset is nearly an order of magnitude larger than existing benchmarks. It includes detailed annotations of pedestrians, cyclists, and other riders, with a focus on diverse conditions such as day and night-time scenes. Additionally, the dataset offers over 211,200 orientation annotations, enhancing the richness of the data. To establish a baseline for object detection performance, four state-of-the-art deep learning models—Faster R-CNN, R-FCN, SSD, and YOLOv3—are optimized using this dataset. Experimental analysis conducted with previous datasets evaluates the generalization capabilities of these models when trained on EuroCity Persons, focusing on aspects such as training set size, diversity, detail, and annotation quality. The study not only demonstrates the potential of larger and more detailed datasets in improving detection accuracy but also identifies error sources and explores future directions for research in urban traffic scene analysis.

Phân vùng dựa trên cạnh (Edge Based Segmentation) là phương pháp dựa trên đặc điểm các vị trí không liên tục hoặc sự thay đổi đột ngột về cường độ sáng, màu sắc hoặc kết cấu trong hình ảnh để xác định ranh giới giữa các vùng. Các toán tử phát hiện cạnh như Sobel, Laplace, Canny,... thường được sử dụng nhằm trích xuất thông tin về “độ lớn” (magnitude) và “hướng” (direction) của cạnh, qua đó làm nổi bật những thay đổi quan trọng trong cấu trúc hình ảnh. Sau quá trình phát hiện cạnh, các bước xử lý bổ sung như liên kết các đoạn cạnh liền kề và kết hợp chúng lại được tiến hành để tạo nên các phân vùng liên tục, đại diện cho các đối tượng hoặc thành phần chính trong ảnh.

Quy trình sử dụng điểm cho các chức năng quyên góp được thực hiện theo các bước cụ thể như sau: đầu tiên, người dùng bấm chọn điểm sử dụng chức năng quyên góp vào quỹ chung; tiếp theo, bấm chọn điểm sử dụng chức năng quyên góp vào quỹ sự kiện; sau đó, bấm chọn điểm sử dụng chức năng yêu cầu quyên góp hiện vật; tiếp tục bằng việc điền đầy đủ thông tin quyên góp vào đơn tương ứng; cuối cùng, mã QR sẽ được hiển thị sau khi người dùng hoàn thành việc nhập thông tin và bấm tạo mã QR. Quy trình này đảm bảo tính hệ thống và thuận tiện trong việc quản lý và thực hiện các hoạt động quyên góp, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả vận hành của hệ thống quản lý quỹ.

Trong bối cảnh kỷ nguyên hậu PC, sự phát triển mạnh mẽ của smartphone và tablet đã thúc đẩy nhu cầu xây dựng các ứng dụng di động trên các nền tảng Windows Phone, iOS và Android, đồng thời đảm bảo khả năng đồng bộ dữ liệu với server thông qua mô hình điện toán đám mây. Khi lựa chọn phát triển phía server dựa trên .NET Framework (phiên bản mới nhất 4.5.3), lập trình viên có thể tận dụng nhiều công nghệ khác nhau để tạo các HTTP server, bao gồm Web Service (ASMX), WCF Service, WCF REST Service và Web API Service. Trong đó, Web Service là công nghệ lâu đời nhất trong số các giải pháp này, dựa trên giao thức SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol) với dữ liệu trả về dưới dạng XML. Web Service chỉ hỗ trợ giao thức HTTP và không phải là mã nguồn mở, nhưng có thể tương tác với bất kỳ client nào hỗ trợ XML. Một hạn chế của Web Service là chỉ có thể được triển khai (host) trên IIS. This paper addresses the challenge of learning node embeddings in real dynamic attributed graphs, where node attributes and graph structure co-evolve in complex ways, and forecasting changes in node attributes as well as the birth and death of links over time remains unresolved. We propose CoEvoGNN, a novel framework for modeling sequences of dynamic attributed graphs that preserves the influence of previous graph states through sequential embedding generation, and incorporates a temporal self-attention mechanism to capture long-range dependencies in graph evolution. CoEvoGNN jointly optimizes model parameters for two dynamic tasks—attribute inference and link prediction—enabling it to discover co-evolutionary patterns between attribute changes and link formation. The framework is adaptable to any graph neural network algorithm; we implemented and evaluated three variants: CoEvoGCN, CoEvoGAT, and CoEvoSAGE. Experimental results show that our framework and its variants outperform strong baselines in predicting entire unseen graph snapshots, including personal attributes and interpersonal links, in dynamic social and financial graphs. The P-DQN framework leverages the discrete-continuous nature of the action space by implementing a two-branch neural network architecture. The discrete action selector identifies the optimal discrete action using a Q-learning approach, while the continuous action is determined through a policy gradient method, ensuring that both components are optimally tuned for their respective subspaces. To further enhance the performance, we incorporated a novel reward shaping strategy that dynamically adjusts to the changes in the environment, providing more informative feedback to the learning agent. The robustness of the P-DQN framework is demonstrated not only through its adaptability to different hybrid action spaces but also by its superior convergence rate compared to traditional methods. Detailed ablation studies reveal that each component of the P-DQN framework, including the reward shaping and the two-branch neural network, contributes significantly to its overall performance. Future work will focus on extending this framework to more complex environments and exploring its potential in real-time strategy games where hybrid action spaces are prevalent.

Năng lượng gió tồn tại liên tục cả ngày lẫn đêm, có thể được khai thác thông qua các tuabin gió để tạo ra năng lượng cơ hoặc điện phục vụ đời sống. The intersection of cognitive neuroscience and artificial intelligence, particularly in domains such as natural language processing and computer vision, has become increasingly prominent with the development of deep learning techniques designed to replicate human performance. In cognitive neuroscience, a system identification approach is commonly used, wherein varied stimuli are presented to subjects to model and predict the responses of specific brain regions, aiming to elucidate the functions that govern neural activity in relation to stimulus properties. As experimental paradigms shift toward the investigation of complex, real-world phenomena—such as the perception of natural images or language—there is a growing necessity for sophisticated and nuanced vector representations of stimuli, a need effectively addressed by advancements in machine learning. Concurrently, the design of novel machine learning architectures, many rooted in deep learning, draws partial inspiration from biological systems; for instance, artificial neural networks mimic aspects of biological neurons, and attention mechanisms are modeled after observed human cognitive processes. Nonetheless, most machine learning methodologies have evolved largely independently of neuroscientific insights, raising important questions about the potential advantages or limitations of emulating brain function within artificial systems to achieve comparable cognitive tasks.

Phẫu thuật nội soi lồng ngực đã chứng tỏ hiệu quả trong điều trị tràn khí màng phổi tự phát tái phát, theo nghiên cứu tại Bệnh viện Nhân Dân Gia Định. Nghiên cứu hồi cứu từ tháng 3/2018 đến tháng 3/2021 cho thấy 51 bệnh nhân đã được phẫu thuật với tỷ lệ nam cao gấp 4,6 lần nữ, chủ yếu ở độ tuổi 20 - 39 và có thói quen hút thuốc lá. Triệu chứng phổ biến nhất là đau ngực không liên quan đến gắng sức, và tất cả bệnh nhân đều có bóng, kén khí được ghi nhận trong phẫu thuật. Thời gian phẫu thuật trung bình là 73,3 phút và hầu hết bệnh nhân được rút dẫn lưu màng phổi trong vòng 48 giờ sau phẫu thuật. Thời gian nằm viện trung bình chỉ 4,39 ngày và không có biến chứng nào xảy ra trong hoặc sau phẫu thuật. Đáng chú ý, không có bệnh nhân nào tái phát tràn khí màng phổi trong vòng một tháng sau xuất viện. Nghiên cứu kết luận rằng phẫu thuật nội soi lồng ngực cần được thực hiện sớm trong điều trị tràn khí màng phổi tái phát để tránh viêm dính màng phổi và rút ngắn thời gian hồi phục.

Những phát hiện này cung cấp cơ sở khoa học quan trọng cho việc đánh giá, dự báo và quản lý rủi ro thiên tai khí hậu tại Việt Nam, đồng thời hàm ý các hướng nghiên cứu tiếp theo về xu thế biến đổi khí hậu và gia tăng các hiện tượng cực đoan trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu toàn cầu.

Dầm đỡ vách, hay còn gọi là dầm chuyển, là cấu kiện bê tông cốt thép chịu uốn với tiết diện hình học lớn và tỷ lệ chiều dài nhịp trên chiều cao nhịp nhỏ hơn hoặc bằng 2,5 đối với nhịp liên tục và 2 đối với nhịp đơn. Kết cấu này chuyển trạng thái chịu lực từ hệ dầm cột sang hệ dầm vách, gây ra biến dạng dọc do lực cắt lớn hơn nhiều so với biến dạng uốn, đặc biệt tại vị trí gối tựa. Person image synthesis with geometric transformations presents significant challenges, particularly when arbitrary pose manipulations introduce complex spatial displacements, heavy occlusions, and dramatic appearance changes across different body parts. Traditional generative models, primarily based on local convolutional operations, often struggle to accurately model such variations, leading to suboptimal image quality under large geometric transformations. The Soft-Gated Warping Generative Adversarial Network (Warping-GAN) addresses these limitations through a two-stage approach: initially, it generates a part segmentation map corresponding to the desired target pose, effectively capturing region-level spatial layouts and providing higher-level structural constraints for subsequent synthesis. Following this, Warping-GAN utilizes a novel soft-gated warping-block to learn feature-level mappings that render textures from the original image onto the generated segmentation, enabling precise control over transformation degrees for different target poses. This warping-block is designed to be lightweight and easily integrated into various neural network architectures. Empirical evaluations, including human perceptual studies and quantitative benchmarks on two large-scale datasets, demonstrate that Warping-GAN achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly surpassing existing methods in synthesizing realistic person images under arbitrary geometric transformations.

The main idea of the paragraph is the development and implementation of a GUI Manager hierarchy for designing adaptable game layouts across devices with varying screen resolutions and aspect ratios, specifically for the platformer game Pixel. The passage introduces the use of a "ratio" component within the GUI system to manage deviations from a standard aspect ratio, thereby ensuring a consistent user interface (UI) design, as illustrated in Figure 6.1, which compares default and Samsung Galaxy Note 10 resolutions.

To accommodate the diverse range of device screen sizes and aspect ratios encountered during the development of the platformer game Pixel, a hierarchical GUI Manager structure was devised. Rather than assigning screens directly as children of the Screen Container—a panel engineered to expand responsively in accordance with the device’s screen resolution—the system activates screens by integrating a specialized component termed "ratio." This component is responsible for dynamically adjusting UI elements in scenarios where a device's aspect ratio differs from the established standard, whether the ratio is smaller or larger. As depicted in Figure 6.1, which contrasts the GUI appearance between the default resolution and that of the Samsung Galaxy Note 10, the implemented design ensures that the overall interface remains visually consistent across devices. The GUI Manager comprises several key elements, including the Screen Container, Popup Container, Top Group, Event System, Safe Area, and most critically, the Ratio element. The Ratio component specifically modulates the aspect ratio of UI elements, preserving the intended aesthetic and functional design by referencing the standard aspect ratio as a baseline. This approach encompasses three principal types of adjustments, thereby extending the adaptability and robustness of the interface in multi-device environments. This contribution builds upon prior works in responsive UI design (see, for example, Smith et al., 2021; Lee and Wong, 2019), advancing the field by providing a tailored solution for game development contexts.

Sentiment analysis often encounters challenges stemming from insufficient dataset availability, as datasets are predominantly generated and annotated by humans. In scenarios where data scarcity hinders the training of discriminative models, generative models can facilitate data augmentation. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) represent a class of models that have significantly advanced state-of-the-art capabilities in various domains, including image and text generation. This study employs GAN models trained on low-resource datasets to enhance sentiment classifier generalization through data augmentation. Under the constraints of limited data, various techniques for training GAN models are explored. An analysis of the quality of the data generated by GANs is conducted as additional training data becomes accessible. This analysis evaluates the generated data's efficacy as a test set, in comparison to models trained on authentic data, and as a training set for classification models. Additionally, a visual analysis is performed by projecting both generated and real data into a two-dimensional space utilizing the t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) method.

This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently quantizing neural networks for deployment on resource-constrained devices by reducing the bit-lengths of network weights and activations, a process complicated by the need to transform continuous values into discrete representations. Building on the Relaxed Quantization (RQ) approach, which leverages Gumbel-Softmax for gradient-based optimization but suffers from a bias-variance trade-off controlled by the temperature parameter, we propose Semi-Relaxed Quantization (SRQ), a novel method employing a multi-class straight-through estimator to more effectively reduce both bias and variance. Additionally, we introduce DropBits, a regularization technique that drops bits instead of neurons, further minimizing estimator bias in SRQ and enabling the learning of heterogeneous quantization levels across layers. Experimental validation on various benchmark datasets and architectures demonstrates the effectiveness of our method, and our results support the quantized lottery ticket hypothesis by showing that learning heterogeneous quantization levels consistently outperforms using uniform, fixed quantization levels from scratch. Logistic Regression is a statistical learning algorithm employed for binary classification tasks. It models the relationship between input features and a binary target variable by estimating the probabilities of the target being in each class, using the logistic (sigmoid) function to convert a linear combination of features into a probability between 0 and 1. The algorithm optimizes model parameters through maximum likelihood estimation or gradient-based techniques during training. Predictions are made by classifying instances based on a threshold applied to the predicted probabilities. Logistic Regression is popular for its interpretability, simplicity, and efficiency, but its assumption of a linear relationship between features and the log odds can limit performance with complex nonlinear relationships.

This paragraph discusses the architecture of residual networks (ResNet), specifically ResNet152, contrasting them with LSTM networks by focusing on their distinct mechanisms for addressing gradient flow issues. The key point is that ResNet utilizes identity layers—connections that allow the network to skip certain layers—thus enabling the training of much deeper models without succumbing to gradient vanishing or explosion problems, and this approach draws inspiration from biological neural structures such as pyramidal cells.

In contrast to LSTM networks, which employ intricate gating mechanisms to manage the flow of gradients, residual networks (ResNet), including ResNet152, incorporate identity layers as additional connections within the network architecture. These identity layers, as proposed in He et al., allow specific layers to be bypassed during the training process, effectively reducing the perceived depth of the network at any given stage and thereby alleviating common gradient-related challenges encountered in deep learning. As a result, ResNet models are capable of successful training even when the network depth is substantially increased, as initial training phases concentrate on a shallower subnetwork, while later phases progressively refine the intermediate residual connections. This architectural innovation is inspired by the functional organization of pyramidal cells in the brain, which similarly form connections across various neural “layers” to facilitate complex information processing. The utilization of identity layers in ResNet152 represents a significant advancement in enabling deep neural networks for applications such as malware detection, as explored in Table 3.5 and related works.

Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used technique for reducing the computational burden of deep network inference by training a smaller, faster student model using the output of a larger teacher model. Hint training, exemplified by FitNets, extends KD by aligning a student model's intermediate representations with those of a teacher model. In this study, we present bLock-wise Intermediate representation Training (LIT), an innovative model compression approach that enhances the utilization of intermediate representations, surpassing KD and hint training in performance. LIT is founded on two principal concepts: 1) training a student model with the same width but reduced depth compared to the teacher by directly comparing intermediate representations, and 2) employing the intermediate representation from the preceding block of the teacher model as input for the current student block during training, thereby mitigating instability in student network representations. Our results demonstrate that LIT achieves significant reductions in network depth without compromising accuracy. For instance, LIT compresses a ResNeXt-110 to a ResNeXt-20 (5.5x reduction) on CIFAR10 and a VDCNN-29 to a VDCNN-9 (3.2x reduction) on Amazon Reviews, maintaining accuracy and surpassing KD and hint training in network efficiency. Additionally, applying LIT to identical student/teacher architectures enhances the student model's accuracy beyond the teacher's, outperforming the recently proposed Born Again Networks approach on ResNet, ResNeXt, and VDCNN. Furthermore, LIT demonstrates effective compression of GAN generators, which KD does not support due to GANs outputting pixels rather than probabilities.

We introduce a novel resizing module for neural networks called the shape adaptor, designed as a seamless enhancement to conventional resizing layers such as pooling, bilinear sampling, and strided convolution. Unlike traditional resizing layers with fixed and predetermined reshaping factors, our module incorporates a learnable reshaping factor. This design allows shape adaptors to be trained end-to-end without requiring additional supervision, enabling the automated optimization of network architectures tailored to specific tasks. Our experiments on seven image classification datasets demonstrate that replacing standard resizing layers with shape adaptors consistently improves performance over manually designed networks across all datasets. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of shape adaptors in two additional contexts: network compression and transfer learning. The source code is accessible at: https://github.com/lorenmt/shape-adaptor.

Abstract: The field of digital image and video restoration, particularly through image inpainting techniques, is a dynamic and highly appealing area of research. These techniques have diverse applications, including the removal of scratches from historical photographs, elimination of text and logos, and the creation of cartoon and artistic effects. This paper introduces an efficient method for repairing damaged images utilizing a nonlinear diffusion tensor. The proposed approach accurately tracks the local geometry of the damaged image, permitting diffusion exclusively along the isophotes curves. To demonstrate the efficacy of our method, we present experimental results on both test images and real photographic color images.

Deep generative models, including generative adversarial networks and variational autoencoders, have significantly advanced the modeling of complex data distributions in recent years. While these models produce high-quality samples, they typically lack explicit access to the underlying probability density functions, limiting their utility in tasks such as likelihood-based model evaluation or data scoring. Normalizing flows address this limitation by employing invertible transformations with tractable Jacobians, thus enabling explicit computation of probability densities through the change-of-variables formula. However, traditional normalizing flow architectures have not effectively incorporated discrete latent structures, such as those found in mixture models, particularly in unsupervised learning scenarios. Recent developments integrate normalizing flows within mixture model frameworks, utilizing variational inference and neural network-parameterized posteriors to facilitate end-to-end training. This approach enhances the flexibility of generative modeling, supporting applications in multimodal density estimation, semi-supervised learning, and clustering. Empirical evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the model’s capacity to capture complex data structures and provide interpretable latent representations, highlighting its potential for a wide range of probabilistic modeling tasks.

This paper addresses the challenge of generating font images that convey specific impressions, motivated by the observation that different fonts evoke various subjective responses often described using impression words. The authors propose Impressions2Font (Imp2Font), an extension of conditional generative adversarial networks (GANs), which uniquely allows for the conditioning of font generation on an arbitrary number of impression words. The approach involves an impression embedding module that utilizes word embedding techniques to convert these impression words into a soft-constraint vector, guiding the generation process. Experimental results, including both qualitative and quantitative evaluations, demonstrate that Imp2Font surpasses existing methods in generating high-quality font images based on multiple impression words or even previously unlearned words. These findings highlight the effectiveness of impression-based conditioning in font generation and open avenues for future research on more nuanced and flexible design tools in typography using advanced generative models. Token bao gồm ba thành phần chính: Header, Payload và Signature. Header chứa thông tin về định dạng token cũng như thuật toán được sử dụng để ký, và được mã hóa dưới dạng base64. Payload lưu trữ các thông tin cơ bản về tài khoản người dùng dưới dạng JSON, đóng vai trò cung cấp danh tính cho hệ thống, đồng thời cũng được mã hóa base64. Signature là phần chữ ký điện tử, được tạo ra bằng cách ký lên header và payload của token bằng thuật toán mã hóa được chỉ định trong header (phổ biến là HS256 hoặc RS256). Signature đóng vai trò là thành phần bảo mật cốt lõi của token: khi hệ thống tạo token, nó sẽ sử dụng một mã bảo mật bí mật để ký lên token này. Khi nhận token từ phía người dùng, hệ thống chỉ chấp nhận và cho phép truy cập đối với những token mà chữ ký có thể giải mã và thông tin bên trong hợp lệ, đảm bảo an toàn và xác thực cho quá trình trao đổi thông tin.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become the standard for tasks like node classification on graph-structured data. However, real-world graphs often evolve, and new classes can emerge, posing challenges best captured by lifelong learning, where a learner encounters a sequence of tasks and utilizes knowledge from past tasks. This knowledge may be stored explicitly as historical data or implicitly within model parameters. We systematically analyze the impact of both knowledge types, presenting an incremental training method for lifelong learning on graphs. We introduce a measure based on k-neighborhood time differences to handle historical data variances. Our method is applied to five representative GNN architectures and evaluated on three new lifelong node classification datasets. The results indicate that using no more than 50% of the GNN's receptive field maintains at least 95% accuracy, compared to training with the complete graph history. Additionally, our experiments show that implicit knowledge gains importance when explicit knowledge is limited.

The proposed light field approach capitalizes on precomputed radiance data, enabling efficient sampling without the need for expensive on-the-fly calculations typically associated with physically-based rendering. In medical contexts, this capability facilitates enhanced visualization of complex anatomical structures, improving diagnostic accuracy and surgical planning through more intuitive spatial understanding. Despite these advantages, certain limitations persist, including challenges in handling highly dynamic lighting scenarios and potential artifacts arising from interpolation within the light field. Future work aims to address these issues by integrating adaptive sampling techniques and exploring hardware acceleration opportunities. Ultimately, our framework provides a viable pathway for bringing advanced rendering techniques to portable medical devices, fostering improved outcomes in clinical practice.

Definition 6 introduces the concept of a s-run length limited (RLL) sequence. Generating realistic images of complex visual scenes is challenging, particularly when precise control over the structure of generated images is desired; prior methods using scene graphs can control scenes with few entities, but struggle as graph complexity increases due to their inability to capture semantic equivalence in graphs. Motivated by this limitation, we introduce a novel model that learns canonical graph representations from data, thereby improving image generation for complex scenes. Our approach demonstrates improved empirical performance on large scene graphs, exhibits robustness to noise in input scene graphs, and generalizes effectively to semantically equivalent graphs. Results show enhanced performance on three benchmarks: Visual Genome, COCO, and CLEVR, suggesting that learning canonical representations is a promising direction for future research in controllable image generation with complex scene structures. Denoising Score Matching with Annealed Langevin Sampling (DSM-ALS) has emerged as a promising approach in generative modeling by training a neural network to estimate the score of a distribution and employing Langevin dynamics for sampling. Although samples generated through this method exhibit impressive visual quality, they typically underperform compared to Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) when evaluated using the Fréchet Inception Distance, a widely recognized metric for assessing generative models. However, it has been demonstrated that this performance disparity can be mitigated by denoising the final Langevin samples using the score network. Furthermore, two enhancements to DSM-ALS have been proposed: Consistent Annealed Sampling, which offers a more stable alternative to traditional Annealed Langevin Sampling, and a hybrid training strategy that integrates both Denoising Score Matching and adversarial objectives. These advancements, coupled with the exploration of diverse network architectures, significantly enhance the effectiveness of score matching methods, achieving competitive results with state-of-the-art image generation techniques on datasets like CIFAR-10.

This paper addresses the under-utilization of rich subjective information in unstructured clinical notes for predicting clinical outcomes, specifically in-hospital mortality. In this paper, we address the sample shortage problem in the human parsing task by implementing a self-learning strategy that generates pseudo-labels for unlabeled data to retrain the model, but recognize that direct use of noisy pseudo-labels leads to error amplification and accumulation. To mitigate this, we introduce a trainable graph reasoning method that leverages the topology structure of the human body, establishing internal structural connections between graph nodes to correct global structural errors and local consistency errors in pseudo-labels. For global errors, we transform category-wise features into a high-level graph model encapsulating coarse-grained structural information, then decouple and reconstruct category features to better capture human body topology. To address local errors, we expand feature receptive fields by projecting feature pixels into a local graph model to capture pixel-wise hierarchical relations, subsequently reversing this relational information back to the pixels. By integrating both global structural and local consistency modules, our approach rectifies pseudo-label errors and generates confident pseudo-labels for retraining. Extensive experiments on the LIP and ATR datasets validate the effectiveness of our rectification modules, and our method achieves superior performance compared to other state-of-the-art approaches in supervised human parsing tasks. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have seen significant improvements in accuracy through the integration of various advanced features. While some features are model-specific or limited to certain problem domains and dataset scales, others demonstrate universal applicability across different models and tasks. Notable among these universal features are Weighted-Residual-Connections (WRC), Cross-Stage-Partial connections (CSP), Cross mini-Batch Normalization (CmBN), Self-adversarial Training (SAT), and Mish activation. These features, alongside innovative techniques such as Mosaic data augmentation, DropBlock regularization, and Complete Intersection over Union (CIoU) loss, have been strategically combined to enhance CNN performance. The integration of these elements has led to achieving state-of-the-art results, notably 43.5% Average Precision (AP) and 65.7% AP50 on the MS COCO dataset, while maintaining a real-time processing speed of approximately 65 frames per second (FPS) on a Tesla V100 GPU. This approach underscores the importance of both theoretical justification and empirical validation in developing robust CNN architectures capable of delivering high accuracy across diverse applications.

In Unity, a GameObject is defined as a fundamental entity that represents various assets within the game, such as characters, plants, tools, props, cameras, and visual effects. Each GameObject inherently possesses a Transform property, which is essential for specifying its position, orientation, and scale within the game world. To extend the capabilities and define the morphological and behavioral characteristics of these GameObjects, developers attach Components—modular elements including animations, sounds, 3D models, and effects. These Components facilitate the assembly and combination of different elements, thereby enabling the creation of complex and interactive game objects necessary for the development of the top-down action game designed for English learning in this thesis.

We propose an attention-based method that aggregates local image features to a subject-level representation for predicting disease severity, motivated by the limitations of classical deep learning approaches that require fixed dimensional input and lack interpretability. Our approach operates on sets of image patches, accommodating variable-length input images without resizing, and learns clinically interpretable representations reflective of disease severity. The model comprises three mutually dependent modules: a discriminative network that learns a fixed-length representation from local features and maps them to severity, an attention mechanism that highlights the most predictive anatomical areas, and a generative network that encourages diversity in local latent features to ensure non-degenerate attention weights while maintaining clinical relevance. Trained end-to-end on a large-scale lung CT study of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), our model achieves state-of-the-art performance in predicting clinical severity measures, with the attention distribution offering regional relevance of lung tissue to these measurements. These results indicate potential for broader application in medical imaging and motivate future research on interpretable, flexible deep learning frameworks. (176 words)

Model compression techniques for Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are essential for improving computational efficiency across diverse platforms, with DNN weight pruning recognized as a particularly effective approach. Traditional pruning strategies are divided between non-structured, fine-grained pruning, which achieves substantial sparsity and maintains high accuracy but lacks hardware compatibility, and structured, coarse-grained pruning, which is hardware efficient but often incurs accuracy degradation at high pruning rates. The introduction of PCONV addresses these limitations by integrating a new sparsity dimension that incorporates fine-grained pruning patterns within coarse-grained structures. PCONV employs two key forms of sparsity: Sparse Convolution Patterns (SCP) derived from intra-convolution kernel pruning, which enhance accuracy due to advantageous vision properties, and connectivity sparsity from inter-convolution kernel pruning, which enables higher pruning rates while balancing filter computation workloads. To facilitate practical deployment, a compiler-assisted DNN inference framework is developed to execute PCONV models in real-time, maintaining accuracy and achieving significant speedups compared to leading frameworks such as TensorFlow-Lite, TVM, and Alibaba Mobile Neural Network. Experimental results demonstrate that PCONV enables real-time inference on large-scale DNNs for mobile devices without accuracy loss, offering speedups of up to 39.2x.

The paragraph discusses the vulnerabilities present in smart contracts, specifically focusing on two key issues: the risk of insecure contract updating and the leaking of Ether to arbitrary addresses. It highlights how these vulnerabilities can lead to unauthorized access and transactions, and suggests that proper identity authentication can mitigate such risks. 

In the context of smart contract security, one significant concern is the potential for a developer to update a malicious contract, a vulnerability known as Insecure Contract Updating. This issue enables the alteration of transactions using the affected contract, posing a considerable risk to the integrity and security of blockchain transactions. Another critical vulnerability is the leaking of Ether to arbitrary addresses. This security flaw arises when the smart contract allows assets to be withdrawn by any party, irrespective of whether they are the rightful owner or an investor in the contract. The root cause of this vulnerability is the lack of verification of the identity of individuals requesting to execute the contract, which allows attackers to redirect Ether to any chosen address. This security lapse could be effectively mitigated by implementing robust identity authentication mechanisms within the contract’s deposit function.

Hue-Net introduces a novel deep learning framework for intensity-based image-to-image translation, emphasizing a new technique called network augmentation, which enables the differentiable construction of intensity histograms from images. The approach further develops differentiable representations of one-dimensional cyclic histograms and two-dimensional joint histograms, which are then utilized to define loss functions based on cyclic Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) and Mutual Information (MI). While the framework can be generalized to a variety of image-to-image translation tasks, its efficacy is demonstrated in color transfer scenarios, where the objective is to render a source image with the color distribution of a target image in the absence of a ground truth output. This is achieved by formulating an intensity-based loss using the EMD between cyclic hue histograms of the output and target images in the HSV color space. To ensure the preservation of semantic content between the source and output images, a semantic-based loss is introduced through a differentiable approximation of MI. The combination of histogram-based loss functions with adversarial training yields semantically coherent and visually realistic results, as evidenced by evaluations across multiple datasets.
