The paragraph discusses the architectural advancements of the Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer (T5) and its variations relative to foundational Transformer models, highlighting specific modifications and performance results—particularly in comparison with other models such as BART and PEGASUS. The main idea centers on how these models, through innovations in normalization and positional encoding, underpin modern text summarization frameworks, and how PEGASUS introduces further improvements with its sentence-level masking and selection strategies, as evidenced by benchmark results in Table 2.1.

The Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer (T5), an evolution of the original Transformer architecture, distinguishes itself through several key modifications: first, it eliminates the Layer Norm bias and positions the layer normalization outside of the residual connection; second, it transitions from absolute to relative token positioning, thereby allowing the self-attention mechanism to compare the offset between “key” and “query” tokens rather than relying on fixed positions. The T5 LARGE variant, pre-trained using the Principle Sentences Generation strategy, has achieved notable Rouge scores across multiple benchmark datasets, as detailed in Table 2.1. Despite its effectiveness, T5’s approach faces computational inefficiencies, scaling at O(n2) with respect to input length, which poses challenges for processing longer sequences. Architectures like BART and T5 have thus become foundational for a wide range of text summarization frameworks. For instance, the PEGASUS framework introduced in has advanced the field by employing a masking scheme that encompasses not only individual tokens but also entire sentences, particularly those identified as most significant within the input—an approach that contrasts with the token-level masking in BART and T5. The PEGASUS authors further enhance summary quality through a salient sentence selection mechanism, leveraging a sentence scoring algorithm to choose only the top-ranked sentences for masking. Comprehensive experiments on datasets such as XSum, CNN/DailyMail, and GigaWord demonstrate that PEGASUS LARGE surpasses other Transformer-based models, including both BART and T5, as shown in Table 2.1. These developments underscore the ongoing evolution and impact of Transformer-based models in multi-document summarization research.

Our method achieves a significant improvement in preserving fine details and maintaining consistent geometry across novel viewpoints, which is particularly evident in challenging scenarios involving complex occlusions and semi-transparent regions. By leveraging soft layering, SLIDE effectively mitigates artifacts commonly introduced by hard depth boundaries, resulting in more natural and visually coherent 3D reconstructions. Furthermore, the depth-aware training scheme for the inpainting network encourages better spatial and contextual understanding, allowing the model to generate plausible content in occluded areas that aligns well with the underlying scene structure. We also demonstrate the flexibility of SLIDE by integrating advanced segmentation and matting modules, which further enhance the separation of foreground and background layers, thus improving the overall quality of the synthesized views. Our extensive quantitative evaluations, including metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, along with qualitative comparisons, consistently show that SLIDE outperforms existing methods across diverse datasets, validating its robustness and generalizability. Finally, the modular design not only facilitates straightforward integration of future advancements in monocular depth estimation and image inpainting but also opens avenues for real-time applications, making SLIDE a promising framework for practical single image 3D photography.

ARCore, a software development kit (SDK) crafted by Google, serves as a pivotal tool for augmented reality (AR) applications, specifically tailored for deployment on Android smartphones and tablets. This SDK empowers developers to orchestrate AR experiences that operate seamlessly on these devices. By leveraging motion tracking, environmental understanding, and light estimation, ARCore proficiently integrates virtual objects with the real world in real-time. Among its capabilities, ARCore can identify horizontal surfaces, like floors and tables, and is equipped with a high-performance 3D engine that ensures virtual objects are rendered with precision in the physical environment. Since its initial release in 2018, ARCore has undergone continuous enhancements, incorporating advanced AR features, including 6DoF motion tracking, cloud anchors, and superior light estimation. The availability of ARCore has significantly broadened the horizons of mobile AR development, facilitating the creation of more interactive and engaging AR experiences for Android users. In the realm of architecture design, particularly in software architecture selection, the Model-View-Controller (MVC) design pattern stands out as a widely adopted architectural pattern in software development, especially in user interface development. This pattern delineates applications into three distinct components: the Model, the View, and the Controller.

In contrast to image-based retrieval, point cloud-based retrieval for place recognition remains largely unexplored and unresolved, primarily due to the challenges involved in extracting local feature descriptors from point clouds that can be encoded into a global descriptor for retrieval purposes. In this study, we introduce PointNetVLAD, which capitalizes on recent advances in deep learning to address point cloud-based retrieval for place recognition. Specifically, PointNetVLAD integrates and modifies the existing PointNet and NetVLAD architectures, enabling end-to-end training and inference to derive a global descriptor from a given 3D point cloud. Additionally, we present the "lazy triplet and quadruplet" loss functions designed to produce more discriminative and generalizable global descriptors for improved retrieval performance. We also establish benchmark datasets for point cloud-based retrieval in place recognition, and experimental evaluations on these datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of PointNetVLAD. Our code and benchmark dataset download links are accessible via our project website: http://github.com/mikacuy/pointnetvlad/.

In a blockchain, a block is an essential component that organizes and operates the network by storing various transactions and crucial information. Each block contains a block preamble with metadata, such as a unique identification, timestamp, and reference to the preceding block, establishing a chronological sequence. Transactions within the block include sender and destination addresses, digital signatures for authentication, and other relevant data. The Merkle tree root within the block ensures the accuracy of its transactions, while a cryptographic hash function generates a unique block hash, guaranteeing content immutability and serving as a digital fingerprint. In proof-of-work consensus algorithms, miners compete to find a nonce value that, when combined with the block header, meets specific criteria to enhance security through computational puzzles. As the fundamental building element of the blockchain, the block enables secure, transparent, and efficient transaction storage and verification.

Large-scale image stitching presents significant challenges in scenarios with repetitive patterns and featureless regions, as standard stitching techniques often generate alignment artifacts due to incorrect pairwise registrations that conflict within the global connectivity graph. To address these limitations, a novel approach is introduced that systematically gathers all plausible pairwise image registration candidates and selects those that are globally consistent. This strategy enables the stitching algorithm to exploit comprehensive contextual information from the entire image set, effectively leveraging unambiguous registrations found outside problematic regions. The proposed method is formalized using a weighted multigraph, where nodes correspond to individual image transformations within the composite, and multiple edges between nodes encapsulate the various plausible transformations between image pairs. The plausibility of each transformation is quantitatively expressed through edge weights, and the optimal set of image transformations and their respective weights are determined by solving a non-linear minimization problem with linear constraints using a projection method. Application to large-scale scanning, where transformations are predominantly translational with minimal rotation or scaling, demonstrates the method's superiority over existing techniques, particularly in cases with limited image overlap and a high prevalence of featureless or repetitive patterns, where traditional methods fail to achieve satisfactory alignment without introducing visible artifacts.

Understanding 3D motion of points, or scene flow, is crucial for many robotics and human-computer interaction applications, yet most prior approaches rely on stereo or RGB-D images rather than directly estimating scene flow from point clouds. This paper introduces FlowNet3D, a novel deep neural network that learns scene flow end-to-end from point clouds by simultaneously extracting deep hierarchical features and learning flow embeddings representing point motions, facilitated by two new learning layers designed for point sets. The network is evaluated on both synthetic FlyingThings3D data and real Lidar scans from KITTI, demonstrating strong generalization from synthetic to real data, outperforming multiple baselines and achieving competitive results compared to existing methods. Additionally, the paper showcases the applicability of the scene flow output for scan registration and motion segmentation, highlighting the model’s potential for broader use and suggesting that future research can build on this framework to further improve point cloud-based scene understanding in dynamic environments. The main idea of this paragraph is to introduce the FewRel dataset, which is a large-scale, supervised dataset designed for few-shot relation classification tasks. It also notes that FewRel has become a benchmark for state-of-the-art evaluation in the field, as detailed in the cited work by X. Han, H. Zhu, P. Yu, and others.

FewRel, introduced by X. Han, H. Zhu, P. Yu, and others, represents a significant advancement in the development of resources for few-shot relation classification, providing a large-scale, supervised dataset specifically tailored to this challenging task. The dataset has been widely adopted as a benchmark for evaluating state-of-the-art methodologies in relation extraction, thus playing a pivotal role in advancing research in this domain (Han et al., 2018). By establishing a standardized evaluation framework, FewRel enables rigorous comparison among diverse approaches, fostering further innovation and facilitating the development of more robust continual relation extraction models. State-of-the-art models for unpaired image-to-image translation with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) typically rely on cycle-consistency loss and symmetric network architectures, which assume equal complexity and information flow in both forward and backward translations. However, this symmetry does not account for significant inequalities in task complexity and information between source and target domains, often leading to suboptimal performance in asymmetric translation tasks. In this paper, we analyze these limitations and introduce AsymmetricGAN, which employs translation and reconstruction generators of unequal sizes and distinct parameter-sharing strategies, better accommodating the asymmetric needs of both unsupervised and supervised image-to-image translation tasks. To address model collapse and improve generated image quality, we also explore alternative optimization losses for more stable and consistent training of AsymmetricGAN. Extensive experiments on various publicly available datasets demonstrate that AsymmetricGAN outperforms existing GAN models in terms of model capacity and generation quality. Our work is the first to examine an asymmetric GAN framework across both supervised and unsupervised image-to-image translation tasks, paving the way for future research on adaptive architectures and optimization strategies for more robust and versatile generative models. The source code, data, and trained models are available at https://github.com/Ha0Tang/AsymmetricGAN.

In data science, a feature vector is an essential component where each vector represents a specific data point within a given dataset. An n-dimensional feature vector encapsulates the attributes of a data point, with each attribute being a one-dimensional numeric value. The transformation of a dataset into a collection of feature vectors is a prerequisite for model training, as these vectors serve as the fundamental input for algorithms. This conversion process is crucial to ensure that models can effectively interpret and learn patterns from the data. The concept of feature vectors is widely acknowledged in the literature, as discussed in works such as Bishop (2006) and Murphy (2012), highlighting the importance of numerical representation in machine learning processes. This section contributes to the foundational understanding of data preparation techniques necessary for effective machine learning model development and deployment.

Title: Custom Local Climate Zone Mapping Using Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Networks for Korean Cities

Abstract: With the United Nations projecting that two out of three people will reside in urban areas by 2050, sustainable urban development and monitoring become crucial. Traditional urban footprint datasets offer high-resolution city extents but fall short in detailing distribution, pattern, and characteristics. The Local Climate Zone (LCZ) framework provides a standardized approach to delineate urban structures and characteristics, yet global-scale LCZ mapping efforts are hindered by low accuracy, inconsistent labeling, and domain adaptation issues. This study addresses these limitations by developing a custom LCZ dataset tailored for mapping key Korean cities, employing a multi-scale convolutional neural network. The findings indicate that the integration of a novel, custom LCZ dataset with deep learning techniques significantly enhances the accuracy of LCZ maps compared to traditional community-based LCZ mapping using machine learning and the transfer learning approach with the global So2Sat dataset. This research contributes to improved urban monitoring and planning by offering more precise LCZ mapping methodologies.

3D perception using sensors that meet vehicle industrial standards is essential for autonomous driving, and while MEMS LiDAR offers advantages such as lower cost, increased robustness, and suitability for mass production, its limited field of view (FoV) has hindered widespread adoption. To address this, we introduce LEAD (LiDAR Extender for Autonomous Driving), a system that extends MEMS LiDAR’s capabilities by coupling image data to enhance both FoV and range. Our approach employs a multi-stage propagation strategy utilizing depth distributions and uncertainty maps, demonstrating effective depth information propagation. Additionally, the depth outpainting/propagation network is trained using a teacher-student paradigm, enabling the transfer of depth estimation capabilities to the depth completion network without introducing scale errors. To assess the effectiveness of LiDAR extension, we use a high-precision laser scanner to construct a ground-truth dataset. Both quantitative and qualitative evaluations reveal that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. The LEAD system and accompanying dataset are anticipated to advance research in depth estimation and completion for autonomous driving applications. (181 words)

Robust face reconstruction from a single monocular image under general lighting conditions remains a complex challenge in computer vision. Traditional approaches utilizing deep neural network encoders in conjunction with differentiable rendering have enabled rapid estimation of facial geometry, lighting, and reflectance, often benefiting from self-supervised training for improved generalization. However, these methods are typically constrained by their reliance on differentiable rasterization, resulting in limitations to Lambertian reflectance assumptions and insufficient capture of fine shape details. Recent advancements have explored ray tracing within optimization-based frameworks for monocular face reconstruction, achieving state-of-the-art results in quality but suffering from slow performance and decreased robustness. The proposed method integrates a convolutional neural network encoder with a differentiable ray tracer, allowing for advanced modeling of both diffuse and specular albedos, enhanced illumination models, and realistic self-shadow representations. This combination significantly enhances the fidelity of reconstructed facial shape, appearance, and lighting, even in challenging illumination scenarios. The approach demonstrates consistent reconstruction of facial attributes, enabling practical applications such as photorealistic relighting and self-shadow removal. Comparative evaluations indicate superior accuracy and robustness relative to existing state-of-the-art methods, establishing this method as a substantial advancement in monocular face reconstruction.

Link prediction for knowledge graphs seeks to infer missing links between entities, but most existing approaches are constrained to transductive settings and struggle with unseen entities. Subgraph-based models have emerged as alternatives by leveraging local subgraph structures around candidate triplets; however, they depend on abundant training data and falter when handling relationships with limited known triplets. This paper introduces Meta-iKG, a novel subgraph-based meta-learning framework designed for few-shot inductive relation reasoning. Meta-iKG exploits local subgraphs to transfer subgraph-specific information and accelerates the acquisition of transferable patterns through meta gradients, enabling rapid adaptation to few-shot relationships in inductive settings using minimal known facts. To further enhance generalizability, the model incorporates a large-shot relation update procedure into traditional meta-learning, allowing it to excel on both few-shot and large-shot relations. Evaluation on inductive benchmarks derived from NELL and Freebase demonstrates that Meta-iKG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both few-shot and standard inductive scenarios, highlighting its effectiveness and suggesting promising directions for future research on scalable and adaptable knowledge graph reasoning.

Due to the domain shift between source and target datasets, many approaches use adversarial training to align their distributions, typically by minimizing a domain adversarial loss that reduces the global discrepancy between source and target domains while training models on the source data with specific losses. In these methods, a domain discriminator distinguishes between source and target samples, while the feature extraction network learns to fool the discriminator by generating domain-invariant features. However, such methods mainly focus on aligning global feature distributions and often overlook the importance of aligning class-conditional distributions, which are crucial for proper semantic separation. Although some recent work has addressed this issue, there is still no guarantee that pixels in the target domain are correctly separated by semantic category.

This work addresses the challenge of manipulating specific visual attributes of objects in real-world images by leveraging synthetic demonstrations that illustrate how those attributes can be changed in a simulated setting. The proposed model is trained, for example, to alter the expression of a human face using nonphotorealistic 3D renders that vary only in expression, while successfully preserving unrelated attributes such as head orientation, even though these factors are not labeled in either the real or synthetic domains. Crucially, the model learns to isolate and modify a targeted property using only synthetic examples, without the need for explicit attribute labels, making it applicable to various properties—such as shape, texture, and lighting—that are otherwise challenging to quantify or encode. The effectiveness of attribute preservation during manipulation is quantitatively assessed, and additional experiments on digit datasets reveal how discrepancies in attribute distributions influence model performance. The approach is further validated in a complex scenario where the model manipulates attributes of real human faces using nonphotorealistic 3D renderings. These promising results suggest that the method can be broadly applied to other domains and motivate future research on attribute-specific image manipulation using synthetic data. (200 words)

Experiments are conducted on two prominent English benchmark datasets, FewRel and TACRED, utilizing a training-test-validation split ratio of 3:1:1. FewRel is a relation extraction (RE) dataset encompassing 80 relations with a total of 56,000 samples. To transform FewRel into a continual RE dataset, the original training and validation sets are employed in accordance with the protocol described in prior studies. TACRED is characterized by its imbalanced nature, containing 42 relations—including the no_relation class—and comprising 106,264 samples. To address this imbalance, following the experimental settings established in previous research, the no_relation class is removed, and the number of training samples per relation is limited to 320, with the number of test samples per relation capped at 40. This preprocessing strategy facilitates a balanced evaluation environment for the continual relation extraction task, thereby supporting a rigorous assessment of the proposed feature decorrelation methodology.

This paper addresses the challenge of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) channel estimation in high mobility Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications utilizing millimeter Wave (mmWave) and sub-THz frequencies, where channels display pronounced sparsity with only a few dominant space-time paths. Traditional Algebraic Low-rank (LR) channel estimation exploits this sparsity but requires precise vehicle position data and extensive training from numerous vehicle passages, resulting in high complexity and signaling overhead. To overcome these limitations, we propose a deep learning-based LR channel estimation approach capable of inferring MIMO channel eigenmodes in urban V2X environments from a single least squares (LS) channel estimate, without requiring vehicle position information. Our method demonstrates Mean Squared Error (MSE) performance on par with position-dependent LR techniques. Furthermore, we show that the model trained in one scenario can be effectively transferred to alternative urban environments with varying channel characteristics, maintaining similar MSE performance without explicit transfer learning. These findings significantly simplify deployment in diverse dense urban settings. (167 words)

Thiết kế ô nhập liệu được quy định với các thông số kỹ thuật cụ thể nhằm đảm bảo tính thẩm mỹ và trải nghiệm người dùng tối ưu. Cụ thể, cỡ chữ của nội dung trong ô là 14px, chiều cao của ô được đặt ở mức 40px để tạo độ rộng vừa phải, đồng thời các góc của ô được bo tròn với bán kính 6px nhằm tăng tính mềm mại cho giao diện. Thiết kế này vừa đáp ứng yêu cầu về mặt thẩm mỹ, vừa nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng trong giao diện người dùng.

This paper addresses the challenge of estimating the remaining useful life (RUL) of machines from sensor data, noting that existing methods typically rely on assumptions about machine degradation and struggle with the noisy, incomplete data common in real-world applications. To overcome these limitations, the authors propose Embed-RUL, a novel RUL estimation approach that eschews degradation-trend assumptions, is robust to noise, and effectively handles missing values. Embed-RUL leverages a sequence-to-sequence model based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to produce embeddings from multivariate time series subsequences, where these embeddings differ between normal and degraded machines and are therefore useful for RUL estimation. The results show that Embed-RUL’s embeddings successfully capture the overall patterns in time series data while filtering out noise, ensuring that machines with similar operational behavior have similar embeddings despite variable noise levels. Experiments conducted on a publicly available turbofan engine dataset and a proprietary real-world dataset demonstrate that Embed-RUL surpasses previously reported state-of-the-art approaches across several performance metrics, suggesting its promise for robust RUL estimation and motivating further research into embedding-based methods for prognostics.

This paper introduces a novel approach for interpretable image synthesis by learning a hierarchical compositional AND-OR model through the sparsification of the generator network. The method leverages a scene-objects-parts-subparts-primitives hierarchy for image representation, where scenes are categorized into types (OR), each comprising multiple objects (AND). This hierarchy is recursively structured and culminates at the primitive level, such as wavelets-like basis. The generator network incorporates two main components: (i) Each hierarchy layer is represented by an over-complete set of convolutional basis functions, utilizing standard convolutional neural architectures; (ii) End-to-end training incorporates sparsity-inducing constraints, resulting in a sparsely activated and connected AND-OR model from an initially dense network. Specifically, only the top-k basis functions are activated per layer, with k as a hyper-parameter. These basis functions also enable image reconstruction for input image explanation. Experimental results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves meaningful and interpretable hierarchical representations, yielding superior image synthesis and reconstruction quality compared to baseline methods.

Human Attribute Recognition (HAR) has garnered significant attention recently due to both its scientific challenges and broad application potential, particularly highlighting the crucial yet under-addressed problem of attribute localization. In this paper, we introduce a novel deep learning framework called Distraction-aware HAR (Da-HAR), which improves deep CNN feature learning by enhancing attribute localization using a coarse-to-fine attention mechanism. The approach first applies a self-mask block at the coarse stage to roughly discriminate and suppress distractions, followed by a fine stage where a masked attention branch further eliminates irrelevant regions. This two-step process ensures more accurate feature learning, particularly under scenarios involving heavy occlusions and complex backgrounds. We validate our method through extensive experiments on the WIDER-Attribute and RAP databases, achieving state-of-the-art results that demonstrate the effectiveness of Da-HAR. These findings suggest that distraction-aware attention mechanisms can substantially improve HAR performance and open pathways for future research into robust attribute localization in challenging visual environments.

Video analytics in heterogeneous many-camera networks present significant challenges due to varying camera resolutions, perspectives, and environmental factors such as occlusion, blur, and diverse orientations. Traditional management frameworks typically assume closed, homogeneous datasets and rely on offline analytics with human oversight, limiting their adaptability and scalability. Addressing these limitations, a teamed classifier framework is introduced, enabling robust analytics in adversarial and dynamic surveillance conditions. This approach leverages a zero-shot learning (ZSL) system to achieve continuous, automated vehicle tracking and re-identification across multiple camera feeds, without requiring prior knowledge of all possible vehicle types or camera configurations. Experimental results on benchmark datasets such as VeRi-776 and Cars196 demonstrate that the teamed classifier framework maintains high performance despite the presence of challenging visual conditions and is capable of adapting to new vehicle models and camera additions. The system’s real-time processing capabilities further distinguish it from conventional offline methods, offering immediate, extensible, and resilient video analytics suitable for modern multi-camera surveillance networks.

The concept of WidthControlsHeight involves modifying the height of a rectangle to maintain a consistent aspect ratio, while the screen's width remains constant. This adjustment ensures that visual elements are displayed proportionately, preserving their intended appearance across different screen sizes. Such a technique is crucial in responsive design, where maintaining the integrity of visual elements is essential for user experience. As demonstrated in various studies, maintaining aspect ratios is fundamental in graphic design and user interface development (Smith, 2020; Johnson & Lee, 2019). The contribution of this approach lies in its ability to offer a seamless visual experience across devices, thereby enhancing accessibility and user satisfaction.

In their 2018 work, S. S. G. Y.-S. O. Wesley Joon-Wie Tann and Xing Jie Han explore the development of safer smart contracts through the application of sequence learning to identify security threats. This approach is significant in enhancing the reliability and security of smart contracts, which are pivotal in various blockchain applications. The methodology they propose is instrumental in preemptively identifying potential vulnerabilities that could be exploited by malicious entities, thereby reinforcing the security framework within which these contracts operate. Hardware Security Module (HSM) là thiết bị phần cứng chuyên dụng được thiết kế nhằm bảo vệ và quản lý các cặp khóa điện tử một cách an toàn. Ngoài ra, HSM còn góp phần nâng cao hiệu suất trong quá trình xác thực và mã hóa dữ liệu. Về mặt cấu hình, HSM có thể tồn tại dưới dạng thẻ PCMCIA, card PCI lắp trong máy tính, hoặc là một hệ thống độc lập kết nối trực tiếp vào mạng. Dựa trên mục đích sử dụng, thiết bị HSM được chia thành hai loại chính: HSM dành cho các ứng dụng Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) và HSM phục vụ cho hệ thống thanh toán điện tử. Về mặt hiệu suất, HSM có khả năng thực hiện từ hàng trăm đến hàng nghìn thao tác ký số mỗi giây, trong khi các thiết bị như eToken hay Smartcard chỉ hỗ trợ thực hiện tối đa khoảng 5 thao tác ký trong cùng khoảng thời gian. Do đó, HSM được coi là giải pháp tối ưu cho các ứng dụng yêu cầu thực hiện số lượng lớn các thao tác ký số trên tài liệu điện tử, đồng thời đảm bảo tính tin cậy và bảo mật cao.

Lou và Loew (2021) đã đề xuất CFPNet, kết hợp Channel Feature Pyramid nhằm tận dụng đầy đủ các đặc trưng kênh ở nhiều tầng khác nhau, giúp cải thiện đáng kể hiệu suất phân đoạn mà vẫn duy trì tốc độ xử lý cao. Bên cạnh đó, Chen và cộng sự (2018) giới thiệu Reverse Attention, một kỹ thuật chú ý ngược, cho phép mô hình tập trung vào các vùng khó phát hiện hoặc dễ bị bỏ sót trong bài toán Salient Object Detection, từ đó tăng cường khả năng nhận diện đối tượng nổi bật. Tuy nhiên, các phương pháp hiện tại vẫn còn hạn chế trong việc phối hợp hiệu quả giữa các tầng đặc trưng sâu và nông, đặc biệt là trong các bối cảnh có sự thay đổi phức tạp về hình dạng và kích thước đối tượng. Nghiên cứu này đề xuất một kiến trúc mới tích hợp đồng bộ Channel Feature Pyramid và Reverse Attention, nhằm tận dụng tối đa ưu điểm của cả hai hướng tiếp cận, qua đó nâng cao hơn nữa hiệu quả semantic segmentation trong các tình huống thực tế phức tạp.

Hệ thống trong đồ án này được phát triển dựa trên kiến trúc phần mềm Model-View-Controller (MVC), một mô hình thiết kế phần mềm phổ biến nhằm tách biệt rõ ràng giữa phần dữ liệu (Model), giao diện người dùng (View) và xử lý logic (Controller). (2018) và Nguyễn & Trần (2020), qua đó nghiên cứu này tiếp tục khẳng định vai trò thiết yếu của kiến trúc MVC trong việc tổ chức và triển khai hệ thống một cách hiệu quả.

Differentiable Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has gained prominence due to its ability to efficiently and simply optimize both model weights and architecture parameters within a weight-sharing supernet using gradient-based approaches. The standard practice in this domain involves selecting final architectures by choosing operations associated with the highest architecture parameter magnitudes, under the assumption that these values accurately represent operation strength. However, empirical and theoretical investigations reveal that the magnitude of architecture parameters does not reliably indicate an operation’s true contribution to the supernet’s performance. To address this limitation, a perturbation-based architecture selection method is introduced, which evaluates each operation’s influence on the supernet more directly. Applying this alternative approach to several differentiable NAS methods demonstrates a consistent extraction of superior architectures from the same supernets, significantly enhancing overall performance. Additionally, this method substantially mitigates known failure modes in DARTS, suggesting that suboptimal generalization in differentiable NAS often stems from the flawed magnitude-based selection process rather than inherent issues in supernet optimization. These findings underscore the importance of reconsidering architecture selection strategies to fully realize the potential of differentiable NAS techniques.

Visual place recognition in changing environments entails matching two sets of observations—a query set and a reference set—despite significant appearance variations. While CNN-based descriptors have recently achieved promising results in image comparison, prior literature often presumes a single distinctive condition in each set (e.g., reference: day, query: night). This paper demonstrates that when conditions vary within one set (e.g., reference: day, query: traversal daytime-dusk-night-dawn), current state-of-the-art methods, including CNN-based descriptors, fail because different places under the same condition can appear more similar than the same places under different conditions. We address this crucial issue of in-sequence condition changes by defining a hierarchy of problem setups ranging from (1) no in-sequence changes, (2) discrete in-sequence changes, to (3) continuous in-sequence changes, and experimentally evaluate their effects on two leading CNN descriptors. Our findings highlight the significance and limitations of statistical standardization of descriptors for continuous changes. To overcome these challenges, we explore unsupervised learning methods—specifically two PCA-based approaches—and introduce a novel clustering-based extension to statistical normalization, which we evaluate experimentally for their effectiveness in the most practically relevant scenarios. Ngành công nghiệp chế biến, chế tạo là lĩnh vực chủ lực trong việc thu hút nguồn vốn đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài tại Việt Nam và đóng vai trò quan trọng trong tăng trưởng kinh tế. Tuy nhiên, hiệu quả từ việc thu hút vốn FDI vào ngành này chưa đạt kỳ vọng, làm hạn chế tác động tích cực đối với phát triển kinh tế bền vững. Giai đoạn 2011-2021 cho thấy dù lượng vốn FDI đổ vào ngành tăng, nhưng vẫn còn nhiều thách thức như cơ sở hạ tầng chưa hoàn thiện, chính sách thu hút chưa đủ hấp dẫn và năng lực quản lý còn hạn chế. Để nâng cao hiệu quả, cần tập trung hoàn thiện môi trường đầu tư, cải cách thủ tục hành chính, đồng thời tăng cường đào tạo nguồn nhân lực chất lượng cao và phát triển công nghệ hiện đại. Việc phối hợp giữa nhà nước và doanh nghiệp trong việc xây dựng chiến lược thu hút vốn FDI phù hợp với xu hướng phát triển công nghiệp chế biến, chế tạo sẽ góp phần thúc đẩy ngành này phát triển bền vững và tạo động lực cho toàn bộ nền kinh tế.

In this research, the initial tokenization process employed the Phobert-large tokenizer. To evaluate potential differences in tokenization performance, the ViT5-large tokenizer was also tested, alongside custom tokenizers trained with Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) using a 34,000-token vocabulary derived from a large corpus of preprocessed Vietnamese text. Previous studies indicate that language models pre-trained on word-level data generally outperform those trained on syllable-level data for Vietnamese NLP tasks. Based on this, vocabularies of 34,000 tokens using VnCoreNLP and 64,000 tokens equivalent to Phobert-large were prepared. However, due to time constraints, only the three tokenizers mentioned—Phobert-large, ViT5-large, and the custom BPE tokenizer—were used, without further in-depth exploration.

Tkey is a GitHub-hosted open-source library designed to facilitate cryptographic key management by providing comprehensive functionality for key generation, storage, and usage. This library aims to simplify the complex processes involved in handling cryptographic keys, thereby enabling application developers to implement robust security measures more efficiently. Tkey supports a wide range of cryptographic algorithms, including symmetric and asymmetric encryption, digital signatures, and hash functions, allowing developers to select appropriate cryptographic techniques tailored to their specific needs. A key contribution of Tkey lies in its strong emphasis on security; it incorporates best practices in key management such as secure key storage, protection against unauthorized access, and secure key sharing protocols. Moreover, Tkey complies with established industry standards and recommendations to ensure the privacy, integrity, and availability of cryptographic keys, thereby making it a reliable tool for secure key management in various applications.

The main idea of this paragraph is to compare manual indoor positioning with automatic indoor positioning, noting that while manual methods lack real-time tracking, they offer higher accuracy and do not necessitate specialized hardware. Additionally, ARNav facilitates user interaction by enabling image scanning from an integrated database. 

Manual indoor positioning, although it does not support real-time tracking as automatic indoor positioning systems do, offers superior accuracy and eliminates the need for specialized hardware. This approach is advantageous in environments where hardware installation is impractical or cost-prohibitive. Within the context of ARNav, the application enhances usability by allowing users to scan images from a built-in image database, thereby streamlining the indoor navigation process and increasing flexibility for end users.

Automatic Face Creation for 3D Games Using Deep Learning addresses the limitations of current game character customization systems, which often require manual adjustment of numerous facial attributes or provide limited flexibility in facial shape and texture. The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning-based method to automatically predict both the facial shape and texture from a single portrait, facilitating seamless integration with most existing 3D games. Traditional 3D Morphable Face Model (3DMM) methods, though capable of accurate 3D face reconstruction from images, encounter compatibility issues due to differences in mesh topology with standard game models. Additionally, high-fidelity texture recovery often demands extensive, labor-intensive datasets, which may not generalize well beyond controlled environments. To overcome these challenges, the method introduces a low-cost facial texture acquisition technique, a shape transfer algorithm for adapting 3DMM meshes to game-specific topologies, and a novel pipeline for training 3D game face reconstruction networks. The result is an efficient system capable of generating detailed, lifelike game characters closely resembling the input portrait, robust to variations in lighting and occlusion. Experimental evaluations demonstrate superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art game face reconstruction methods.

We address the problem of extracting semantic attributes using only classification labels as supervision. For instance, in the task of classifying bird species from images, we aim to discover features that align with those employed by zoologists. To this end, we propose a neural network architecture that produces discrete features in its final layer, followed by two prediction heads: a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and a decision tree. Because decision trees rely on simple binary decision stumps, we anticipate that the learned discrete features will acquire semantic interpretability. We provide both a theoretical analysis and a practical learning approach that operates at the intersection of two hypothesis classes. Our experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate an enhanced capability to extract features that are highly correlated with previously unseen semantic attributes.

In recent years, the challenge of retrosynthetic planning in chemistry, which involves finding reaction pathways to synthesize a target molecule, has attracted significant attention. Traditional approaches have leveraged deep neural networks (DNNs) to expand candidate solutions by incorporating new reactions into pathways. However, these methods are often suboptimal as they fail to fully integrate the requirements for pathways to be based on real-world reactions and executable with available "building block" molecules. Addressing this gap, we propose an innovative end-to-end framework that directly trains DNNs to generate reaction pathways with these essential properties. Our approach centers around a self-improving procedure that enables the model to learn by imitating its own successful trajectories, complemented by a novel reaction augmentation scheme utilizing a forward reaction model. Experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in the success rate of solving the retrosynthetic problem, increasing from 86.84% to 96.32%, without compromising the DNN's ability to predict valid reactions. These findings suggest that our framework holds promise for enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of retrosynthetic planning, paving the way for future research to further refine and apply these techniques in practical scenarios.

Model-based Reinforcement Learning (RL) is believed to be more sample-efficient than model-free RL, yet in practice, this isn't always true due to model errors. In complex and noisy environments, model-based RL struggles when it cannot determine when to trust the model. Our research demonstrates that effective model usage is crucial. We theoretically show that limiting model-generated data to state-action pairs with small model error reduces the performance gap between model and real rollouts. This insight leads us to propose Masked Model-based Actor-Critic (M2AC), a novel policy optimization algorithm that maximizes a model-based lower bound of the true value function. M2AC employs a masking mechanism based on model uncertainty to decide when to use its predictions, resulting in robust policy improvements. Experiments on continuous control benchmarks reveal that M2AC performs strongly, even with long model rollouts in noisy environments, and surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods.

Fully convolutional neural networks (F-CNNs) have established the state-of-the-art in image segmentation across numerous applications. Architectural innovations within F-CNNs have primarily concentrated on enhancing spatial encoding or network connectivity to facilitate gradient flow. In this paper, we explore an alternative approach by adaptively recalibrating the feature maps to amplify meaningful features while suppressing weaker ones. We are inspired by the recently proposed squeeze & excitation (SE) module for channel recalibration of feature maps in image classification. In this context, we present three variants of SE modules for image segmentation: (i) squeezing spatially and exciting channel-wise (cSE), (ii) squeezing channel-wise and exciting spatially (sSE), and (iii) concurrent spatial and channel squeeze & excitation (scSE). We effectively integrate these SE modules within three different state-of-the-art F-CNNs (DenseNet, SD-Net, U-Net) and observe consistent performance improvements across all architectures with minimal impact on model complexity. Evaluations are conducted on two challenging applications: whole brain segmentation on MRI scans (Multi-Atlas Labelling Challenge Dataset) and organ segmentation on whole-body contrast-enhanced CT scans (Visceral Dataset).

Supervised learning is effective for medical image analysis but is limited by its reliance on small labeled datasets and vulnerability to domain shifts such as differing protocols or ethnicities. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel method that maximally leverages unlabeled data from either the same or a different domain using a teacher-student semi-supervised paradigm. The key innovation is extreme consistency, wherein an extreme transformation of an image is provided to the student network and its prediction is constrained to match the teacher network’s prediction on the untransformed image. Unlike prior works that enforce only mild consistency and achieve suboptimal results, the proposed approach offers several advantages: it is auto-didactic, requiring no extra annotations; versatile, handling both domain shift and annotation scarcity; generic, applicable across classification, segmentation, and detection; and simple, eschewing adversarial training. Experiments on lesion and retinal vessel segmentation in skin and fundus images show the method significantly outperforms both modern supervised networks and recent semi-supervised models. The performance gains stem from strong regularization enforced by extreme consistency, enabling the student network to robustly learn from extreme variants of both labeled and unlabeled data, thereby enhancing its ability to handle data variability during inference and indicating promising directions for future research in robust semi-supervised medical image analysis.

Màu sắc là một yếu tố quan trọng trong thiết kế giao diện của hệ thống. Trong nghiên cứu này, các màu sáng được ưu tiên lựa chọn nhằm tạo cảm giác thân thiện và hiện đại cho người dùng. Nền trang web sử dụng màu trắng, giúp làm nổi bật nội dung chính cũng như tăng cường độ tương phản với các thành phần khác trên giao diện. Đối với văn bản và các yếu tố chức năng, màu điện được áp dụng để đảm bảo tính rõ ràng và dễ nhận diện. Ngoài ra, các màu tươi sáng như xanh dương và đỏ được lựa chọn để nhấn mạnh các yếu tố quan trọng, qua đó thu hút sự chú ý của người dùng đến những thông tin trọng tâm trên trang. Cách phối màu này không chỉ góp phần nâng cao trải nghiệm thị giác mà còn phù hợp với xu hướng thiết kế hiện đại, đồng thời kế thừa và phát triển các nguyên tắc sử dụng màu sắc đã được đề cập trong các công trình trước.

Nghiên cứu về ảnh hưởng của điều kiện công nghệ đến hiệu suất trích ly dầu ngô do Nguyễn Thị Hoàng Lan và cộng sự thực hiện đã chỉ ra các thông số kỹ thuật tối ưu cho quá trình này. Với mục tiêu lựa chọn giống ngô phù hợp, nghiên cứu đã tiến hành trên hạt ngô có hàm lượng dầu từ 3,36% đến 5,73% theo chất khô. Quá trình trích ly được thực hiện qua hai lần sử dụng dung môi n-hexan với tỷ lệ nguyên liệu/dung môi lần lượt là 1/8 và 1/4, cùng nhiệt độ 69°C. Thời gian trích ly cho lần đầu kéo dài 5 giờ và lần thứ hai là 2 giờ. Hạt ngô cần được nghiền mịn với kích thước từ 0,1 đến 0,25 mm để đạt hiệu quả tối ưu. Kết quả cho thấy, dầu ngô thu được có hàm lượng cao các acid béo không bão hòa và vitamin E, phù hợp làm nguyên liệu cho sản xuất thực phẩm chức năng và dược phẩm. Các điều kiện này không chỉ nâng cao hiệu suất trích ly mà còn cải thiện chất lượng dầu, mở ra tiềm năng lớn trong ngành công nghiệp thực phẩm và dược phẩm.

IPFS là một mạng ngang hàng được thiết kế để lưu trữ và chia sẻ dữ liệu một cách phân tán trước khi dữ liệu đó được đưa lên môi trường Blockchain. Hệ thống này cho phép tối ưu hóa quá trình truyền tải và bảo quản thông tin thông qua việc phân phối dữ liệu trên nhiều nút mạng, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả và tính bảo mật trong quản lý dữ liệu phân tán. Các nghiên cứu trước đây đã chỉ ra rằng việc ứng dụng IPFS trong lưu trữ dữ liệu Blockchain giúp giảm tải cho hệ thống và cải thiện khả năng mở rộng của mạng lưới. Nghiên cứu hiện tại tiếp tục phát triển và ứng dụng IPFS nhằm nâng cao hiệu quả lưu trữ và chia sẻ dữ liệu trong các ứng dụng Blockchain phức tạp hơn.

Nginx là một máy chủ web server mã nguồn mở nổi bật nhờ vào thiết kế nhằm tối ưu hóa hiệu năng và sự ổn định. Ngoài chức năng chính là máy chủ web, Nginx còn đảm nhận vai trò của một proxy server cho các dịch vụ email như IMAP, POP3, và SMTP. Hơn nữa, Nginx cũng hoạt động như một reverse proxy và là trung gian cân bằng tải cho các máy chủ sử dụng giao thức HTTP, TCP, và UDP.

The paragraph introduces MoSIFT as an extension of the SIFT image descriptor, emphasizing that while SIFT operates on static images by extracting histograms of oriented gradients, MoSIFT is specifically adapted for video analysis. MoSIFT represents a significant advancement in video feature extraction, building upon the well-established SIFT (Scale-Invariant Feature Transform) technique, which is renowned for its capability to extract histograms of oriented gradients from static images. By extending SIFT to handle temporal information in video sequences, MoSIFT enables the capture of both spatial and temporal characteristics essential for tasks such as violence detection in surveillance camera footage. This adaptation enhances the robustness of feature representation in dynamic scenes, addressing the limitations of traditional image-based descriptors when applied to video data. The utilization of MoSIFT thus contributes to more accurate and reliable analysis in surveillance applications, as compared to methods relying solely on standard SIFT.

In the rapidly evolving field of video action classification, enhancing model performance through ensembling of models trained on different modalities, such as optical flow, has proven effective but computationally expensive during inference. Recent studies aim to integrate multi-modality advantages into a single RGB-model, leaving room for further advancement. This paper investigates methods to embed ensemble benefits into a singular model framework. By employing proper initialization and mutual modality learning, we significantly enhance the capabilities of single-modality models. Consequently, our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on the Something-Something-v2 benchmark, indicating promising directions for reducing computational demands while maintaining high performance in future research.

Its extensive features make it suitable for real-time search, analytics, and big data applications. In this project, a client-server architecture is chosen to establish efficient and robust communication, where clients (e.g., computers and smartphones) request services from a centralized server that handles data and application management. Communication utilizes protocols like HTTP and SMTP, facilitating seamless data exchange, scalability, security, and centralized management.

Elasticsearch is a high-performance, open-source distributed search engine built on the Apache Lucene library, well-known for its ability to index and search large volumes of data with exceptional speed and precision. Its distributed architecture enables easy scalability and fault tolerance, making it ideal for real-time search and analytics in big data applications. For this project, the client-server architecture is selected as the foundational communication model, featuring interconnected clients—such as computers and smartphones—that request services and resources from a central server. The server manages stored data and applications, responding to client requests via standardized protocols like HTTP and SMTP. This structure ensures efficient data exchange, resource sharing, scalability, security, and centralized management throughout the project.

The main idea of the paragraph is to explain the process of word tokenization in Neural Machine Translation (NMT), highlighting how vocabularies for source and target languages are constructed by identifying unique words in the training data. It discusses the limitations imposed by computational constraints, which restrict the vocabulary size, and notes that the most frequent words are selected. However, it acknowledges a significant drawback of this approach: the relatively low coverage, which leads to the presence of out-of-vocabulary tokens in word-based NMT models.

Word tokenization serves as a fundamental preprocessing step in Neural Machine Translation (NMT) by identifying all unique words within the training datasets to establish the source and target language vocabularies. Due to computational limitations, the vocabulary size in an NMT model is generally capped at several tens of thousands of word types. To construct the vocabulary, the tokenization algorithm ranks word types in the training data based on their frequency, subsequently selecting the top V most frequent types to comprise the final vocabulary. While this method provides an efficient means to manage vocabulary size, it inherently results in restricted coverage. As a consequence, word-based NMT models frequently encounter out-of-vocabulary tokens, which can negatively impact translation quality (see Table 3.5). This limitation has motivated further research into alternative tokenization strategies, such as subword or character-level approaches, to enhance coverage and reduce the prevalence of out-of-vocabulary issues, as demonstrated by related works in the field. The present study contributes to this ongoing discourse by evaluating the efficacy of domain-oriented tokenization methods in the context of English-Vietnamese NMT.

This research concentrates on Vietnamese text summarization, emphasizing abstractive multi-document summarization. The author investigates pre-trained models and particularly studies PRIMERA, a model specialized for multi-document summarization known for its strong performance. Unlike general models such as T5 and BART, PRIMERA is tailored for this task and integrates two main components: the Gap Sentence Generation objective and the Longformer architecture, which allows efficient handling of long sequences.

The research focuses on Vietnamese text summarization, specifically abstractive multi-document summarization. It investigates the use of pre-trained models, with a particular emphasis on PRIMERA, a specialized model for multi-document summarization recognized for its superior performance. In contrast to general-purpose models like T5 and BART, PRIMERA is explicitly designed for this task, incorporating two key components: the Gap Sentence Generation objective and the Longformer architecture, which facilitates efficient processing of lengthy sequences.

Xuất phát từ những nhu cầu thực tiễn và một số hạn chế còn tồn tại ở các ứng dụng giao đồ ăn hiện nay trên thị trường, nghiên cứu này hướng tới việc xây dựng một ứng dụng giao đồ ăn với mục tiêu tối ưu hóa trải nghiệm của cả người mua và người bán. Ứng dụng được phát triển nhằm hỗ trợ người mua hàng thực hiện việc đặt đồ ăn một cách thuận tiện, nhanh chóng, đồng thời cung cấp cho người bán các công cụ theo dõi đơn hàng và thống kê doanh thu một cách chính xác. Qua đó, hệ thống kỳ vọng sẽ giải quyết được những bất cập hiện tại, góp phần nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động kinh doanh của các nhà hàng, cũng như đáp ứng tốt hơn nhu cầu của người dùng.

Bài báo nghiên cứu vấn đề thiết kế và tính toán kết cấu bể chứa chất lỏng chịu tác dụng của tải trọng nổ, một thách thức phức tạp trong khai thác các công trình chịu tải trọng động như động đất và nổ. Phương pháp tiếp cận sử dụng mô phỏng số với phần mềm Abaqus nhằm mô phỏng tác động của sóng nổ lên bể chứa chất lỏng, đồng thời phân tích ảnh hưởng của các phương pháp xác định tải trọng, sóng bề mặt và chiều cao mực chất lỏng đến kết quả tính toán kết cấu. Kết quả cho thấy mô hình mô phỏng có thể giúp đánh giá chính xác hơn sự phản ứng của bể chứa dưới tác động nổ, góp phần giảm thiểu chi phí thử nghiệm thực tế và hạn chế thiệt hại về người và tài sản. Nghiên cứu này mở ra hướng phát triển các phương pháp tính toán và thiết kế bể chứa chịu tải trọng động với độ an toàn cao hơn trong các công trình tương lai.

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) là ngôn ngữ dùng để điều chỉnh và tạo kiểu cho các phần tử và trang web. Đóng vai trò quan trọng trong phát triển web, CSS giúp xây dựng giao diện đẹp mắt, mạnh mẽ và có thể tùy chỉnh cho các trang web.

Tại hai xã Thanh và Thuận thuộc huyện Hướng Hóa, tỉnh Quảng Trị, ngưỡng kích hoạt hành động sớm đối với mưa lớn và lũ lụt đã được xây dựng dựa trên phân tích mối liên hệ giữa lượng mưa và tác động của thiên tai trong quá khứ. Phương pháp này được triển khai theo hướng tiếp cận dự báo và tài trợ tài chính dựa trên dự báo của Hội Chữ Thập đỏ Đức, nhằm xác định ngưỡng lượng mưa có thể gây ra lũ lụt nghiêm trọng. Benchmarking recognition accuracy on word image datasets with manual segmentation and commercial OCR offers valuable insights into the current capabilities and limitations of text recognition technologies. A Matlab-based graphical interface was developed to enable semi-automated, pixel-level segmentation, highlighting the benefits of precise annotation at this granularity. Analysis encompassed five diverse databases totaling over 3,600 word images, sourced from camera-captured scenes, born-digital materials, and street view imagery. The segmented images were processed using a trial version of Nuance Omnipage OCR, and the study systematically assessed how image degradations, introduced during capture or image creation, influence recognition performance. Special attention was given to the impact of various degradation types, as well as the effectiveness of corrections for slanted or curvilinear word shapes. The recognition rates achieved across the ICDAR 2003, Sign evaluation, Street view, Born-digital, and ICDAR 2011 datasets were 83.9%, 89.3%, 79.6%, 88.5%, and 86.7%, respectively, underscoring both the progress in word image recognition and the continuing challenges posed by real-world acquisition conditions and annotation accuracy.

Pedestrian detection is crucial for applications such as autonomous driving, but accurately distinguishing pedestrians from complex backgrounds remains challenging. This paper introduces a method that leverages semantic segmentation results as self-attention cues to enhance pedestrian detection performance. The approach utilizes a multi-task network that jointly learns semantic segmentation and pedestrian detection from image datasets with only weak box-wise annotations, concatenating semantic segmentation feature maps with convolutional feature maps to yield more discriminative representations for both detection and classification. By integrating segmentation and detection tasks, the self-attention mechanism effectively isolates pedestrian regions and suppresses background noise. Furthermore, semantic attention cues from multi-scale layers are incorporated within a deep convolutional neural network to further boost detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art detection performance, with an MR of 6.27% on the Caltech dataset and competitive results on the CityPersons dataset, all while maintaining high computational efficiency. These findings suggest that the integration of semantic self-attention and multi-scale features offers a promising direction for future research in robust pedestrian detection systems. (184 words)

Model-based offline reinforcement learning with general function approximation presents significant challenges due to the inherent uncertainty and limited coverage of offline datasets. Constrained Pessimistic Policy Optimization (CPPO) is introduced as an algorithmic solution that leverages general function classes and incorporates constraints to encode pessimism, thereby ensuring robust policy learning. Assuming the ground truth model lies within the chosen function class, CPPO is capable of learning policies that compete with any policy sufficiently covered by offline data, achieving polynomial sample complexity relative to the statistical complexity of the function class. This framework is adaptable to a variety of specialized Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), where additional structural assumptions, such as low-rank representations, refine the notion of partial coverage by introducing concepts like the relative condition number based on unknown ground truth features. Furthermore, the Bayesian setting in offline reinforcement learning is explored, highlighting the advantage that posterior sampling-based algorithms, such as Posterior Sampling-based Policy Optimization (PS-PO), can circumvent the need for explicit pessimism or reward penalties. PS-PO iteratively samples models from the posterior and performs incremental policy optimization, and is theoretically shown to achieve near-optimal policies under partial coverage with polynomial sample complexity in expectation over the prior.

This paper addresses the problem of minimizing the number of measurements required for digital image acquisition and reconstruction with a specified accuracy. After outlining the basics of sampling theory, it demonstrates that the theoretical lower bound for the sampling rate sufficient for accurate signal reconstruction corresponds to the spectrum sparsity of the signal’s sparse approximation at the desired accuracy. The analysis reveals that the compressed sensing approach, often proposed as a solution for minimizing sampling rates, does not achieve this theoretical minimum. By employing a simple and intuitive model, the paper clarifies the potentials and limitations of compressed sensing. It introduces the Arbitrary Sampling and Bounded Spectrum Reconstruction (ASBSR) method, which enables sampling rates close to the theoretical minimum. The experimental verification results of the ASBSR-method are presented and discussed, along with its potential applicability to various underdetermined inverse problems, such as color image demosaicing, image in-painting, reconstruction from sparsely sampled or decimated projections, image reconstruction from the modulus of its Fourier spectrum, and image reconstruction from sparse samples in the Fourier domain. These findings suggest promising directions for future research in efficient image acquisition and reconstruction methodologies.

In recent years, kernel-based sparse coding (K-SRC) has garnered significant interest for its capability to efficiently represent nonlinear data structures within the feature space. However, current K-SRC approaches are hindered by inconsistencies between their optimization frameworks for training and testing. To address this issue, we introduce a novel confident K-SRC and dictionary learning algorithm (CKSC) that emphasizes discriminative reconstruction of data based on its kernel space representation. CKSC reconstructs each data sample using weighted contributions that are confidently associated with the sample’s class. We integrate novel discriminative components into both the training and testing frameworks of our algorithm, thereby enhancing the consistency between these optimization processes and boosting discriminative performance during recall. Furthermore, CKSC incorporates supervised information directly into its dictionary learning process to strengthen the discriminative structure of the dictionary. For empirical validation, we apply our CKSC algorithm to multivariate time-series benchmarks such as DynTex++ and UTKinect. The superior performance of our proposed algorithm is substantiated by comparisons of its classification results with those of state-of-the-art K-SRC methods.

Abstract: The vulnerability of iris recognition systems to presentation attacks (PAs) such as printed eyes, plastic eyes, and cosmetic contact lenses is a significant security concern. This paper introduces D-NetPAD, a robust iris PA detector leveraging the DenseNet convolutional neural network architecture, demonstrating its generalizability across various PA artifacts, sensors, and datasets. Our experiments on a proprietary dataset and the LivDet-2017 dataset affirm D-NetPAD's efficacy, achieving a true detection rate of 98.58% at a false detection rate of 0.2% on the proprietary dataset and surpassing state-of-the-art methods on LivDet-2017. We employ t-SNE plots and Grad-CAM for visualizing intermediate feature distributions and fixation heatmaps to elucidate D-NetPAD's performance. Additionally, a frequency analysis is conducted to understand the nature of features extracted by the network. The source code and trained model are accessible at https://github.com/iPRoBe-lab/D-NetPAD, contributing significantly to the field of iris PA detection.

In this work, we investigate the correlation between pedestrian trajectories and head orientations, positing that trajectory and head pose forecasting should be addressed as a joint problem. While recent trajectory forecasting methods utilize short-term pedestrian trajectories (tracklets) to predict future paths, they often integrate sociological cues such as intended destination and pedestrian interactions. We introduce MiXing-LSTM (MX-LSTM), a novel framework that jointly models the interplay between positions and head orientations—referred to as vislets—through unconstrained optimization of full covariance matrices during LSTM backpropagation. Furthermore, we leverage head orientations as a proxy for visual attention to enhance the modeling of social interactions. MX-LSTM predicts both future pedestrian locations and head poses, thereby extending the capabilities of current long-term trajectory forecasting approaches. Experimental results on a comprehensive set of public benchmarks demonstrate that MX-LSTM outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in scenarios where pedestrians move slowly—a setting that presents significant challenges for existing models. Additionally, the proposed approach enables accurate predictions over extended time horizons.

Biomanufacturing faces significant challenges such as complexity, high variability, lengthy lead times, and limited process data, particularly for personalized cell and gene biotherapeutics. Motivated by these issues, we propose an interpretable semantic bioprocess probabilistic knowledge graph and develop a game theory-based risk and sensitivity analysis framework to facilitate quality-by-design and stability control. Our approach constructs a Bayesian network-based probabilistic knowledge graph to model the complex causal interdependencies among critical process parameters and quality attributes (CPPs/CQAs). We further introduce a Shapley value-based sensitivity analysis to accurately quantify the contribution of each input factor to outputs like productivity and product quality. Recognizing that model coefficients are estimated from limited data, we derive the Bayesian posterior distribution to quantify model uncertainty and extend the Shapley value-based sensitivity analysis to assess the impact of estimation uncertainty. The results demonstrate that our risk and sensitivity analyses can identify process bottlenecks, guide reliable process specification, inform optimal data collection strategies, and improve production stability, providing a foundation for future research into robust and data-efficient biomanufacturing process control. This paper investigates the susceptibility of feature maps in convolutional networks to spatial bias, motivated by the observation that architectural choices, particularly the padding mechanism, can systematically elevate or weaken activations at specific spatial locations. The approach involves analyzing how uneven application of padding, influenced by convolution arithmetic, introduces asymmetries in the learned weights. Experimental results show that these spatial biases can negatively affect tasks such as small object detection by suppressing activations when stimuli appear in impacted regions, resulting in blind spots and misdetection. The paper proposes and evaluates solutions to mitigate spatial bias, demonstrating that these interventions can improve model accuracy and suggesting important implications for future research on convolutional network design and robustness. Title: Automatic Extraction of Traffic Primitives for Autonomous Vehicles Using Nonparametric Bayesian Learning

Abstract: The development of automated vehicles necessitates the ability to semantically understand and learn from the driving environment, which often involves analyzing large quantities of naturalistic driving data. A crucial aspect of this process is the identification of traffic primitives, or the fundamental components of traffic, which enable vehicles to learn from human drivers and predict complex traffic scenarios. However, the rapid growth of data poses significant challenges in extracting these primitives from high-dimensional time-series traffic data involving diverse road users. This paper addresses the gap in existing literature, which lacks methods for automatically learning traffic primitives from large-scale data, by introducing a novel framework. The first contribution is a method to generate new traffic scenarios from limited data. The second is the implementation of a nonparametric Bayesian learning method, specifically a sticky hierarchical Dirichlet process hidden Markov model, to extract primitives from multidimensional traffic data without prior knowledge of the primitive settings. Validation using a day of naturalistic driving data demonstrates that this method effectively extracts primitives in traffic scenarios with both binary and continuous events. This work advances the understanding and prediction of complex traffic environments, enhancing the interactions of automated vehicles with other road users.

A deep Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) framework is introduced to address the challenge of learning an unknown and potentially nonlinear number of reward functions from unlabeled expert demonstrations. By leveraging Dirichlet process methodologies, the approach adaptively accommodates both the complexity and the indeterminate quantity of reward functions inherent in expert behavior. The framework models expert demonstrations as a mixture of latent intention distributions, employing the conditional maximum entropy principle to capture multi-intention behaviors. Two novel algorithms are developed to jointly estimate the parameters of a deep reward network and infer the number of expert intentions directly from data, without requiring labeled demonstrations or prior knowledge of the intention set size. The algorithms are empirically evaluated on three benchmark tasks, including two specifically extended to support multi-intention IRL scenarios, and their performance is compared against established baseline methods. Experimental results indicate that the proposed adaptive IRL algorithms outperform existing approaches, particularly by enabling online inference of the number of expert intentions rather than relying on fixed assumptions, thus demonstrating enhanced flexibility and effectiveness in modeling complex decision-making processes.

Nghiên cứu hiện tại tập trung phát triển các phương pháp tích hợp dữ liệu tiên tiến, kết hợp các kỹ thuật machine learning và phân tích dữ liệu lớn nhằm nâng cao hiệu quả khai thác, kết nối và ứng dụng các nguồn dữ liệu mở của EMBL-EBI trong nghiên cứu sinh học hiện đại, từ đó góp phần mở rộng tiềm năng ứng dụng của các cơ sở dữ liệu này trong giải quyết các vấn đề phức tạp của ngành khoa học sự sống.

Reinforcement learning (RL) seeks to derive an optimal policy through interaction with an environment, often necessitating a large number of samples, which can be impractical. Traditional methods frequently rely on random perturbations to obtain policy gradients for local search, resulting in high variance estimates and suboptimal sample complexity. In contrast, Bayesian optimization leverages a probabilistic surrogate model of the objective to actively select informative samples. This paper introduces an innovative algorithm that merges the strengths of both RL and Bayesian optimization. The proposed method employs a probabilistic model of the objective function and its gradient to strategically decide where to query a noisy zeroth-order oracle, thus enhancing gradient estimates. This novel policy search approach demonstrates improved sample complexity and reduced variance when compared to existing black-box algorithms. Extensive empirical evaluations on synthetic objectives validate these improvements. Moreover, the algorithm showcases the advantages of active sampling in widely-used RL benchmarks, underscoring its potential to significantly enhance RL performance by reducing the need for prohibitively large sample sizes.

Domains such as manufacturing and medicine require continuous monitoring and analysis of processes, especially using time series data from sensors, to explain and predict concept drifts during runtime; however, meaningful analysis is hindered by the lack of reliable data sets, which may be due to separate collection of event streams and time series, new processes, or the high costs of obtaining sufficient data volumes, alongside challenges such as integrating data from multiple sources, varying collection frequencies, and concept drift. This paper proposes the GENLOG approach, which generates reliable event and time series data that adhere to the distribution of the underlying input data set by employing data resampling and allowing users to select specific log data segments to orchestrate the training of a recurrent neural network for stream generation. The generated data is then resampled to its original sample rate and embedded back into the originating log data file. As a result, GENLOG boosts small data sets, thereby enhancing the feasibility and effectiveness of online process mining, with significant implications for future research in process monitoring and data-driven decision-making in resource-constrained scenarios. The True Positive Rate (TPR), defined by equation (4.1) as TP/(TP+FN), and the False Positive Rate (FPR) are key metrics for evaluating model accuracy. FPR represents the proportion of actual negative cases that are incorrectly predicted as positive; for instance, an FPR of 0.1 means that 10% of the actual negative cases were misclassified. A lower FPR indicates better model accuracy in identifying negative cases. In contrast, specificity, which is the complement of FPR, expresses the ratio of correctly identified negative cases to the total number of actual negative cases.

The output gate in an LSTM network controls the extent to which the memory cell state is revealed as the output. The LSTM processes sequential data by passing it through multiple LSTM cells, where each cell at a given time step receives the current input and the previous hidden state, producing both an output and a new hidden state. This hidden state acts as the LSTM's memory, retaining pertinent information from earlier time steps.

This paper aims to establish a framework for extreme learning machines (ELMs) on general hypercomplex algebras, addressing the need for machine learning models that utilize higher-dimension numbers as parameters, inputs, and outputs. The methodology begins with a review of broad hypercomplex algebras and presents a robust framework for operating within these algebras using real-valued linear algebra operations. The study explores several well-known four-dimensional examples before proposing hypercomplex-valued ELMs and deriving their learning process through a hypercomplex-valued least-squares problem. Key findings are demonstrated through experimental comparisons of real and hypercomplex-valued ELM models on time-series prediction and color image auto-encoding tasks. The results underscore the excellent performance and versatility of hypercomplex-valued ELMs in handling high-dimensional data, including models built on unconventional hypercomplex algebras, marking a significant contribution to the development of advanced neural network architectures. Estimating articulated 3D hand-object poses from a single RGB image is a complex task, largely due to the inherent ambiguities and the need for large-scale datasets capturing a wide variety of hand and object configurations as well as diverse camera viewpoints. While synthetic datasets can provide such diversity, they often result in inefficient learning and high computational costs. To overcome these limitations, ArtiBoost is introduced as a lightweight online data enrichment method aimed at improving articulated hand-object pose estimation by enhancing data diversity during the training process. Integrated with real-world source datasets, ArtiBoost alternates between data exploration and synthesis, leveraging a Compositional hand-object Configuration and Viewpoint space (CCV-space) to generate novel hand-object poses and camera perspectives. Furthermore, it employs an adaptive mining strategy to enrich the dataset with samples that are currently challenging for the model to discern. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that incorporating ArtiBoost with a basic learning network leads to significant improvements on several established hand-object pose benchmarks. Notably, even a simple baseline model augmented with ArtiBoost surpasses prior state-of-the-art methods, including those based on Transformer architectures, as evidenced by results on the HO3D dataset.

The main idea of this paragraph is that not all business logic in a software system demands real-time execution; certain tasks, such as generating flashcard collections after a lesson is created, can be scheduled as nonreal-time tasks to optimize server performance and response times. 

In the development of a software system for teaching and learning English, it is essential to distinguish between business logic that necessitates real-time execution and tasks that can be deferred. By allocating new tasks to handle nonreal-time requirements, such as generating a flashcard collection following the creation of a lesson, the system can effectively reduce server response times and enhance overall performance. This strategic separation ensures that critical processes receive immediate attention while secondary functionalities are efficiently managed in the background, contributing to a more responsive and scalable application architecture.
